ASPD:
== What is ASPD? ==

ASPD is Attack Speed. It depends on the player's [[Classes|class]], equipped Weapon Type, Speed Modifiers, [[AGI]] and [[DEX]].

== ASPD Formula (0-190) ==

ASPD = 200-(WD-([WD*AGI/25]+[WD*DEX/100])/10)*(1-SM)

[ ] : to round the number to nearest integer

WD : Weapon Delay = 50*BTBA

== BTBA (Base Time Between Attacks (seconds)) ==

[[Image:BTBA.PNG]]

'''BTBA for Dual Wielding (Assassin)'''

BTBA = 0.7*(BTBA1+BTBA2)

== SM (Speed Modifiers (Potions, Skills, Equipment)) ==

Speed Modifiers stacks by adding up all.

== Example ==

Lord Knight wielding a 2-Handed Sword (Base Time Between Attacks 1.1 second / 145 ASPD), and no AGI or DEX, stacking speed mods:
*Berserk Potion (0.2 IAS) + Twohand Quicken (0.3 IAS) + Frenzy (0.3 IAS) = 0.8 IAS
*Combining them together, attack interval becomes a whooping 0.22 seconds between attack (189 ASPD).
*To reach the attack speed cap (0.2 seconds per attack / 190 ASPD), a total of 23 points of AGI+DEX/4 equivalents.

== Hits per Second ==

Hits/Second = 1/TBA = 50/Delay = 50/(200-ASPD)

TBA : Time Between Attacks (seconds)

ASPD represents attack speed as a hyperbolic function (different from exponential function) that approaches infinity attacks/second as ASPD gets close to 200.

For example, a Monk that has his or her Spirit Spheres absorbed in mid-cast of [[Asura Strike]] will still complete their [[Asura Strike]] (unless the cast is interrupted or the targeted player evades it, of course). Accuracy:
Similar to +HIT, "Accuracy" increases a character's chance of hitting a target. Unlike HIT, however, accuracy's increase to hit chance is '''relative to your overall chance of hitting a target'''.

For example, a level 96 [[Crusader]] with 49 DEX has 145 HIT. If they were to hit a [[DRILL]] enemy, with its 166 HIT requirement (to never miss), they would have an 79% chance of hitting the [[DRILL]].

If that same [[Crusader]] were to hit the [[DRILL]] with [[Holy Cross]] rank 10 with its 20% accuracy bonus, the [[Crusader]] would now have a 1.2 * 79 = 94.8% chance to hit.

'''Sources of accuracy'''
* [[Weaponry Research]]
* [[Holy Cross]]
* [[Bash]]

==Overview==

[[Image: Acolyte.jpeg|thumb|left]]

Those who are guided by their faith and wish to devote themselves to the Gods start their holy path as acolytes. 

Acolytes are a 1st job centered primarily around support, they have access to two of the most important buff skills in the game: [[Blessing]] and [[Increase AGI]]. Though they don't have the same kind of offensive skills that jobs like [[Swordman]] and [[Thief]] do, acolytes make up for it by strengthening themselves with their buff skills, and have access to potent anti-[[Undead]]/[[Demon]] passives in the form of [[Divine Protection]] and [[Demon Bane]].

Upon reaching job lvl 40, acolytes can choose to further their devotion to the Gods, either directly as [[Priest]]s or through a different path of rigorous training and enlightenment as [[Monk]]s.

==Jobchange Guide==
''See [[Acolyte Job Change Guide]] for detailed information.''










==Acolyte Builds==
To ensure your acolyte becomes functional later on, you've got to plan your skill build according to the 2nd job you'll graduate as. This section details different [[Priest]] and [[Monk]] builds to give you a good idea of what they do, whether you might like to turn your acolyte into one and how you should allocate your skill and stat points until you job change. You can see the recommended stat allocation, skill overview and example builds on the [[Priest]] and [[Monk]] pages.

===Magnus Exorcismus Priest===
Magnus Exorcismus (ME) priests are a more late-game build that focus on dealing AoE [[Holy]] damage with [[Magnus Exorcismus]], primarily to [[Undead]] and [[Demon]] enemies. ME priests are for those who are generally more solo-oriented and interested in the playstyle of mobbing and killing groups of enemies.

* '''Pros''' : Once they hit their stride a ME priest is both a fast leveler and excellent money maker, extremely durable with nigh-infinite SP
* '''Cons''' : Not very new-player friendly, both in terms of being very gear-dependant and having a high skill floor, it is difficult to level on your own until later on

For more information see: [[Priest#Magnus Exorcismus Priest]]

===Turn Undead Priest===
A priest that specializes in killing [[Undead]] element enemies with the [[Turn Undead]] spell, a skill which has a high chance of killing them in a single hit regardless of how much health they have. Though these characters can be built as hybrids, they are generally for those who want to level their priest solo to 99 as fast as possible, or who like seeing huge numbers show up in front of them.

* '''Pros''' : Can start leveling very fast on their own right out of the gate, the cheapest character to play/level among all priest builds, fairly straightforward playstyle
* '''Cons''' : Very limited in terms of which maps/targets they can viably hunt, owing to their narrow focus as [[Undead]] killers.

For more information see: [[Priest#Turn Undead Priest]]

===Battle Priest===
A melee-oriented priest for those that want a more unorthodox build that smashes things in the head with maces and the powerful [[Holy Strike]] skill. These characters excel on their own or in a duo with other melee (especially [[Blacksmith]]s). 

* '''Pros''' : Amazing sustain in terms of sp and survivability that other melee characters will envy, in later levels they are the best farmers of certain high value targets like Corruptors or any [[Shadow]] element enemy with high HP
* '''Cons''' : Maintaining their many buff spells may feel tedious for some, especially for those who exclusively play auto attackers, though they can visit maps without enemies vulnerable to [[Holy]] they will be considerably weaker than other melee characters in those places

For more information see: [[Priest#Battle Priest]]

===Full Support Priest===
The game's foremost support character, Full Support (FS) priests are characters made to provide very potent group utility/healing and be extremely durable. These characters are for those who intend to level in groups/duos all the way to 99.
 
* '''Pros''' : Essential in any party, you will never struggle to find a group, (eventually) very tough to kill, can function in most capacities on the cheap
* '''Cons''' : More or less powerless solo as this is entirely a group character

For more information see: [[Priest#Full Support Priest]]

===Combo Monk===
A fast-hitting and evasive melee character that can built either for skill-spamming via "full combos" or purely as an autoattacker relying on self buffs, heals and [[Triple ATtack]]. These characters are a popular choice for new players.

* '''Pros''' : Can function really well on the cheap thanks to relatively inexpensive elemental fists, has high sustain thanks to their access to [[Heal]], has an easier time dodging enemies thanks to [[Dodge]] and [[Increase AGI]].
* '''Cons''' : At the higher end of gear/levels, these characters won't be dealing as much damage as a [[Hindsight]] [[Sage]] or Double Dagger [[Assassin]]

For more information see: [[Monk#Combo Monk]]

===TSS Monk===
Monks who play almost like a kind of spellcaster, these characters use [[Finger Offensive]] and [[Investigate]] to deal heavy ranged damage and defense-'''exploiting''' damage respectively. 

* '''Pros''' : Can level surprisingly fast and on the cheap with the only mandatory piece of equipment being a SCOUT-carded headgear, one of few characters that can efficiently kill extremely high DEF targets like Sleepers or Phendarks
* '''Cons''' : Early leveling before becoming a Monk is difficult (no AGI or VIT), SP sustain can be a concern without Magmawhip-carded armor or until getting decent INT

For more information see: [[Monk#TSS Monk]]

===Asura Monk===
'''The One Punch Man'''. [[Asura Strike]] is an enormously powerful skill that pours all of a monk's SP into launching a single, deadly strike. The Asura monk is built for killing MvPs and mini bosses as efficiently and quickly as possible, with the skill potentially reaching upwards of 6 digit numbers in damage.

* '''Pros''' : There is a huge potential for money-making being a killer of MvPs, with careful stat planning you can level pretty decently solo as a quasi TSS monk
* '''Cons''' : Asura monks are arguably the most expensive MvP build at the high end, asura monks struggle on higher DEF MvPs compared to some of their competition (provided they can't be affected by [[Signum Crucis]])

For more information see: [[Monk#Asura Monk]]

===MS Monk===
The Mental Strength (MS) or "[[Steel Body]]" monk is a tank, pure and simple. This monk is for those who want to create an incredibly sturdy character intended exclusively for group situations.

* '''Pros''' : When properly geared, an MS monk takes less damage than any other tank build from either magical or physical damage (providing it does not ignore defenses)
* '''Cons''' : MS monks rely entirely on [[Steel Body]]'s multiplying of their DEF/MDEF values and so are extremely gear dependant, these characters struggle to level on their own and will require parties/leeching most of the way to 99

For more information see: [[Monk#MS Monk]]

====NPC Gear====
The cheapest armor an acolyte can buy is from an NPC (Look for the sword icon in [[Geffen]], [[Prontera]] or [[Payon]]). Buying all of the following equipment nets you 17 DEF (i.e., 17% physical damage reduction) for 93,000z before [[Discount]]. Upgrading it to +4 with elunium increases your DEF up to 32 (32% physical damage reduction), but is considerably more expensive and likely not worth it (100k in NPC costs + 20 Elunium which is generally ~25,000z '''each''').

*Head: Geek Glasses (20,000) - 1 DEF, Biretta [0] (9000z) - 4 DEF
*Weapon: Arc Wand [1] (45,000z) - +3 INT, Staff [2] (9500z) - +2 INT, Stunner [0] (60,000z)
*Shield: Guard [0] (500z) - 2 DEF
*Body: Saint's Robe [0] - (54,000z) - 6 DEF
*Garment: Muffler [0] (5000z) - 2 DEF
*Boots: Shoes [0] (3500z) - 2 DEF

====First Investments====
(combo/TSS monk)

* Elemental Fist weapons made by [[Blacksmith]]s are usually (at time of writing) 400,000z or less, and will serve you well later on as a Monk. [[Wind]] and [[Fire]] fists are the most popular first choices. 

(BP)

* A Chain [3] with 3 Santa Poring Cards represents a reasonably good general-purpose weapon that targets many of enemies that BP kill, both at early and later levels. The Ancient Mummy combo (Mummy card x1 in weapon, Ancient Mummy card in shield) is another, albeit more expensive option that might be worth considering as a cost-effective general purpose weapon + shield combo.

(TU priest)

* A Thara Frog carded Buckler [1] and Poo Poo Hat are good first major investments for a TU priest, as they help considerably with damage taken from their best target (Anubis). The Necrofantasy set also represents a cheaper alternative to Raydric card for damage reduction, as a TU priest's targets are '''always''' [[Undead]] element.

=== TSS/Asura Monk ===
''' Recommended Skill Progression '''
* [[Divine Protection]] 5
* [[Blessing]] 10
* [[Heal]] 3
* [[Increase AGI]] 10
* [[Demon Bane]] 10
* ''After this point skill point allocation depends on the aco's planned skill build, see [[Monk#Builds]].

''' Recommended Stat Progression '''
* Follow the stat progression for BP/Combo Monk above until 45, then (after resetting stats) you should focus primarily on STR with a little bit of DEX (E.g., Aiming for ~80 STR, ~30 DEX by base lvl 55). 

An aspiring TSS/Asura Monk should build their attributes and level on the same monsters as an BP/Combo Monk would until level 45, and then reset their stats as appropriate by talking to Pheonix (See: Stat_Reset). Afterwards, they can continue on the same path as them, but it will be difficult without any defensive stats (i.e., no AGI or VIT). Generally speaking, most TSS/Asura Monks will rely on grouping in places like Louyang Field until job change.

==Gameplay Tips==
===Debuffing Demons and the Undead===
Certain acolyte and [[Priest]] beneficial spells have negative effects when used against [[Demon]] race or [[Undead]] '''element''' enemies. Making use of these spells as debuffs can give the user an extra edge against these foes.

*[[Blessing]]: Reduces [[Demon]] race and [[Undead]] element DEX and INT by 50% for the skill duration (100% success rate).
*[[Heal]]: Deals half its normal healing amount as [[Holy]] damage to [[Undead]] element only. The damage it deals is modified by the target's [[Undead]] element level (e.g., 200% weakness to [[Holy]] for [[Undead]] 4 monsters). Using [[Heal]] to damage [[Undead]] is commonly referred to as "Heal bombing".

=About Al De Baran=
Al De Baran is a peaceful town, home to the Alchemist guild. The adjoining guild map of Luina can be accessed from the western portal in town. To the north lies the cities of Juno, Einbroch, and Lighthalzen. 

===Story===
Al De Baran is the southern city at the end of the Schwarzwalds Republic, which lies on the northern side of the {{map| id=mjolnir_01 Mt. Mjolnir}}. The entrance, a beautiful canal that surrounds a clock tower, adds to the quaint environment of this small town. Al De Baran is famous for attracting [[Alchemist]]s who wish to further research this strange science. It is also known for its beautiful windmills, as well as for being the home of the [[Kafra]] Headquarters.

== Overview ==
[[Image:Alchemist.jpg|thumb|right]]
'''Alchemists''' wield artifice and preparation as their specialty as they adventure through Rune-Midgard. They craft potions and other consumable items, with which they rejuvenate allies and reshape battlefields to lead their foes to destruction. Concoctions are their primary weapons and tools, rather than blades or magic.

The most experienced Alchemists can brew potions whose healing potency far exceeds those sold by standard tool dealers. Their services are highly sought after by elite adventurers embarking on dangerous missions.

== Job Change Guide ==
''See [[Alchemist Job Change Guide]] for detailed information.''

== Builds ==
These are general suggestions to guide toward something workable. The stat numbers in these lists are of base stats. A "+" indicates excess stat points can be spent on that stat.
=== SVD: The Battle Standard ===
*STR: 60-91
*AGI: 1
*VIT: 40-80
*INT: 1-35
*DEX: 60-91
*LUK: 1
SVD can do it all, and does it all really well. You have good plants, strong marine spheres, decent Acid Terror spam, and excellent Demonstration tactics. Depending on the situation, you can switch your playstyle between mobbing with Demo, kiting/AT spam, plants with autocast, blowing things up, or mixing it all together. This is kind of the primary alchemist build after all the alchemist reworks since it is the most flexible and has the largest list of viable maps. SVD favors Demo the most, but does great at everything else as well.

These wide ranges catch multiple buckets, which can skew various ways. An AT and Demo focus will want to prioritize STR, with secondary DEX and VIT. A Sphere Mine focus will want to prioritize DEX and VIT, with secondary STR. To balance all skills equally, take VIT to around 70, INT to at least 24 total, and split the rest between STR and DEX. You want STR for overall damage, VIT for spheres plus durability to hold mobs inside kill zones, and DEX to cast everything quickly. Get enough INT to support your SP, tuned to how much you're okay with pitching yourself blues. What you prioritize is up to you. Pretty much all battle Alchemist builds branch from this base.
=== VD Bomber ===
*STR: 1+
*AGI: 1
*VIT: 90+
*INT: 1+
*DEX: 90+
*LUK: 1
This specialization of SVD takes Sphere Mines to the extreme, for the lovers of bombs and explosions. You need 80 total VIT to return Mines to their original damage. You get a ton of durability along the way, supported by Geo Heals and Potion Pitcher. DEX is vital for mine-laying, due to the full round of 3 mines taking 6.5 seconds to cast. Most of those who take this build prefer to max out DEX. A little VIT can be let go for some INT and/or STR. Mines deal fire damage, and laying them optimally takes a bit of finesse (see [[#Detonating_Sphere_Mines]]).

**24 = 2 Shot Deviruchi/Nightmare
**56 = 1 Shot Marionette
**61 = 2 Shot Isis

**86 = 2 Shot Dullahan
=== SAD ===
*STR: 80+
*AGI: 80+
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 1+
*DEX: 50+

An Alchemist who does not care about Sphere Mines can forgo VIT in favor of AGI as a defensive stat. Flee makes kiting easier and lowers the chance AT and Demo get interrupted, reducing the demand for DEX. Those points can be invested into further STR and AGI. This is arguably the best plant build. See the [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1X_zN-BsD080XAaGeL9LDJeBTWHT0eQq8-LCWUE0eRr4/edit?usp=drivesdk plant damage spreadsheet] [[#Plant_Damage_Calculator|further on]] for more information.

Before Acid Terror got a 0.22sec cooldown, there was a sort of hidden meta where its cast time could clip, so it could spam even faster than PS's 5/sec limit. You can reach that 0.22sec time between casts with high ASPD and Bragi.

== Gameplay Tips ==
Alchemist gameplay is substantially different from their base Merchant. Since all Alchemist skills can be used from range, regular melee attacks are not recommended. For that matter Mammonite is very niche as well. For any case it's more effective than Acid Terror, you might as well play a Blacksmith. Instead Alchemists favor kiting and grenadier battle plans. It's not a requirement that monsters be allowed into melee range, but that can be advantageous to hold them inside Demonstration flames or set off Sphere Mines. Alchemists can become quite tanky, and heal themselves rapidly with Potion Pitcher and their Geographer's Heal. They offer the same healing to their allies. Use the cart to store backup potions.

Kind in mind when mobbing around that Acid Terror and Demonstration can be interrupted by monster attacks. Their short cast times can slip between 1 or 2 monsters' attacks, but there's no hope of them finishing when already swarmed. Sphere Mines and Bio Cannibalize on the other hand don't get interrupted.

=== Bio-Cannibalize ===
Initially, plants are a huge step up from autoattacking by yourself. They deal consistent damage while allowing you to avoid melee combat. The 2 Parasites have the highest DPS as well as the longest attack range, while 4 Hydras hit more rapidly and can cover more ground, for 1 less range each. However, as you gain DEX and better gear, Alchemist's other skills deal damage more quickly. Eventually the Geographer will be the best plant in most cases, for its Heal (6 second cooldown). Plant it off to the side so it doesn't get distracted from using Heal, unless you equip a Tengu card. Make sure to pick up [[Herbicide]].

=== Detonating Sphere Mines ===
The new platinum skill [[Remote Detonator]] makes mines far more convenient and practical. Their simultaneous explosions open up a new use for Mines. Up to 3 can be concentrated in a small area where their Areas of Effect overlap, so they each hit every monster. That is where you get multiple-sphere one-shot breakpoints. However, the way the game processes knockbacks can prevent concentrated spheres from all hitting. They essentially kick targets outside of each other's AoE. The next two images are of 3 mines all stacked on a single cell:
[[File:Detonation Stacks 1st.png|center|frame|At ground zero this shroom gets knocked westward twice.]]
[[File:Detonation Stacks 6th.png|center|frame|From several spaces away it gets knocked westward once. A video of this: [[File:Detonation_Stacks_Final.mp4]]]]

For all of these 3 stacked mines to hit, the mob must be against a wall. For open spaces the mines must be spread like so:
[[File:Detonation Triangulation.png|center|frame|Various triangles work, they just have to knock into each other's AoE.]]
and detonated at the moment the target(s) is in between them. The easiest way to ensure the right positioning is to stand there yourself. If you have enough movement and cast speed, you can set them up ''after'' gathering a mob, rather than beforehand, allowing you to blow up as many as possible all at once.

=== Demonstration (Bomb) ===
Following up from mines, when they are within 2 cells of their caster, Demo automatically launches them as if hit by a melee attack. They can be cast nearly continuously this way, resulting in many explosions over time. Also, they lose no HP since they are Water 3.

As monsters step out of a Demonstration flame, they can be knocked back in, by [[Cart Revolution]] or a well-placed sphere mine.

Demonstration can't be placed within another's 3x3 AoE, but it can be placed in the next cell adjacent. All monsters standing on overlapping cells are hit by each flame. Precise placement and respect for the cooldown can fit up to 4 flames overlapping in 1 cell, outputting massive damage.

=== Potion Creation ===

Manuals and the skill [[Prepare Potion]] are needed to begin making potions.

==== Potion Math ====

Success Rate = LearningPotion * 0.5% + Pharmacy * 3% + JobLevel * 0.2% + (Int/2+Luk+Dex)*0.1%

Some items have addition bonuses or penalties to their success rate:

* +20% and variable bonus between +0.1% and +10% : Red Potion, Yellow Potion, White Potion
* +10% and variable bonus between +0.1% and +10% : Alcohol
* variable bonus between +0.1% and +10% : Acid Bottle, Plant Bottle, Sphere bottle, Bottle Grenade
* variable penalty between -0.1% and -5% : Slim Yellow Potion
* variable penalty between -0.1% and -10% : Slim White Potion, Glistening Coat

==== Potion Materials Hunting Guide ====

* Red Herb : Best from Familiars (Payon Caves) or Red Plants.
* Yellow Herb : Best from Bonguns (Payon Caves) or Yellow plants.
* White Herb : Best from Ghouls (Glast Heim Abbey & Churchyard), White Plants, Blazers and Lava Golems in Magma Dungeon.
* Blue Herb : Found throughout Rune-Midgard, mainly through Blue Plants, Goats or Nightmares.
* Alcohol : Found primarily off Mushrooms.
* Stem : Mandragoras and Floras (near [[Prontera]]).
* Poison Spore : Poison spores (near [[Alberta]]).
* Cactus Needle : Mukas (near [[Morroc]]).
* Mole Whiskers : Martins (two upper levels of Coal Mines).
* Witch Starsand : Bathories (Clock Tower Basement level 4).
* Fabric : Whispers (Glast Heim or Sunken Ship level 1)
* Maneater Blossom : Geographers (Poring Dig Site) or Floras (near [[Prontera]]).
* Tendon : Marine Spheres (lower levels of Izlude Dungeon).
* Detonator : Marine Spheres (lower levels of Izlude Dungeon).
* Immortal Heart : Verits (Pyramids).
* Zenorc Fang : Zenorcs (Orc Dungeon level 2).
* Heart of Mermaid : Obeaunes (Izlude Dungeon level 3).
* Empty Bottles : Generally found from low level monsters, i.e. Porings, Ant Eggs, Peco Peco Eggs.
* Honey : Generally found from Bigfoots, Vitata and Turtles.
* Aloe : Red Plants.
* Ment : Green Plants.

==== Fame System ====

For Brewers there is a ranking system where players are scored according to who has made the most potions:

* Rank Point +1: 3 Condensed White Potions/Blue Potion created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +2: 5 Condensed Yellow Potions/7 Condensed Red Potion created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +5: 5 Condensed White Potions/Blue Potion created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +7: 10 Condensed Red Potion created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +8: 7 Condensed Yellow Potion created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +15: 7 Condensed White Potion/Blue Potion created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +20: 10 Condensed Yellow Potions created without failure in a row.
* Rank Point +50: 10 Condensed White Potions/Blue Potion created without failure in a row.

Alchemist ranks can be checked via usage of the "/alchemist" command ingame. Potions made by an Alchemist who is in the top 10 list will receive a bonus to their potency. 50% healing bonus for first place alchemist, 49% for second place, going down to 41% healing bonus for 10th place. This does not apply to potions used via [[Potion Pitcher]].

==  Description ==
Consumes 1 Trap item to set a trap that will immobililze an enemy for a set duration. The effective duration of the trap is reduced by the enemy's [[AGI]], and [[Boss]] monsters are immobilized by traps for only 1/5 of the normal duration. Although trapped enemies cannot move, they can still attack and use skills. Enemies can also be released if a [[Hunter]] targets them and casts [[Remove Trap]].

|-

|-
| align=center | ''' Immobilization Duration (seconds) 	''' || align=center | 4 || align=center | 8 || align=center | 12 || align=center | 16 || align=center | 20
|}

==  Information ==
*  Trap Duration (but not Immobilization Duration) lasts 4 times as long in WoE.
* Guild castles contain some map squares on which an Ankle Snare is not visible. Even though it can't be seen, the snare is still there and functional.
* In PvP and WoE, snares will trap all players, even the player who set the snare.
* In WoE, players may move past a snare before coming to a stop. They may also occupy multiple snares. When this happens, the Immobilization Duration of the first snare they encountered determines how long they remain trapped. All of the snares they occupy will vanish at the same time. Casting Remove Trap on any of the snares will remove all of the snares, but return only 1 Trap. See the discussion for more in-depth information.
* The action against some "boss" flagged monsters is similar to that of players in WoE. They may move past a snare before stopping, and may occupy multiple snares. Be careful when trapping these monsters.
* Ankle Snare can be cast into "nothingness". When casting Ankle Snare onto a forbidden (black) area of the map, the skill will fail with a warning message, and no SP or Trap will be used. However, if the skill is cast onto a map square which is occupied by an object (not a monster/player), the SP and Trap will be consumed, but an Ankle Snare will not be laid and a warning message will not be issued. These map squares can be identified when the green targeting square vanishes. Clock Tower 3, is an example of a map full of (non-obvious) locations that will cause this. Many guild castles also contain map squares with this behavior, only the targeting square might not disappear.

Their range gives them several advantages, which includes: *The ability to change the element of their weapon quickly by changing their arrow type. This makes Archers able to exploit elemental advantages easily. *Accuracy and damage is increased by the same stat (DEX), allowing all attacks to connect and deal a lot of damage. *Range enables archers to defeat stationary or slow-moving opponents that are stronger than they are without being hit. Drawbacks of the Archer class include: *Low VIT limits their ability to survive when they are caught up in melee situations. *Require Arrows for every attack with a Bow. ==Overview==

[[Image: Assassin.jpg|thumb|left]]

Silent and deadly, assassins make use of their blinding speed and lethal poisons to debilitate and kill their prey. The assassin represents some of the highest damage in the game thanks to their unique ability to dual wield weapons, and the special Katar weapon class which doubles critical hit chance. Assassins can make use of extremely high damage skills like [[Sonic Blow]] or [[Venom Splasher]] to dispatch enemies in a single hit, or use poison to wear their foes down with [[Venom Dust]] and [[Enchant Poison]]. 

Though assassins excel on their own, they can also function as a valuable asset in groups as a mobber thanks to their high flee, fast movement speed and higher than normal health pool. 

==Job Change Guide==

''See [[Assassin Job Change Guide]] for information.''


















==Builds==

=== Double Dagger(DD) ===
*STR: 99+
*AGI: 70-80
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 1+
*DEX: 50+
*LUK: 1

The pinnacle of single target DPS. No other class or build can match a Double Dagger (DD sin)'s raw power when autoattacking targets. DD sins capitalize on the assassin's dual wielding in order to deliver extremely high damage [[Double Attack]] hits. By no means limited to autoattacking, a DD sin also makes for an exceptional group killer by using the [[Venom Splasher]] skill. 

DD sins usually prioritise their STR over AGI in their build (as STR benefits both [[Venom Splasher]] and autoattacking), and may take some amount of INT depending on how they plan to sustain their [[Venom Splasher]]-use (See [[Assassin#Double_Dagger(DD)_2]]).

A less-common option for DD sins is to focus on [[Double Attack]]ing with Sidewinder carded katars and katar skills as "DA hybrid" assassins. Typically, these assassins do not differ from DD sins in terms of attributes, only insofar as their skill build. An assassin might opt for this path because the weapons are much more affordable, or because they prefer [[Grimtooth]] mobbing over [[Venom Splasher]]. 

Example skill build (DD): [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?job=Assassin&s=MT05JjQ4PTEwJjQ5PTEwJjUwPTEwJjUxPTgmNTI9MTAmNTM9MSYxMzI9NSYxMzM9NSYxMzg9NSYxMzk9MTAmMTQwPTUmMTQxPTEwJjEzNT05Jg== Here]. 

Example skill build (DA Hybrid): [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?job=Assassin&s=MT05JjQ4PTEwJjQ5PTEwJjUwPTEwJjUxPTgmNTI9MTAmNTM9MSYxMzQ9MTAmMTM3PTUmMTM1PTMmMTM2PTUmMTM5PTEwJjEzOD01JjEzMj01JjEzMz01JjE0MD0xJg== Here]. 

=== Critical ===
*STR: 70+
*AGI: 80+
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 1
*DEX: 1-20
*LUK: 30-80

True to their name, critical assassins or "crit sins" strive towards maximizing their critical hit chance and damage when autoattacking and mobbing with [[Grimtooth]]. Critical hits ignore enemy DEF, flee and always deal maximum damage. These assassins typically hunt high value targets that other characters struggle to kill because of their high defence or evasiveness. 

A crit sin build requires careful planning, as the amount of LUK taken varies greatly depending on whether the assassin relies primarily on their weapon/equipment for +crit% boosts (i.e., a "equip crit sin"), or their attributes for +crit% boosts ("natural crit sin"). Regardless of type, most crit sins strive towards reaching a 100% chance to critically hit.

Crit sins can hunt on their own, duo with a [[Priest]] to great effectiveness thanks to [[Gloria]], mob in parties (thanks to their high flee and perfect dodge) or even fill the role of an ABB [[Hunter]] in dispatching large groups of enemies. 

Example skill build: [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?job=Assassin&s=MT05JjQ4PTEwJjQ5PTEwJjUwPTEwJjUxPTgmNTI9MTAmNTM9MSYxMzQ9MTAmMTM3PTUmMTM1PTgmMTM2PTEwJjEzOD01JjEzOT0xMCYxNDA9MSY= Here]. 
2 skill points could also be taken out of [[Sonic Blow]] to get [[Cloaking]] 10, making [[Grimtooth]] usage easier (See [[Assassin#Mobbing_With_Grimtooth]]).

=== Sonic Blow (PvE) ===
*STR: 90+
*AGI: 1-50
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 42-90
*DEX: 1-20
*LUK: 50-80

An uncommon assassin build, Sonic Blow (PvE) assassins make use of [[Sonic Blow]]'s high damage modifier and ability to critical hit to kill high DEF/Flee foes in a single strike. Similar to Crit sins, these assassins aim to reach 100% crit rate with katars by combining a specific amount of LUK with +crit% equipment. Unlike their more common counterparts, however, SB sins focus on maximizing their SP recovery rather than their ASPD, though they may get some amount of AGI to get decent flee and to lower [[Sonic Blow]]'s ACD somewhat.

[[Sonic Blow]] has a high SP cost (34) and assassins have low maxSP. SB sins reconcile these two things by using the lowest rank of [[Sonic Blow]] necessary to one hit a target (reducing its SP cost) and by donning SP cost reduction gear (See [[Assassin#Sonic_Blow_(PvE)_2)]]). This build is not recommended unless an individual already has all the necessary equipment and has carefully planned their leveling path and stat distribution. 

Example skill build: [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?job=Assassin&s=MT05JjQ4PTEwJjQ5PTEwJjUwPTEwJjUxPTgmNTI9MTAmNTM9MSYxMzQ9MTAmMTM3PTUmMTM1PTgmMTM2PTEwJjEzOD01JjEzOT0xMCYxNDA9MSY= Here]

=== Double Dagger(DD) ===

DD Assassins pursue the same type of equipment that most flee-based melee do, but STR and ATK are generally considered to be a priority because of how [[Venom Splasher]] works. DD sins typically use gladius [3] and main gauche [4] as their weapons of choice, with how these weapons are carded being a matter of some complexity (See: [[Assassin#DD Sin Carding]]). It should be noted that while dual wielding, assassins are the only class who can change their weapons ''without'' losing a weapon endow like [[Endow Blaze]] so long as both weapons aren't removed at the same time.

Assassins struggle with their SP-pools, and it can be difficult to sustain [[Venom Splasher]] use without due consideration. In place of getting a small amount of INT in their build, DD sins can use cards like Magmawhip or Earth Deleter to sustain AoE farming. Another option is to use the Ninja Suit + Shinobi Sash combo to reduce SP costs.

Though DD Sins are largely considered to be very expensive, there ''are'' options for new players who want to make an assassin.

Blacksmith-made elemental damascus are a classic option for new players. A Poring Dagger is a very affordable weapon with a +20% [[Formless]] damage boost and high weapon ATK. A Main Gauche [4] with 4 Goblin cards represents a good first carded weapon to pursue, as it's relatively cheap, easy to farm and is a solid option for many good targets like Spring Rabbits, Minorous and Ninetails.

=== Critical ===

Like many melee characters, Crit sins use equipment that boosts ATK, STR & AGI, and flee. Unlike most characters however, they also seek items that boost their critical hit rate and damage. Typically Jur [3] are slotted with cards that increase damage against race, crit+% cards or crit race cards (See [[Assassin#Cards_(+%_Crit)]]) depending on other equipment and the assassin's planned final LUK stat. These assassins aim to eventually reach 100% crit rate while wielding katars, be it with [[Gloria]], [[Brutality]] active or unbuffed. 

Specialty Jur [4], Ring of the Claw and Green Maiden cards represent the extreme end of luxury for Crit sins. They should be considered "chase items" for crit sins to pursue and aren't something that's necessary to level or farm effectively.

A popular "universal katar" that many recommend to new crit sins (who either aren't new to the server or who are willing to farm for it) is a Jur [3] with 2 Skeleton Soldier and 1 Bonechewer card. This weapon allows for decent autoattack damage with a large boost to %crit that can be used on any target. Elemental katars like Katar of Piercing Wind are very affordable options for new players who are interested in playing crit sins. Goddess of Fortune's Cursed Brooch are a cheaper alternative to Kobold Cards, but the rapid attack rate will trigger their [[Curse]] relatively often, so anyone intending to use these accessories should be sure to keep Holy Water handy.

=== Sonic Blow (PvE) ===

Sonic Blow Assassins typically use equipment that maximizes their ATK, increases their crit%/dmg and increases their SP recovery/max SP. They usually use Jur [3] or Specialty Jur [4], carded according to how much LUK/+Crit equipment they plan on having (similar to crit sins).

The Ninja Suit + Shinobi Sash combo provides one method of reducing SP consumption (-20%) for these assassins. Magmawhip-carded armor can also be used to refund 5 SP on each kill with [[Sonic Blow]]. The Earth Deleter card is not recommended given that [[Sonic Blow]]'s SP cost will never fall to 10 or below, regardless of equipment or rank used.

== Gameplay Tips ==

=== Mobbing With Venom Splasher ===
The way [[Venom Splasher]] works is it marks a single target as a "bomb", which then explodes after 2 seconds dealing the skill's full damage to all enemies in range. Each target hit has its damage taken calculated separately, independant of whichever target is chosen as the bomb. This mechanic, paired with the skill's 3 cell range means that it is almost always possible to safely use [[Venom Splasher]] without getting hit by melee attacks. 

A reliable way of using [[Venom Splasher]] is a with a 5 step method:

# Gather a group of monsters.
# Walk in a circle around the group of monsters, or drag the group in diagonal directions to get them to stack more tightly together.
# Use [[Venom Splasher]] on a stray target near you and the group.
# Walk past the bomb target, letting them swing at you once so that they stand still and join the group of monsters.
# Boom.

<div style="text-align:center;">[[File:ASO's_VS_Diagram.png|500px|]]</div>
<div style="text-align: center">''A diagram illustrating how to properly and safely use [[Venom Splasher]], courtesy of ASO from the PSRO discord.''</div>


=== Mobbing With Grimtooth ===
[[Grimtooth]] can only be used while in the [[Hiding]] status, and is a small radius (3x3) AoE. These two factors can make it difficult to use the skill, but when used correctly [[Grimtooth]] has the potential to be a high DPS, DEF-bypassing AoE.

A reliable way of using [[Grimtooth]] is a with a 4 step method:

# Gather a group of monsters.
# Walk in a circle around the group of monsters, or drag the group in diagonal directions to get them to stack more tightly together.
# Stop, and use [[Cloaking]] right before the closest enemy in the group of monsters reaches you.
# Use [[Hide]] then spam [[Grimtooth]] on the stack of enemies. 

Don't forget that the [[Venom Knife]] skill allows assassins to equip arrows, and that equipping a Cursed Arrow can help with [[Grimtooth]] mobbing. 

<div style="text-align:center;">[[File:GrimDemo.gif|400px|]]</div>
<div style="text-align: center">''A Crit sin gathers a group of enemies and kills them with proper use of the [[Grimtooth]] skill''</div>

=== DD Sin Carding ===
Since all monsters have a size, element, and race, a weapon combining aspects targeted for each property of the monster will be the most effective. For example, a 2x Flora 2x Drainliar Main Gauche [4]. Flora card does 20% more damage to [[Fish]], and Drainliar card does 20% more to [[Water]] element. The weapon will do 140% x 140%, or 196%, damage to a monster with both water and [[Fish]] properties because different types of +% damage boosts (ele, race, size, crit dmg, etc) stack multiplicatively. A quad fisher or quad saharic would only do 180% damage, but be less limited in terms of potential targets. Adding a third card for size would potentially further strengthen the weapon, at even greater cost of universal use. 

DD sins typically card their daggers in any of the following ways, depending on funds:

*Option 1: 3x size gladius [3] mainhand, 2x2x ele/race main gauche [4] offhand 
The most expensive option, but also the most effective. Carding their daggers in this way requires many more main gauche [4]s as each one is carded for very specific (race/element combination) monsters. 

*Option 2: 3x size gladius [3] mainhand, 4x ele or race main gauche [4] offhand
The most common option, and a nice middle ground for effectiveness. The difference in damage compared to option 1 is ~18%, and often irrelvant in terms of average kill time for a monster depending on its maxHP and other factors.

*Option 3: 4x ele main gauche [4] mainhand, 4x race main gauche [4] offhand
Less common but still an effective option. More daggers are needed than option 2, but this setup will result in more damage at higher STR and ATK values (~110+ STR or so). 

*Option 4: 3x ele or race gladius [3] mainhand, 4x size main gauche [4] offhand
The least common method, this setup can be used for convenient offhand swapping with hotkeys on maps where enemies differ primarily by size. This also allows DD sins to share equipment more readily with [[Rogue]]s.

1.  Journey to the Assassin's Guild, found in moc_fild16 moc_fild16 (205, 296), two maps South and two maps East of Morroc. The entrance to the guild is located near the center on the upper portion of the island.

2. Talk to the Guildsman NPC (in_moc_16 19, 33), who allows would-be Assassins into a room with another NPC as long as they are [[Thief|Thieves]] at Job level 40 or above.

3. Walk near the Guildsman at (in_moc_16 25, 90). After signing up, access to the next room will be granted.

4. Once inside the room, walk forward, and hidden NPC will reveal himself. He will ask the player 10 questions about [[Thief]] and Assassin knowledge ranging from skills to cards to equipment. Nine out of ten questions must be answered correctly in order to proceed.
*'''Note:''' If you are Job Level 50, you only have to do one set of questions.
'''Set 1'''
#''Choose the correct amount of the maximum dodge rate increase from the 'Increase Dodge' skill when at level 10.'' '''30'''
#''Choose a monster which  detects hiding/cloaking Thieves and Assassins.'' '''Andre'''
#''Choose a group of weapons that cannot be used by an Assassin at once.'' '''Katar + Main Gauche'''
#''Choose the town where Thieves can change their jobs.'' '''Morocc'''
#''Choose a card that does not affect the AGI stat.'' '''Whisper Card'''
#''Choose the correct specialty of the Assassin class.'' '''''any answer is correct'''''
#''Choose the maximum AGI bonus an Assassin can get at job level 50.'' '''10'''
#''Choose the item that an Assassin cannot equip.'' '''Helm'''
#''Choose the job change item for Thief.'' '''Orange Gooey Mushroom''' or '''Orange Net Mushroom'''
#''Choose a card that would typically benefit an Assassin the least.'' '''Elder Willow card'''
'''Set 2'''
#''Choose the skill that is not required to learn Grimtooth.'' '''Level 2 Right hand Mastery'''
#''What property does Enchant Poison possess?'' '''Poison'''
#''On Payon stories, how does Level 4 'Right hand Mastery' work?'' '''Increase damage to 110% of base amount'''
#''What is the item required for using Venom Dust?'' '''2 Venom Canines'''
#''Which skill can you learn when you reach Level 5 Enchant Poison?'' '''Venom Dust'''
#''Among the following skills, which allows you to become invisible while moving?'' '''Cloaking'''

#''How much SP does Double Attack use?'' '''It's a passive skill, so SP use is 0.'''

'''Set 3'''

#''Choose a monster that Fire property daggers work the best on.'' '''Hammer Goblin'''
#''Choose the non-elemental Katar.'' '''Infiltrator'''

#''Choose the monster that is not Undead.'' '''Spore'''
5. After the quiz, enter the pub for the next test. Wait your turn if someone else is already in the test area. You'll then be sent to a room filled with Porings, Drops, Lunatics and Poporings. You must kill 6 monsters of the exact name given by the announcer in three minutes.

The name will usually be "Target Monster" or "Job Change Test Monster" but may vary in different versions of RO. The target monsters also always consist of 3 Porings, 1 Drops, 1 Lunatic and 1 Poporing. '''Killing monsters other than the targets or falling into traps results in failing and being teleported back to the entrance NPC.''' Killing all target monsters will automatically kill every other monster in the room and open a portal for the next test.

You should turn off the "snap to monster" and "snap to item" options during this test, since having them on will interfere with hovering your mouse pointer over exactly the monster you want.

6. In the next area, you must run to the other side of a room filled with Mummies and Hydras. Stopping to attack monsters is not necessary. Getting to the sides of the room and going as quickly as possible is highly recommended to avoid getting mobbed.  This part of the test can be made easier through good use of [[Hide]], and is trivial if the player has a Frilldora-carded garment.

Once you reach the NPC at the end of the room, all monsters will die and the you may proceed to the next room. Dying results in failing the test and you will be teleported to  the entrance of the guild and must retake the test. If you die, it is not required to use healing items as the entrance NPC will heal the you back to full health.

7. You will then be sent to a series of rooms that look exactly the same. There is no significance to those other than walking through the portals until reaching a large room with invisible walls. You must traverse through the invisible maze and go beside the Assassin Master at the bottom left corner of the room.

[[Image:Assassin_Maze.png]]

There may be blocked paths but eventually you can reach the NPC through trial and error.

If you hover your mouse pointer over a piece of floor, there will be nothing if there's an invisible wall there, but there'll be a green-square-corners "cross-hair" if it's a walkable floor.  You can use this to work your way backwards from where you want to go.

8. Talk to the NPC and he will talk and ask a few questions about the pride and honor in being an Assassin. Successful [[Thief|Thieves]] are then be rewarded with a Dagger or Katar-class Weapon (depending on Job Level) or a weapon of choice (Job 50), as well as a Necklace of Oblivion (Warning: Do not sell this last item).

9. You will be sent back to the entrance of the Assassin's Guild. Present the Necklace of Oblivion to the Entrance NPC to be changed into an Assassin.

==  Description ==
Consumes a percentage of the monk's remaining [[SP]] to deal massive damage to one target. Asura Strike is effected by race/size/element cards, but always remains a [[Neutral]] property attack. The conditions required to use Asura Strike are variable (See notes).

It '''does not''' ignore the target's [[DEF]].

{| class="wikitable"
! Skill Level !! % (Max) SP Damage Formula !! % (Current) SP Consumed
|-
 | 1 || ATK*(8 + 0.2*SP/10) + 1000 || 20
|-
 | 2 || ATK*(8 + 0.4*SP/10) + 1000 || 40
|-
 | 3 || ATK*(8 + 0.6*SP/10) + 1000 || 60
|- 
  |4 || ATK*(8 + 0.8*SP/10) + 1000 || 80
|-
  |5 || ATK*(8 + SP/10) + 1000 || 100
	
|}
== Notes ==
* Damage reduction by [[DEF]] is a custom change does not work the same way [[DEF]] usually does: Asura damage is reduced by 1% per '''HardDEF''' of target.
* Damage is derived from this formula: ATK * (8 + Remaining SP/10) + Skill Level Bonus.
* Casting ''can'' be interrupted.
* [[Dispell|Dispelling]] a Monk while Asura Strike is being casted will not disrupt it's execution; it is necessary to do so before casting starts.
* It is possible to use [[Hiding]] or a skill like it to evade a directly casted Asura Strike. Other evasion skills, such as [[Cicada Skin Shed]], also function. [[Cloaking]], however, does not.
* A line of sight must be available when the skill activates, otherwise Asura will deal no damage but still drain the caster's [[SP]].
* It is possible to observe if Asura Strike successfully does damage to a target by the screen shaking effect. If it does not occur, then the target has evaded the hit and no damage has been done.
* There are three ways Asura Strike can be cast:
** If the caster has 5 [[Spirit Sphere]]s and is in the [[Critical Explosion]] state, then Asura Strike can be cast in the same manner as single-target skills; by selecting Asura by a hotkey and clicking on a target.
** If the caster has 2 [[Spirit Sphere]]s and is in the [[Combo Finish]] delay, then the caster can cast Asura Strike. This will ''bypass'' the cast time. This is done as the last part of a Monk combo.
** If the caster has 4 [[Spirit Sphere]]s, is in the [[Critical Explosion]] status, and has [[Blade Stop]]ped a target with level 5 [[Blade Stop]] learned, then Asura Strike can be cast on the [[Blade Stop]]ped target.

==Overview==
After a life of plucking their bows, many Archers feel the itch to strum strings of a different kind. The Bards of Ragnarok Online are the right choice for the idealists among Archers who wish to change the world with their poetry.

The voice of a Bard is laden with magical harmonies, singing hymns that invoke the ancient Gods of Asgard to instill fear in the hearts of his enemies and inspire his comrades to victory with songs of eternal youth and glorious charges. Where their female counterparts, the Dancers, are more bent on disruption, Bards specialize in support, which make them central in all defensive strategies during the War of Emperium.

Supporting with a Bard or Dancer requires a different approach than other classes. Music-based buffs are mostly percentual values, as opposed to the absolute values of Priest buffs, and require careful strategy and positioning, but playing as an Archer should already provide some experience in this respect. Despite their supportive role, one should not forget that Bards are also capable of dealing good quantities of damage, one of their main advantages over Hunters is their immense SP pool which allows them to continually use Double Strafe instead of normal attacks, ensuring a very nice damage output.

In general, there are 2 types of skills for both Dancers and a Bards; skills which can be sung or danced without a partner of the opposite gender and those where the player needs another Bard or Dancer respectively.

As a Bard, only Instruments, Daggers, and Bows are available for weapons, whereas Dancers can use Whips instead of Instruments.
*When armed with an Instrument:
:*Bow skills (Double Strafe, Arrow Shower, Arrow Repel) cannot be used
:*Performance Skills, as well as Amp and Encore are available
:*Instrument skills (Melody Strike) can be used
Unbarring Octave and Pang Voice are usable regardless of weapons.

==Jobchange Guide==
''See [[Bard Job Change Guide]] for detailed information.''

In order to become a Bard, one must go to Comodo and look for the Roaming Bard. The applicant has to perform various tasks:

*Item Collection
*[[Snowysnow Quest|Making friends with Mr. Snowman]] in Lutie
*Singing Test

Once these have been completed, the applicant will be made a bard by the Wandering Bard.

== Information ==
*{{item|id=4212 Bongun Card}} accessories give a chance to cast level 1 Bash on an enemy when doing a physical attack. This Bash also pushes the enemy away 5 tiles. 
*{{item|id=1135 Cutlus}} enables the use of level 5 Bash. 
*The [[Accuracy]] gained is a percent of your [[Stats#HIT | hit rate]] added to your [[Stats#HIT | hit rate]]. Therefore, if you have a 67% chance of hitting a monster, level 10 Bash will give you a 100% chance of hitting them: ((50% of 67%) + 67%) or (1.5 x 67)%.
*[[Status Effects#Stun | Stun]] chance inceases with base level.

== Strategies ==

PvM 

*Levelling with Bash is a fast way to level up a [[Swordman]], although quite SP-intensive. It adds a lot of damage even to 10-30 [[Stats#STR | STR]] [[Swordman | Swordmen]] and helps compensate for the lack of [[Stats#HIT | hit rate]] due to being low level. One may want to get it early on if they have the resources to keep up with the high SP cost. 
*There are better skills to [[MvP]] with rather than Bash. 


PvP 

*Bash is used in PvP just as it would be in PvM situations. 
*Every aspect of Bash can be employed at once or separately: a [[Knight]] may use it to deal decent damage to a high-[[Stats#FLEE | flee]] character while rendering its opponent useless by taking advantage of the [[Status Effects#Stun | stun]] chance, whereas a [[Grand Cross]] [[Crusader]] may wish to use Bash purely to [[Status Effects#Stun | stun]] victims before using [[Grand Cross]], so the opponent cannot escape. 
*Do not waste time attempting to [[Status Effects#Stun | stun]] high [[Stats#VIT | VIT]] characters with Bash.

'''Plant Bottles:''' The skill does not require Plant Bottles, but if the Alchemist is holding any, they may summon +1 above the max at the cost of one bottle. Furthermore, Plant Bottles are active items that can only be used by Alchemists on a 60 second cooldown, whether they know Bio Cannibalize or not. Targeting the ground will spawn a Geographer that is separate from the Bio Cannibalize skill.

To support mobility, the platinum skill [[Herbicide]] was added. It kills off the plant so a new one may be summoned elsewhere without spending a Plant Bottle or waiting for it to expire.

Herbicide can also be cast on yourself to kill all plants at once. But you have to hold shift and cast or do type "/ns" or "/noshift".

==Notes==
*Plants do not benefit from [[Axe Mastery]]'s bonus damage.
*Plants will continue attacking targets even if the alchemist uses [[Hiding]] or [[Cloaking]] via items like Smokie Card or Frilldora Card.
*The Tengu Card changes the behaviour of summoned Geographers so that they only use their [[Heal]] skill. This effect applies so long as an accessory with this card was equipped before summoning the Geographer. Removing the accessory ''after'' summoning the Geographer will not revert its behaviour back to normal, for as long as it is summoned.
*Monsters will not attack these plants, and these plants will not attack players in PvM.
*These plants can be attacked by players, so it is generally not a good idea to use them in highly bot-infested maps.
**Good way to detect a low-quality bot.

== Overview ==

[[Image: Blacksmith.jpg|thumb|left]]

Blacksmiths have the ability to forge weapons. They can master the power to imbue weapons with elements of Fire, Earth, Wind and Water and also have the ability to increase the weapon damage further. Of course, Blacksmiths can also be based off raw physical power, and even have the highest melee damage among the other 2nd classes. A Battle Blacksmith's main skills revolve around the theme of self-buffing to increase damage. The main offensive skills are Mammonite and Cart Revolution, which both can be learned as a Merchant. 

==Job Change Guide==

''See [[Blacksmith Job Change Guide]] for information.''

















== Builds ==
=== Battle Smith (VIT) ===
*STR: 90+
*AGI: 1+
*VIT: 70+
*INT: 1+
*DEX: 17-30
*LUK: 1

Able to dole out and take heavy hits, a VIT battle smith is your quintessential brawler-type character. VIT battle smiths make for excellent mobbers, tanks and AoE farmers owing to their enormous carry capacity (via [[Enlarge Weight Limit]] and their cart) for healing items, natural hardiness thanks to [[Skin Tempering]] and their [[Hammer Fall]] and [[Cart Revolution]] skills. 

Being efficient as a VIT battle smith means needing as few [[Cart Revolution]]s or [[Mammonite]]s as possible to kill things. As such, STR is the priority stat with smiths generally aiming to reach 110 - 120 total STR self-buffed. VIT is of secondary importance as it increases the healing potency of items (like Meat, Potions or Ice Cream) which battle smiths rely on for their self-sustain when farming or tanking. Though not the priority, some investment into AGI is beneficial for increasing DPS, whether spamming [[Cart Revolution]] or [[Mammonite]]. Battle smiths do not value DEX very highly and typically get 30 or less. This is because they get a large DEX job bonus (+12), [[Weaponry Research]] gives +20 to HIT/[[Accuracy]], and [[Maximize Power]] alters your attacks as though you had infinite DEX (i.e., you always deal the maximum damage within your damage range). 

With regards to INT, see the [[Blacksmith#Battle Smiths, INT and SP Management]] section below.

=== Battle Smith (AGI) ===
*STR: 80+
*AGI: 90+
*VIT: 1
*INT: 1+
*DEX: 17-30
*LUK: 1

For those wanting a build that is both durable and quick, AGI battle smith represent a relaxing playstyle wrapped around an overall effective character. AGI battle smith are primarily autoattackers, leveraging their buff skills to deal a steady stream of hard hits and be an ''extremely'' valued addition to any DPS duo or split party. Despite relying primarily on FLEE for their defence, AGI battle smith still have their high maxHP modifier and [[Skin Tempering]] passive and are the sturdiest autoattackers around.

True to their name, AGI battle smith value Agility over all else. Firstly because they do not get any +FLEE via skills or passives, and secondly so that they can better leverage tools like [[Corruptor Card]] to help with self-sustain. STR is usually at least 80 (to benefit from the Giant Whisper Card) and AGI battle smiths aim to reach anywhere from 100 to 110 total strength. Like their VIT counterparts, AGI smiths do not value DEX very highly and typically get 30 or less. This is because they get a large DEX job bonus (+12), [[Weaponry Research]] gives +20 to HIT/[[Accuracy]], and [[Maximize Power]] alters your attacks as though you had infinite DEX (i.e., you always deal the maximum damage within your damage range). 

With regards to INT, see the [[Blacksmith#Battle Smiths, INT and SP Management]] section below.

=== Battle Smiths, INT and SP Management ===

In terms of INT and SP management, consider the following. With 1 INT at base lvl 99, a blacksmith has 5 SP regen. A blacksmith's buff skills cost a total of 1.963 sp every 5 seconds:

* [[Maximize Power]] 1 sp / 5 seconds
* [[Weapon Perfection]] 10sp/270 -> 0.185 sp / 5 seconds
* [[Power-Thrust]] 10sp/270 -> 0.185 sp / 5 seconds
* [[Adrenaline Rush]] 32sp/270 -> 0.593 sp / 5 seconds

This leaves 3.037 sp every 5 seconds with which a blacksmith can use [[Greed]] (10 SP), [[Cart Revolution]] (12 SP), [[Hammer Fall]] (10 SP) or [[Mammonite]] (5 or 7 SP). What this means in practice is that a blacksmith's natural SP regeneration is sufficient to sustain full buffs while auto attacking with the occasional [[Greed]] or [[Hammer Fall]] use every ~15 seconds. 

When using the Magmawhip Card (+5 SP on kill), blacksmiths can additionally sustain [[Cart Revolution]] spam providing at least '''5 enemies''' are killed with 2 or fewer [[Cart Revolution]]s, '''8 enemies''' are killed with 3 or fewer [[Cart Revolution]]s, and so on (3 enemies killed per cart revo use required). Killing more enemies at a time than these minimum thresholds allows using other skills, like [[Greed]] or [[Hammer Fall]] more often. Using Magmawhip carded armor also allows sustaining [[Mammonite]] use providing it kills an enemy in one hit. 

When using the Earth Deleter Card (+10 SP on kill, SP regeneration disabled) blacksmiths can sustain [[Cart Revolution]] spam providing at least '''3 enemies''' are killed with 2 or fewer [[Cart Revolution]]s, '''4 enemies''' are killed with 3 or fewer [[Cart Revolution]]s, etc. Killing more enemies at a time than these minimum thresholds allows using other skills, like [[Greed]] or [[Hammer Fall]] more often. Using Earth Deleter carded armor allows sustaining [[Mammonite]] use providing it kills an enemy in at least two hits (or 1 hit with [[Zeny Pincher]] toggled on).

In parties, both [[Hammer Fall]] and [[Greed]] are very useful. With [[Blessing]] and [[Magnificat]] or a [[Dancer]]'s SP buff, both [[Greed]] and [[Hammer Fall]] can be used once per mob (for the [[Mailbreak]] effect and looting respectively) providing mobs are no more frequent than every 10 seconds. 

Overall, battle smiths can get by with 1 INT, but it is worth considering investing points into INT if...

* You're tanking for parties where repeated [[Hammer Fall]] spam for its [[Stun]] or [[Freeze]] (with Sasquatch carded armor) effects are very useful.
* You're in a party with '''very''' frequent loot drops like Prontera Guild Dungeon [[Ninja]] parties and need to sustain constant [[Greed]] use.
* You aren't using Magmawhip or Earth Deleter carded armor, and want to sustain skill-use
* You are using Magmawhip carded armor, and are on a map where you are killing fewer enemies at a time than is necessary to sustain [[Cart Revolution]] spam (see above) or [[Greed]] use.

Remembering that INT grants a bonus to SP regeneration every '''6 points''' and you get an additional point of SP regeneration every '''100 maxSP'''. Example breakpoints which hit both of these bonuses are '''22 base INT''' (unbuffed), '''36 base INT''' (with [[Blessing]]) and '''46 base INT''' (unbuffed).

=== Pure Forger ===
*STR: 9
*AGI: 1
*VIT: 1
*INT: 1
*DEX: 99
*LUK: 99

Pure Forger blacksmith are expert craftsman who eschew battle capability to focus entirely on their trade. Special "VVVS" and elemental weapons that serve as bread and butter cost-effective weapons for players are made by these characters. A pure forger blacksmith is a character that is only made by those with deep pockets, or else a host of guild members or friends who are willing to fund an enormously expensive character as most who create pure forgers do so with the aim of placing on the ''ranked /blacksmith list'' (see [[Forging]]).

The success rate of forging weapons is based on DEX (+0.1%), LUK (+0.1%) and job level (+0.2%). There is little to deliberate over in terms of stat choice, as 99 points into both DEX and LUK is the only thing they can do insofar as attributes go to improve their weapon forging.

=== Battle Smith (VIT) Gear ===
VIT battle smith use very similar equipment to [[Knight]]s, favouring +STR/ATK gear but also focusing on %damage reduction like Raydric Card and %Race reduction shields. Like [[Knight]]s and other VIT mobbers, VIT battle smith make good use out of Spring Rabbit or Snowier carded accessories. One caveat to using Snowier Card is that Ice Cream can [[Freeze]] you, which is fine if you use it when taking hits from monsters (freeing you from the ice) but can be tedious at times.

In terms of tanking, the otherwise unremarkable-looking Martin Card is a very good choice for blacksmith because its [[Neutral]] resistance stacks with both Raydric Card and [[Skin Tempering]], for a total of 43% [[Neutral]] resistance. Because of how damage reduction is worked out in the game, it's almost always better to stack as much of you can of a single source of damage reduction rather than spread it out over multiple sources. Sasquatch Card is also a very cost-effective tanking choice for VIT battle smith, because it changes [[Hammer Fall]] to have a secondary roll to [[Freeze]] enemies if they aren't [[Stun]]ned by the initial effect, helping mitigate a mob's damage to the blacksmith.

VIT battle smiths generally favour one-handed [[Axe]]s like Axe [4], Orcish Axe [3], or Masterwork Axe [2] as being able to use a shield is a huge boon to efficiency when mobbing. It is also worth considering using Two-Handed Axes, either to save money (Two-handed Axe [2] is cheap and effective) or if its extra damage means using one fewer [[Cart Revolution]] to kill something, saving SP. It should be pointed out that using [[Weapon Perfection]], a VIT battle smith could conceivably use many different types of weapons. [[Dagger]]s, [[Mace]]s and Swords are all reasonable options if you have a ready-made arsenal from other characters (including special weapons like Frozen Pick, Dragon Killer, etc). It may also be worth using Light Epsilon if you aren't using an endow and have excess SP, saving on consumables in between pulls.

For newer players, a regular npc-bought Two-Handed Axe [1] is a decent starter weapon for its high base ATK, while a blacksmith-forged elemental VVS Two-Handed Axe ([[Forging]]) serves as a solid option for a first major investment. A very good choice for a more-expensive but very handy investment is a "High Orc Axe", i.e., either "3x Orc Lady 1x Hydra" or "2x Orc Lady 1x Vadon 1x Hydra" Axe [4]. Orc Warrior/Orc Lady (as a merchant or fresh blacksmith) and High Orcs (lvls 70-99) represent one of the best places for VIT battle smith to level. The first type of high orc axe is cheaper and more useful for merchant leveling, whereas the second is slightly better damage, and particularly better in the Clock Tower High Orc map. All of the cards that go into either type of axe can be easily farmed by determined players, be they newbies or veterans.

=== Battle Smith (AGI) Gear ===
AGI battle smith equipment is fairly typical for autoattackers (+STR/ATK, +AGI/FLEE), with an added emphasis on +FLEE/AGI as they need it more than others, given the lack of any skills or passives to boost their evasion. These blacksmith are a great candidate for using [[Corruptor Card]] as they have a very fast attack speed and have no natural means of helping with sustain, aside from carrying a lot of restoratives. 

Carded Two-Handed Axe [2] are a popular choice in terms of weapons for AGI battle smith, though eventually carded Battle Axe [4] will overtake it in terms of damage (~100-110 STR depending on other +ATK cards like Giant Whisper Card). The blacksmith should consider whether they prefer the more economical choice of Two-Handed Axe [2] or are willing to pay more for a slight edge in DPS.

In terms of budget options, a regular npc-bought Two-Handed Axe [1] is a decent option because of its high base ATK, while a blacksmith-forged elemental VVS Two-Handed Axe ([[Forging]]) should be what a new/budgeting battle smith aims for as their first major investment. A slightly more expensive, but forever useful alternative is a 2x Goblin carded Two-Handed Axe [2], as many great targets for AGI battle smith are [[Brute]]s. Sandals, Sakkat and Brooch remain cheap early investment options for any autoattacker.

== Description ==
Once Blade Stop is cast, it allows the caster to "catch" an enemy if they use a normal attack against the caster during the skill's Catch Time. If Blade Stop is successfully casted, then both the [[Monk]] and enemy are thrown into the "Blade Stop" status. During the Blade Stop status, only the caster may attack, by use of skills, and what skills they can use are determined by the level of Blade Stop they have learned (exception if the opponent is also a monk, see notes). 

Blade Stop only works on physical attacks and requires 1 [[Spirit Sphere]] per cast, regardless if an enemy is caught or not. Blade Stop refunds its [[Spirit Sphere]] cost when [[Investigate]] or [[Finger Offensive]] are used.

{| class="wikitable"
!Skill Level || Skills || Catch Time || Duration  
|-
|1 || None || .5 seconds || 20 seconds  
|-
|2 || [[Finger Offensive]] || .7 seconds || 30 seconds 
|- 
|3 || [[Investigate]] || .9 seconds || 40 seconds  
|-
|4 || [[Chain Combo]] || 1.1 seconds || 50 seconds 
|- 
|5 || [[Asura Strike]] || 1.3 seconds || 60 seconds  
|}

The Catch Time associated with Blade Stop is the amount of time you have to actually "catch" an enemy attack to launch the Blade Stop status.

== Continuing as a Combo ==
[[Asura Strike]] only requires 4 [[Spirit Sphere]]s to be cast in the Blade Stop status (since Blade Stop takes one [[Spirit Sphere]] to cast) but still requires the [[Fury]] state. 

It is possible to continue the [[Chain Combo]] to [[Combo Finish]] if you select the enemy just after quadruple.
* Blade Stop -> [[Chain Combo]] -> [[Combo Finish]]

== Notes ==
* Blade Stop cannot catch players or monsters using skills.
* Since this skill is of the [[Monk]] discipline, if the user Blade Stops an enemy [[Monk]], then the enemy can also use skills while in Blade Stop; which skills are available is determined by each player's level of Blade Stop.
* During the Blade Stop status, players/monsters will retain all of their original characteristics, ''except'' the inability to move or attack. They can be damaged, attacked, use items or even change gears.
* Blade Stopped players/monsters are also susceptible to effects like knockback (and it will not affect the Blade Stop status).
* [[Throw Spirit Sphere]] is weakened when used from Blade Stop, as Blade Stop itself consumes one spirit sphere.
* Blade Stop only works from melee range. It can be used against ranged attackers, but the monk using Blade Stop must be within melee range.

== Description ==
Blitz Beat uses the [[Falconry Mastery|Falcon]] to attack an enemy and all surrounding foes within a 3*3 cell area. When casted manually, enemies within a 3*3 cell area around the target will receive the same amount of damage as the targeted enemy. This skill will also go off passively.

== Information ==
*Requires a Falcon. 
*Blitz Beat is always [[neutral]] [[element]] but will bypass Raydric cards in [[PvP]] if elemental arrows are equipped. 
*Damage is based on [[INT]], [[LUK]], and [[Steel Crow]]. 
*[[Steel Crow]] adds 6 points per level, up to 60. 
*Damage formula is: ([LUK] + [INT/2] + 6 * Steel Crow Lvl + 20) * 2) '''*Note:''' This damage formula is current as of 8/11/25. More information can be found [[Class Rebalance#Hunter|[here]]]. 
*Cards increasing [[ATK]] will not affect the damage of Blitz Beat and it will not inflict status ailments. 
*Blitz Beat will bypass [[Guard]]. 
*Blitz Beat will bypass [[Defending Aura]] in [[PvP]] and [[WoE]].

== Auto-Blitz Beat ==
*Only set off from normal attacks with a bow. Attacking with skills, daggers, or fists will not trigger it. 
*May be triggered even if the attack misses or is blocked by a skill. Basically, a chance for every arrow. 
*For every 3 points of [[LUK]] there is an additional 1% chance Auto-Blitz Beat will be triggered. 
*Does not consume SP, has no cast time, and has no cast delay. 
*Auto-Blitz may occur during a cast delay. 
*The number of times Auto-Blitz Beat will hit its enemy depends on the level of Blitz Beat and the job level of the character. Job levels 1-9 allow it to hit up to one time, while job levels 40+ allow the maximum of 5 hits if level 5 Blitz Beat is attained.

Bowling Bash:
{{Skill Info | class = Knight | class2 = Mercenary | type = Offensive | levels = 10 (Selectable) | prereqs = ([[Swordman]]) [[Bash]] Lv. 10, [[Magnum Break]] Lv. 3, [[Two-Handed Sword Mastery]] Lv. 5, ([[Knight]]) [[Twohand Quicken]] Lv. 10, [[Counter Attack]] Lv. 5 | time = 0.7 seconds(Not Interruptible)(reduced by [[Stats#DEX | DEX]]) | delay = [[Stats#ASPD | ASPD]] dependent (Animation delay) | target = Foe | range = Melee | area = 3 x 3 | knock = 1 |spcost=12 + Skill Level}} == Description == Bowling Bash will knock targets backward, causing damage in a 3x3 cell area that hits twice. Bowling Bash cannot be interrupted by attacks. [[DEX]] determines cast time while [[ASPD]] determines the delay. During the cast time of Bowling Bash, the user's DEF is reduced to 2/3 of its original value. {| class=wikitable style="border 1em #aaaaaa solid" |- | align=center | '''Skill
Level''' || align=center | '''ATK''' || align=center | '''SP
Consumption''' |- | align=center | 1 || align=center | 130% || align=center | 13 |- | align=center | 2 || align=center | 160% || align=center | 14 |- | align=center | 3 || align=center | 190% || align=center | 15 |- | align=center | 4 || align=center | 220% || align=center | 16 |- | align=center | 5 || align=center | 250% || align=center | 17 |- | align=center | 6 || align=center | 280% || align=center | 18 |- | align=center | 7 || align=center | 310% || align=center | 19 |- | align=center | 8 || align=center | 340% || align=center | 20 |- | align=center | 9 || align=center | 370% || align=center | 21 |- | align=center | 10 || align=center | 400% || align=center | 22 |} == Information == *The two hits of the skill proc at the same moment but are counted separately, meaning: **Skills that have a set number of hit deflection are affected twice. **Only the first hit's damage can be doubled by [[Lex Aeterna]]. **Status effects from cards and special weapons apply for both hits separately. *Even when used with a bow on a [[Rogue]] class, the skill is still melee. Hence it is not blocked by [[Pneuma]], and also does not consume arrows. **Due to the attack being close range, some effects such as the bonus for equipping a Crystal Arrow with Frozen Bow [1] will not apply. *The knockback effect will move the target into the direction the caster has last moved or faced toward. When turning away from a target and then performing the skill, it results in the opposite effect where the target becomes drawn to the caster. *The knockback effect is applied before damage. Due to this, [[Safety Wall]] does '''NOT''' block the skill. *Since the Cast Delay is based on [[Stats#ASPD | ASPD]], which is the caster's sprite animation itself basically, engaging a foe that has [[Reflect Shield]] turned on, results in the animation to be broken when the caster takes damage. This essentially negates the cast delay, and Bowling Bash can be recasted immediately without much delay, resulting in a very high damage output per second. {{Navbox Knight}}
Brandish Spear:
{{Skill Info | class = Knight | class2 = Mercenary | type = Offensive | levels = 10 | spcost = 12 | prereqs = ([[Knight]]) [[Spear Stab]] Lv. 3, [[Peco Peco Ride]] Lv. 1 | time = 0.7 seconds(Not Interruptible)(reduced by [[Stats#DEX | DEX]]) | delay = [[Stats#ASPD | ASPD]] dependent (Animation delay) | target = Foe | range = Melee | area = Depends on skill level | knock = 3 | cf_name = Weapon | cf_value = Spear }} ==Description== Attacks an area of ememies around the caster. The area of effect increases in range at skill levels 4, 7, and 10. The damage dealt by the skill for each enemy increases the closer they are to the caster. The affected range starts outwards from the knight, from 4 tiles in front toward the target (Minus the edges for the front-most row) to 1 tile behind the knight (+1 in case of diagonals). Targets struck by this skill are knocked back 3 cells. If targets struck collide with an unmoveable cell (e.g., a wall) after being knocked back at least one cell, then they take two hits from the skill. {| class=wikitable style="border 1em #aaaaaa solid; text-align: center;" align="center" |+ '''Area of effect by Skill Level''' |- | ||style="background:lightgreen;"| 10 ||style="background:lightgreen;"| 10 ||style="background:lightgreen;"| 10 || |- |style="background:yellow;"| 7+ ||style="background:yellow;"| 7+ ||style="background:yellow;"| 7+ ||style="background:yellow;"| 7+ ||style="background:yellow;"| 7+ |- |style="background:orange;"| 4+ ||style="background:orange;"| 4+ ||style="background:orange;"| 4+ ||style="background:orange;"| 4+ ||style="background:orange;"| 4+ |- |style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:red;"| 1+ |- |style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:lightblue;"| Player ||style="background:red;"| 1+ ||style="background:red;"| 1+ |} The damage dealt by Brandish Spear is not straightforward. Normal damage at level 10 is 300% (100% + 20% per skillLv), to that is applied a bonus of 50% + 25% + 16.6% if they're close (see below). Being hit into a unmoveable cell rolls another attack with those same properties and that bonus is multiplicative Range 1: 300 * 1.8333
Range 2: 300 * 1.75
Range 3: 300 * 1.5
Range 4+: 300 Put another way, the damage Brandish Spear does depends both on whether something was knocked into an unmoveable cell ''and'' on which cell the monsters are relative to the knight. Proper use of the skill involves gathering mobs of enemies so they are close together, and then using Brandish Spear as soon as they reach the knight in a direction so that they'll be knocked into a wall/pillar/etc. ==Notes== *During the cast time of Brandish Spear, the knight's DEF is reduced to 2/3 of its original value. *Brandish Spear does two hits if the targets "collide" with an unmoveable object, but this isn't entirely accurate. What actually happens is if after the knockback there is an unmoveable object behind them, ''then'' they take two hits. *Requires the player to be wielding a Spear. *Requires the player to be mounted on a [[Peco Peco Ride|Peco Peco]]. *Requires a targeted enemy to determine direction, but the area of effect is based on the position of the player. * Knock-back does not occur during [[WoE | War of Emperium]]. {{Navbox Knight}}

Brutality:
Brutality is a beneficial status effect that can be triggered by the Bonechewer Card. 

This status increases crit +5% and critical damage by 50% for 10 seconds. This effect cannot trigger again for 2.5 seconds after activating, but can overwrite itself. Multiple Bonechewer Cards in a weapon increase the chance of triggering the effect, but only one instance of the Brutality status can be active at a time. The Brutality status is ''not'' removed after unequipping a weapon compounded with a Bonechewer Card, and so it is possible to trigger the effect with a weapon and then switch to another as needed.
Brute:
'''Brute''' are a race of [[Monster]]. Most of them are animals or have animalistic traits. Some examples of Brute monsters are Spring Rabbits, Minorous and Wild Rose.

Cards which concern the brute race include:
* '''Cruiser Card''': Inflict 10% more damage with Critical Attack. Critical +7 on Brute monsters.
* '''Goblin Card''': Increase damage on Brute monsters by 20%.
* '''Leib Olmai Card''': Add the chance of gaining 'Red Blood' item each time a Brute monster is killed. Add 10% more tolerance against [[Fire]] Property Attack.
* '''Mini Demon Card''': Receive 10% more Experience Points from Brute Monsters. Receive 20% more damage from Brute Monsters.
* '''Nereid Card''': Gain 5 SP each time a Brute monster is killed by Physical Melee Attack. Drain 5 SP as the weapon is unequipped. Increase damage against Brute monsters by 4%.
* '''Orc Warrior Card''': Reduce damage from Brute monsters by 30%.
* '''Puck Card''': Receive 15% less damage from [[Holy]] property monsters. Reduce damage from Brute monsters by 25%.
* '''Spring Rabbit Card''': Add the chance of gaining 'Meat' or 'Monster's Feed' item each time a Brute monster is killed. Meat and Monster's Feed restore 50% more HP.
* '''Stem Worm Card''': Add the chance of gaining '12032 Box of Storms' item each time a Brute monster is killed. 

Equipment which concerns the brute race include:
* '''Kitchen Knife''': Dagger. Adds a 50% chance of the 'Meat' item dropping when killing a Brute race monster
* '''Slaughter''': Axe. Pierces Defense of Brute monsters. Causes [[Coma]] effect on Brute monsters by a low chance. [[Earth]] Elemental.

Skills concerning the Brute race include:
* '''[[Beast Bane]]''': [[Hunter]] skill that increases [[ATK]] against the Brute and [[Insect]] races.

== Description ==
The second skill in the Monk's combo skill set, Chain Combo is a more powerful attack that hits four times and can be used in succession for 3 seconds after [[Triple Attack]] triggers. The only other circumstance when a Monk can successfully perform Chain Combo is during a level 4 [[Blade Stop]] status. If the user has learned [[Combo Finish]], then [[Combo Finish]] can be chained after the use of Chain Combo. 

Putting any amount of skill points into this skill will trigger the "Combo Finish Ready" status for 800 seconds or (1000 - 4*agi - 2*dex + 300) + 25 ms (whichever is greatest), enabling the use of [[Combo Finish]]. [[Triple Attack]] cannot trigger while this status is active, but autoattacks still continue (See the Combos section of [[Class Rebalance#Monk]] for more information)

== Description ==
Charge Attack is a quest skill that causes you to rush the targeted monster/player, dealing more damage depending on how far away you are from it. Targets struck by Charge Attack are knocked back by 1 cell.

{| class="wikitable"
!Distance || < 3 Cells || < 6 Cells || < 9 Cells  
|-
|Damage || 100% || 200% || 300% 
|}

== Information ==
*[[Safety Wall]] does not block it since it is a ranged attack 
*Enemy can reduced the damage by simply moving closer to you 
*During [[WoE]], your body will not “charge” or move when you use this skill. It becomes another range physical attack. 
*If charge attack misses (like there is a [[Pneuma]]), your body will still relocate. 
*Charge attack can get you “out” of any trap, like the skill [[Close Confine]] of [[Rogue]]s (provided another enemy is nearby to charge).

{{Skill Info
