| prereqs = ([[Ninja]]) [[Shadow Leap]] Lv. 5
| spcost = 9 + (Skill Level * 3)
| duration = 10 + Skill Level * 10 secs
| delay = None
| target = Self
}}

== Description ==

Enables Cicada Skin Shed status, which causes the caster to automatically dodge a set number of physical attacks. Each dodge is followed by a backward movement of 7 cells in the direction the ninja is attacked. Cicada Skin Shed ends after its duration expires or upon reaching the maximum number of hits. Cicada Skin Shed will only evade skills whose damage is affected by % cards, and will not dodge elemental skills from monsters.

{| class="wikitable"
!Level ||Hits Blocked ||SP Cost ||Duration
|-
|1 ||1 ||12 ||20 Secs.
|-
|2 ||1 ||15 ||30 Secs.
|-

|-
|4 ||2 ||21 ||80 Secs.
|-
|5 ||3 ||24 ||90 Secs.
|}

== Notes ==

* Natural Flee, Perfect Dodge, [[Safety Wall]], and [[Kyrie Eleison]] take priority over Cicada Skin Shed; if one causes the attack to fail, Cicada does not activate..
* Does not overlap with the [[Mirror Image]] skill, using one of these skills will remove the other. 
* In [[PvP and WoE#WoE|War of Emperium]] the dodge effect applies but there is no backslide effect.
* Any effect given by the attack will still apply, despite no damage being taken. For example, you can be frozen (while simultaneously being thrown back) if you are attacked with a weapon that can freeze.
* Effects of cards that trigger when the user is being hit (ie. {{item|id=4315 Pest Card}}) are still applied.
* This skill cannot be dispelled with [[Dispell]].

Classes:
Classes, or Jobs, define your character in Payon Stories. You start out as a [[Novice]] and upon reaching job level 10 you can progress into one of six base classes. After your initial promotion to the first class of your choice you will have the option to reach even greater heights of strength and power by reaching Job level 40 and completing a job change quest that will change you into a 2nd job. Each base job has two options for 2nd jobs they can choose from.

== Effects ==
*Cloaking makes the target invisible to players and monsters while retaining the ability to move unlike Hide. 
*Characters cannot attack and do not regenerate HP or SP with in the Cloak status. They can use skills (which will cancel cloaking) and items. 
*Does not cancel targeted skills (eg. [[Fire Bolt]], [[Guillotine Fist]]) unlike [[Hiding]].

== Custom Changes ==
*The skill doubles the first attack/double attack when coming out of Cloak.
*The skill increases the damage of Sonic Blow when cast from Cloak. 
*Can Cloak from Hide and can Hide from Cloak.

== Revealing Cloaked Players ==
*Revealing or seeing a cloaked player is the same for Hidden ones. 
*Monsters that can detect cloaked players: [[Insect]] race, [[Demon]] race, those with the [[Boss Protocol]]. 
*Skills that will reveal a cloaked player: [[Detect]], [[Improve Concentration]], [[Ruwach]], [[Sight]], [[Heaven's Drive]], [[Earth Spike]], [[Arrow Shower]]. Ruwach and Sight will reveal cloaked players as long as they remain within the range, whereas a player can immediately Cloak again after being revealed by another skill. 
*Items that reveal a cloaked player only to the user: Box of Sunlight, Maya Purple carded headgear. 
*AoE (Area of Effect) skills can hit players out of cloak.

==Costumer NPC (Turn Regular Headgears into Costumes)==
[[File:Costumer at Payon.png|thumb|321x321px|Costumer NPC in Payon]]

In Payon (oldnewpayon 61, 182) you can fina a '''<u>[[Costumer]]</u>''' NPC that turns regular headgear into costume in exchange for zenny charge. Headgears are divided into 4 groups with different zenny costs for creating a costume: 

*S-Tier Items - exchange cost 2,000,000 zenny
*A-Tier Items - exchange cost 1,000,000 zenny
*B-Tier Items - exchange cost 500,000 zenny
*C-Tier Items - exchange cost 200,000 zenny

Costumes created by NPC are tradeable, that means you can buy/sell them from other players by vending.

====Check the '''<u>[[Costumer]]</u>''' page to get full currently available Costume list.====
'''''Note:''' When you turn headgear with Stat/Skill bonuses into Costume you will loose all the headgear bonuses!''

Alternatively, a user can begin casting Counter Attack and then click on a monster within range during the skill. == Overview ==

[[Image: Crusader.jpg|thumb|left]]

Fighting in the name of their God, crusaders are warriors preparing for the holy war. A mix of martial strength and faith-driven magic, crusaders are an exceptionally sturdy hybrid class with a particular emphasis on supportive and defensive skills. They can trivialize damage taken using [[Auto Guard]] and [[Defender]], and help protect allies with [[Sacrifice]] and [[Providence]].

By no means limited to defense, crusaders wield powerful [[Holy]] element skills like [[Grand Cross]] and [[Holy Cross]]. They're also experts at fighting with spears, capable of wielding them with greater force and speed owing to their [[Spear Mastery]] and [[Spear Quicken]] abilities.

Crusaders are the gold standard for mobbing in parties, and an essential component for any group dealing with difficult enemies or MvPs. Aside from their stellar group capabilities, crusaders make for able soloers and farmers, especially when dealing with [[Demon]]s or the [[Undead]].

* STR: 30-60
* AGI: 1
* VIT: 40-70
* INT: 90+
* DEX: 50-80
* LUK: 1

A crusader with spellcasting prowess who uses the powerful [[Grand Cross]] skill. [[Grand Cross]] is an AoE [[Holy]] spell that deals damage based on both the caster's magical mATK and physical ATK, and so these "GC saders" get high amounts of INT and low-moderate amounts of STR to facilitate its use. As the spell is centered around the caster, inevitably a lot of damage is taken by the gc sader. VIT helps the crusader stay alive, whereas DEX reduces the cast time of [[Grand Cross]], reducing its damage range and the amount of time being hit by enemies. 

Though STR is usually taken to increase the physical ATK portion of [[Grand Cross]]'s damage, it is of a considerably lesser priority compared to INT as gc saders struggle with their SP management given [[Grand Cross]] and [[Heal]]'s high SP costs. A GC Sader will take as much STR and DEX as is needed to hit some kind of threshold, like being able to guarantee 2-hit an Abysmal Knight or 1-hit a Khalitzburg with [[Grand Cross]]. For planning a GC Sader always be sure to consult a stat calculator ([[Crusader#See Also]]) for damage dealt to a given target.

GC saders primarily hunt [[Shadow]] and [[Undead]] element enemies, but can reasonably kill monsters of any element that they can group up and tank.

=== HC (Holy Cross) ===

* STR: 90+
* AGI: 40+
* VIT: 1
* INT: 18+
* DEX: 50+
* LUK: 1

[[Holy Cross]] is a powerful physical skill, noted for its SP efficiency (Rank 1 HC is 325% ATK for 3 SP), range and innate [[Holy]] element. Holy Cross Crusaders or "HC saders" are built entirely around this skill, focusing on maximizing their ATK so they can kill targets with as a few [[Holy Cross]]es as possible. Because of its innate [[Holy]] element, these crusaders typically hunt [[Shadow]] and [[Undead]] element enemies exclusively. 

Because many high level [[Shadow]] element enemies also have high flee, these crusaders often get high DEX. INT (in multiples of 6 for regen bonuses) and AGI are secondary priorities to sustain skill use and increase attack speed respectively. These crusaders typically spam rank 1 [[Holy Cross]] for its efficiency, but can use higher ranks for high health or very high flee targets (like Abysmal Knight and Bloody Murderer) as the skill's accuracy bonus is skill rank dependant.

=== AGI Spear ===

* STR: 70+
* AGI: 90+
* VIT: 1
* INT: 1+
* DEX: 50+
* LUK: 1+

For crusaders who have a need for speed! AGI Spear crusaders (or "spear saders") are capable of reaching 185+ ASPD, autoattacking more than 4 times per second. Getting no innate bonus to their flee, these crusaders usually go all in on AGI. Unlike HC saders, they don't focus primarily on shadow/undead element enemies but instead have a much broader range of targets, limited only by the variety of spears in their arsenal. AGI crusaders have a 3 cell range when autoattacking targets rather than the normal 1 cell range, owing to the greater length of their weapons.

Spear saders can opt to get LUK and become "crit spear saders" if they like, building on [[Spear Quicken]]'s 10% boost to CRIT and using weapons like Crescent Scythe (+30% crit). These types of spear crusaders will kill high defense targets faster than their more typical counterparts, but not perform as well on softer foes.

=== Boomer (Shield Boomerang) ===

* STR: 90+
* AGI: 1 or 27
* VIT: 40+
* INT: 66+
* DEX: 1
* LUK: 1

Shield Boomerang Crusaders or "Boomers" are crusaders built entirely around the [[Shield Boomerang]] skill. This skill can never miss, and always deals near-maximum damage. For this reason, boomers ignore DEX and aim to maximize their STR, and then get INT (in multiples of 6) and VIT to help sustain their skill use and HP recovery. Boomers typically hunt any target they can kill in 3 or less [[Shield Boomerang]]s (See the [[Shield Boomerang]] calculator in [[Crusader#See_Also]]), and make for excellent card farmers and hunters of low level enemies.

[[Shield Boomerang]] is ASPD-based, but has a 0.7s delay. While wielding a dagger and using a Berserk Potion, 27 AGI is enough to bring the crusader's ASPD delay with [[Shield Boomerang]] down to its 0.7s hard delay, maximizing how often it can be used. Some boomers opt to get no AGI, however, as this slight boost to how often the skill can be used is difficult to perceive or may even be irrelevant with high enough latency.

=== Devo (Devotion) ===

* STR: 1+ 
* AGI: 1
* VIT: 99
* INT: 18+
* DEX: 71+
* LUK: 1

Devotion Crusaders or "devo saders" are a pure support character and tank who's entire focus is the protection of their party or guild members. Devo saders use their [[Sacrifice]] skill to take damage in place of allies, relying on their enormous health pool and protective skills like [[Auto Guard]] to reduce the damage the party takes overall and keep their allies from dying. Aside from [[Sacrifice]], these crusaders make the best mobbers and tanks.

For "Full Support" devo saders, VIT is the most important attribute. DEX is of secondary importance, owing to the relatively long cast time of [[Sacrifice]]. Some devo saders take as much STR as they can spare so they can carry more consumables (especially if they are WoE/PvP focused). 

Being a hybrid boomer or GC devo sader is also an option, opting for stats closer to those builds in exchange for considerably less dex and slightly less vit. Going this path allows for functional solo leveling, and in a pinch could even add to the boomer's group utility somewhat. Be advised that with less DEX than a full support devo sader, a Phen Card accessory becomes absolutely necessary to avoid being interrupted when casting [[Sacrifice]].

=== GC (Grand Cross) ===
The first priority usually for Grand Cross crusaders is to get a shield with a Thara Frog Card, both to reduce damage taken from popular GC sader targets (Zenorcs, Raydrics, etc), and from [[Grand Cross]]'s recoil damage. Raydric Card is another priority, as its 20% damage reduction can help tremendously with downtime and survivability. Aside from those two pieces of gear, GC saders typically want +INT, +ATK and maxSP/SPregen on their equipment. Porcellio is the usual armor card used, but Argiope is another option (to reduce shadow damage taken without increasing [[Grand Cross]] recoil) or even Bathory (despite the +25% recoil damage) to avoid dangerous/annoying [[Shadow]] element attacks like Dark Jupital Thunder and SP Drain Attack.

Haedonggum [2] is usually the armament of choice for GC saders. It can be carded with Andre or Zipper Bear cards, with Andre being ideal generally, and Zipper Bear being ideal when the sader reaches a point where SP is no longer a concern (high levels, high INT, ample +maxSP/INT/SPregen gear, etc). Bazerald represents another, albeit expensive option, benefiting from the large boost to INT so long as its lower weapon attack doesn't result in more hits of [[Grand Cross]] needed to kill a given target. There are other weapon options that a GC Sader might use to help reduce downtime, see [[Crusader#On Grand Cross and SP Management]] for more information.

New players wanting to play a GC sader should still save up/hunt a Thara Frog Card as a priority. Otherwise, high defense npc-bought equipment like Greaves and Full Plate can add up to decent +DEF, and Earring[0] and Crown[0] serve as relatively affordable sources of +INT.

=== HC (Holy Cross) ===
HC Saders value the same type of equipment that most physical melee do, with a much larger emphasis on damage (+STR, +ATK) rather than AGI or flee as enemies are often dispatched with [[Holy Cross]] at range before reaching the crusader. Being an ASPD-based skill with no aftercast delay, HC saders typically use 2 handed spears like Trident [3] to benefit from [[Spear Quicken]]'s large boost to attack speed. Weapons with Santa Poring Cards are usually used. These can be mixed with a Hydra or Strouf card as most [[Shadow]] element enemies are either [[Demi Human]]s or [[Demon]]s for an 8% higher modifier (68% vs 60%) for those specific enemies. An Ahlspiess is also a common weapon choice for [[Demi Human]] [[Shadow]] enemies like Raydric and Abysmal Knight in Glast Heim.

To help sustain their skill use, Magmawhip carded armor is typically used. If it reduces the total number of [[Holy Cross]] needed to a kill a target, Porcellio/Picky Card may be used instead. Mummy cards may be slotted into tridents to help with early leveling on evasive enemies, or for particularly evasive higher level enemies (e.g., the 3 sword minibosses).

A Trident [3] with 3 Santa Poring cards can serve as an all-purpose weapon for pretty much any target an HC sader would want to hunt, and should be the first priority for new players. Typical budget equipment used by physical melee builds are also good first investments for HC saders.

=== Boomer (Shield Boomerang) ===
Boomers prioritize STR and ATK in their equipment, aiming to get the highest multiple of 10 STR they can through their attributes and gear. In terms of weapons, because [[Shield Boomerang]] doesn't factor weapon damage at all, Main Gauche [4] are typically used with [[Race]]/[[Element]] cards slotted depending on what target is being hunted. For shields, a Herald of God will always deal more damage with [[Shield Boomerang]] than a Tamruan carded Stone Discus [1], regardless of upgrade, but is far more expensive. For anything you want to throw your shield at, consider whether a more expensive shield or weapon would even reduce the number of [[Shield Boomerang]]s needed to kill it (Use the [[Shield Boomerang]] calculator in [[Crusader#See_Also]]).

Similar to HC saders, Magmawhip (typically) or Porcellio/Picky Card (if it reduces the number of [[Shield Boomerang]]s needed) are typically used as armor cards. Sohee or Eggyra cards can be used in footgear to help with reducing downtime, as until high levels SP regen is likely to be an issue even for targets that only require 2 [[Shield Boomerang]]s to be killed.

A Tamuran carded Stone Discus [1] (Ideally +7, as Stone Discus [1] are extremely cheap and they boost damage per upgrade+) should always be the first focus as an investment for new players. Like other dagger-wielding builds, a Poring Dagger is a decent cheap option, as are mantis clips and ring [0]s. Aside from the shield and weapon, high defense swordsman/crusader only npc-bought equipment can serve as a decent choice for armor on the cheap.

=== Devo (Devotion) ===
For using [[Sacrifice]], the crusader's damage reduction is largely irrelevant. Instead, increasing VIT and maxHP are helpful when serving as the damage funnel for the party. For mobbing or tanking, racial reduction shields (e.g., Penomena Card), Raydric carded garments, elemental armor/cards (Pasana, Dokebi, etc) and high DEF/MDEF equipment are sought to minimize damage taken, especially the former items as their effectiveness is not reduced when being hit by multiple targets.  

As a budget option for tanking/mobbing, a fairly high DEF value can be achieved with just npc-bought [[Swordman]]-only items like Greaves, Helm and Full Plate upgraded to +4 (the safe limit for armor).

==Gameplay Tips==
===On Grand Cross and SP Management===
[[Grand Cross]] at rank 10 costs '''100 SP'''. Even with high INT and proper equipment, a GC Sader will inevitably run out of SP while soloing and have a lot of downtime. There are tools and strategies to help manage and reduce downtime as a GC Sader. 

The first is overkilling enemies. If using a stat calculator (See: [[Crusader#See_Also]]) shows you deal 15k holy damage to a Raydric that has 8613 HP, you are essentially wasting SP using rank 10 of [[Grand Cross]]. Each rank of [[Grand Cross]] costs 7 additional SP and has a +40% increase to its modifier (E.g., Going from rank 10 -> rank 9 saves 7 SP and deals 460% DMG instead of 500% DMG). In the aforementioned example with Raydric, killing them with rank 5 [[Grand Cross]] saves 35 SP per cast but still kills them in a single cast. There are other tradeoffs to doing this, if you end up with more than one Raydric on the same cell when [[Grand Cross]] goes off, it may not kill them as the number of waves that hit will be reduced. A good strategy is to find out what the lowest rank of [[Grand Cross]] you need to kill a given target is, and have that hotkeyed as well as [[Grand Cross]] rank 10, using one or the other as needed.

Another way to save SP as a GC Sader is through certain weapons. A Hunter Fly carded Saber [3] will heal the crusader (based on the number of cards) at a given chance for a given amount, for each target hit ''per wave of [[Grand Cross]]''. If you can still kill a given target with a single [[Grand Cross]], using this weapon can save on [[Heal]] casts afterwards. Similarly, using a Moonlight Dagger restores 3 SP per target hit, ''per wave of [[Grand Cross]]'', and is another option to decrease downtime.

Cute Pet System:
==Basics== A cute pet is a tamed monster which will follow you throughout the game to keep you company. They have no special skills, but Pets which achieve a Cordial or Loyal level intimacy will provide their owner with certain bonuses while accompanying them. There are several different types of Cute Pets with varying levels of difficulty to obtain and maintain (keep fed). Unlike other servers, you can change the name of your pet as many times as you'd like! ==Obtaining a Pet== To get a pet, you will need to have a pet taming item and an incubator. Incubators can be purchased from various pet NPCs in most major towns. Pet taming items must be obtained via monster drops or some special items/quests. Refer to the chart below to see what is needed for each pet. To use a taming item, double click on it in the item window. When you see the monster you want to tame on the screen, hover the circle over the monster, and click. A slot machine will appear and you must click again to get a chance at taming the monster. If you fail, you lose the taming item and get no pet. If you succeed, you will use the taming item and receive a pet egg. The success rate is only affected by the remaining HP of the monster. Getting the monster to 1% HP will increase the success chances to twice the capture rate. Once you have obtained a pet egg, use a [[Image:643.png]] [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=643 Pet Incubator] (sold by pet NPC in major towns) to hatch it. To hatch the egg, click on the Incubator and a small menu will appear like the one you get when you use a magnifier. Click on the pet you wish to hatch and it will appear. It is a good idea to have food handy when you open the egg for the first time because the pet will be hungry. ==Raising a Pet== The first thing that should be done is feeding the pet. If it's not fed quickly enough it will likely run away. It is also likely to run away if it is fed too much. When feeding a pet, open the status window for the pet. Right click on the pet and click on the option for status. A window will pop up where you will see the name of the pet, what level the pet is, if it is wearing any accessories, and whether or not it is hungry. To feed your pet, right-click on it and choose "Feed Pet". Your pet will then make an emote, letting you know it has eaten. It is possible to overfeed your pet. Only feed it once at a time and its intimacy will slowly rise. It should give you the [[Image:Ok.gif|31x31px]] Ok! emote. If you continue to feed it it will give the [[Image:Hmm.gif|30x30px]] Hmmm or [[Image:Pif.gif]] Pif emote. Feed it again and it will use the [[Image:Omg.gif]] OMG! emote and die. You must control how much your pet eats. Another note about feeding pets: [[Image:528.png]] [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=528 Monster's Feed] is not the same as [[Image:537.png]] [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=537 Pet Food] despite having identical icons. Pets will not eat Monster's Feed. Monster's Feed is only good for recovering your own HP. See the Pet Comparison charts for the appropriate food for your pet. When you are tired of your pet or have run out of food to keep it out, you can return it to egg status. Simply right click on the pet and choose "Return to egg". You will need an Incubator to hatch the pet again. You do not need to take accessories off the pet when you put it into its egg. ==Mechanics== There are 5 Hunger and Intimacy Levels. == General ==
DEF (''def''ense) protects against physical attacks. Physical attacks are generally attacks based wholly or partially on [[ATK]]. However, there are exceptions.

The descriptions used here refer to hard and soft DEF. These names are used for clarity. The vast majority of players do not use these terms in general conversation, and instead refer Armor Def (hard) and Vit Def (soft). Hard DEF works as a percentage reduction. Soft DEF is a subtractive reduction.

== Hard DEF ==
var HARD_DEF = 0;
HARD_DEF += HARD_DEF_A;
HARD_DEF = Math.floor( HARD_DEF * (1 + HARD_DEF_B / 100 ) );

HARD_DEF_A : Sum of additive bonuses
HARD_DEF_B : Sum of multiplicative bonuses

Base value of 0. Add bonuses from armor, cards, skills, etc. 

=== Additive Bonuses ===

*Armor [[Refinement System|upgrades]]: +0.7 per point (inaccurate, exact value unknown)

== Soft DEF ==
var SOFT_DEF = 0;
SOFT_DEF += Math.floor( VIT * 0.5 );
SOFT_DEF += Math.max( Math.floor( VIT * 0.3 ) , Math.floor( VIT^2 / 150 ) - 1 );
SOFT_DEF += SOFT_DEF_A;
SOFT_DEF = Math.floor( SOFT_DEF * (1 + SOFT_DEF_B / 100 ) );

SOFT_DEF_A : Sum of additive bonuses
SOFT_DEF_B : Sum of multiplicative bonuses

Base value of 0. Add complex result of VIT. Add bonuses from other sources.

== DEF Reversal ==
In special conditions, such as for the Ice Pick weapon and [[Occult Impaction]] skill, the DEF formula is reversed.

In this special case of reversed DEF, the damage multiplier is found by (Hard DEF + Soft DEF)/100. For example, against a 5+15 DEF target, a normal 200 ATK weapon would only deal 175 damage; an Ice Pick on a character with 200 ATK, would do 40 damage. Conversely, against a 50+90 DEF target, the weapons would do 10 and 280 damage respectively.

==Overview==
Rhythm and balance are qualities cultivated by all Archers, however, only the truly talented are allowed to learn the secret steps of the Dancers. These scantily clad seductresses gain the power to influence the minds of allies and enemies alike.

It is said that time slows down when a Dancer starts to move her hips to the sound of some mysterious tune; that those watching may lose control of their bodies and find their magic reserves either greatly improved or gone altogether. Where their male counterparts, the Bards, are more bent on support, Dancers specialize at disruptive maneuvers, which make them an invaluable asset in the War of Emperium.

Supporting with a Bard or Dancer requires a different approach than other classes. Music-based buffs are mostly percentual values, as opposed to the absolute values of Priest buffs, and require careful strategy and positioning, but playing as an Archer should already provide some experience in this respect. Despite their supportive role, one should not forget that Dancers are also capable of dealing good quantities of damage, one of their main advantages over Huntresses is their immense SP pool which allows them to continually use Double Strafe instead of normal attacks, ensuring decent damage output.

To understand how to build a Bard or Dancer, knowledge of all their skills is needed. Dancer and Bard skills are, in comparison to other classes, very stat dependent. In general, there are 2 types of skills for both a Dancer and a Bard; skills which can be sung or danced without a partner of the opposite gender and those where the player needs another Bard or Dancer respectively.

As a Dancer, only whips, daggers and bows are available for weapons, whereas Bards can use instruments instead of whips.

* When armed with a Whip:
** Bow skills (Double Strafe, Arrow Shower, Arrow Repel) cannot be used
** Performance Skills, as well as Amp and Encore are available
** Whip skills (Slinging Arrow, Arrow Vulcan) can be used
** Whip damage depends on the Dancer's dex, NOT str. Just like it does for bows

1. Head to Comodo. Near the Kafra employee, there will be a male NPC named Bor Robin (comodo 193, 151) who will grant entrance into the Dancer Quest area.

2. Upon heading inside, talk to Aile (job_duncer 43, 93) to the left side of the stage. She will ask the player to bring one of the following set of items:

3. Once finished signing up, it's time to head to the right side of the stage and talk to Bijou (job_duncer 95, 93) to take the quiz.

5. After passing the quiz, Bijou will send the player to Dance on the stage. At this point one should make sure to equip a Bow and some arrows and then head behind the stage to meet another NPC with a "Waiting Room" chat window above her head. Entering the chatroom will put the player on queue for the trial. 

6. The exam is a simple test of movement and quick responses. Hotkeying Arrow Shower or Double Strafe and Improve Concentration is suggested. 

*'''Note''': there's a poring at the end that has to be killed with a bow. Using Improve Concentration is optional, even though the NPC will ask for it.
[[File:DancerQuest.png|frameless]]

The Dancing pattern is as follows.

# Up
# Down
# Left
# Right
# Center
# Hold (just remain on the center tile)
# Improve Concentration
# Left
# Down '''(Skip this step and go right directly)'''
# Right 
# Hold (just remain on the right tile)
# Left, Center, Right, Up
# Right
# Left, Center, Down, Up
# Left, Center, Down, Up
# Down
# Left
# Center
# Arrow Shower or Double Strafe

For those future dancers who are having problems with this part of the test: An effective way to pass this exam is to only perform the first and last steps for sequences with more than two steps, rather than hitting all the tiles. For example: instead of doing "Left Center Right Up" one simply goes from Left to Up.

7. Return to the NPC who gave the quiz for the job change to Dancer. She will reward you with either a Whip for Job 50, or a Rope for any job level lower than 50.

From May 8th, 2024 Patch Notes. Costumes are '''purely cosmetic & have no stats'''. They're also are '''account bound/non-tradeable'''.

=== Why Donate? ===
Up until now, all the costs of running our servers – from the main server to web servers, patch servers, proxies, and test servers – have been covered by the staff. That's right, no one gets paid for their hard work! But here's the thing: We only have one developer right now to keep things running smoothly. However, with the demand for new features and content growing, we need to expand our team. That's where donations come in.

=== How Will Donations Help? ===
With your generous contributions, we'll be able to:

* Hire additional developers to speed up the creation of exciting new content, maps, quests, and events.
* Cover server costs, but only if we gather more donations than we need to cover expenses. Otherwise, we've got it covered!

=== Transparency is Key ===
We're committed to transparency. That's why we'll be providing quarterly reports detailing our server expenses, whether we've received donations or not. We want you to know exactly where your money is going.

=== A Final Note ===
We want to stress that even if we don't receive any donations, our team will continue to support the server financially. Your support means the world to us, and we're incredibly grateful for each and every one of you. Thank you for being part of our community and for your continued support.

=== How to Donate ===
Donate @ https://buymeacoffee.com/payonstories  and open a ticket (⁠💵open-ticket) with all your details in Discord. Points are manually processed and will be transferred to your account in 24-48 hours from the ticket creation date.

=== Costume Points & Costume Shop ===
Once the ticket is processed in Discord, your account will be loaded with Costume Points.

Use the @costumeshop command to access the Costume Shop.

* Items in costume shop will be exclusive for at least 6 months. [After which, they may be obtainable in-game via quest or events]

* Items gained from costume shop are account-bound.

* Pets gained from costume shop are loyal by default and do not get hungry.

Costume Points can be gained via donation, more Information on ⁠💵open-ticket in Discord

Endless Tower:
== Overview ==
'''Endless Tower''' is completely '''reworked, fully customized Payon Stories instance''' perfect for parties seeking for new and exciting PvM challenges.

Participating parties make their way up the 100 floor tower, fighting various monsters, mini bosses and MVPs on their way up (including custom Payon Stories monsters and MVPs) during given time limit. Players must defeat all monsters on a particular floor before the door to the next floor can open. Once on a floor, players are unable to go backwards; thus the only ways to leave the tower is to die and respawn, leave the party, log out, use a Butterfly Wing, or use Warp skill.

There are no consumables item use limitations (except for Fly Wings).

Entering the Endless Tower is account limited and available once a week, with a 7 days cooldown. '''Server-wide cooldown reset takes places every Sunday at 18:00 (servertime).'''

<u>Key Features:</u>
* '''100 Floors''' full of monsters, mini bosses and MVPs fights
* Maximum party capacity: '''8 players'''
* '''160-minute Time Limit''' to finish the challenge
* '''7 days Entrance Cooldown - Account Bound''' (resets every Sunday 18:00 servertime)
* '''Rewards including Treasure Chests''' full of exciting items available after completing the challenge
* Recommended for parties/players minimum at '''90+ Base Level'''
'''''Note: With ongoing forward, Endless Tower will be reworked and further balanced in future to better fit the new content and player progress of Payon Stories server.'''''

== How to Enter? ==
[[File:TowerKeeper.png|thumb|233x233px|Tower Keeper NPC]]

=== Starting instance ===
To enter Endless Tower, create a party and speak to the '''Tower Keeper NPC''' '''(oldnewpayon 121,183)''' located in north-east part outside of Payon Palace.

When generating instance, Party leader will be shown list of members, who are eligible to warp. Players who are not eligible, will be shown proper message when they try to enter the instance.

Tower Keeper NPC charges every party member with zenny fee for entering Endless Tower:

* 50.000 zenny if you enter the instance for the first time
* 10.000 zenny if you enter the instance for the second, third, etc. time.

=== Phantom Floors ===
there are 4 unnumbered floors through the tower which act as an attendance check.

Phantom floors have a time limit and only one enemy which takes only 1 point of dmg from all sources and has to be reduced by 1000 HP within the limit, otherwise the ET run immediately ends.

* 1st Phantom floor appears after clearing floor 25, Phantom start with 4000 hp and has to be reduced to 3000 hp, 150s time limit
* 2nd Phantom floor appears after clearing floor 50, Phantom start with 3000 hp and has to be reduced to 2000 hp, 120s time limit
* 3rd Phantom floor appears after clearing floor 75, Phantom start with 2000 hp and has to be reduced to 1000 hp, 90s time limit
* 4rd Phantom floor appears after clearing floor 99, Phantom start with 1000 hp and has to be reduced to 0 hp, 60s time limit

Each phantom floor awards all players with 1 Ashes of Darkness item, which can be later used to re-enter the tower at higher floor and skipping the long walk. The Ashes of Darkness is awarded on entrance, so make sure you have free inventory space before entering the phantom floor. The Ashes of Darkness is only awarded if you enter the phantom floor within two minutes after the portal in spawned.

=== Re-entering the Tower during ongoing instance ===
If you need to re-enter the Tower during currently ongoing instance (i.ex. after your party dies), you can do it by speaking to '''Tower Keeper NPC''' again and paying him additional '''10.000 zenny fee'''.

There is a limitation of 10 re-entries per party allowed during each intance.

Upon entering Floor 1 entrance, you can talk to special '''Immortal Blazer NPC (upper one),''' and give him various amounts of '''Ashes of Darkness''' custom items (dropped in Endless Tower) to exchange them for teleport to the higher Endless Tower floors:

* 25 Floor - 1 Ashes of Darkness consumed
* 51 Floor - 2 Ashes of Darkness consumed
* 76 Floor - 3 Ashes of Darkness consumed

'''''Note: Using Ashes of Darkness is the only way to reach Endless Tower top levels faster. If you don't have the Ashes you'll have to climb all the floors <u>on foot</u> (all defeated monsters on previous floors will no longer be there).'''''
[[File:ET Immortal Blazer.png|center|thumb|260x260px|Immortal Blazer location at F1 entrance]]

== Rewards ==
To complete the Endless Tower challenge and '''receive hard-gained rewards''', party members need to '''defeat all monster on all 100 floors within given time limit''' (160-minutes). Please note that even if you will be challenged by a party wipe during on-going instance (withing time limit), you can still re-enter the Tower, climb the floors and continue to kill monsters to receive the rewards at the end.

On completion of 100F (after killing last monster), all party members will be warped out of Endless Tower. '''Only party leader''' will be able to enter Treasure Room and collect Rewards from '''special Treasure Chests''' by initiating talk with '''Tower Keeper NPC'''. This is done to ensure instance timer doesn't end before treasure chests are opened.

'''Treasure Chest''' '''contain various different items as rewards''': consumables, equipment pieces, etc useful items. Official Treasure Chest drop list is not yet released, so it is recommended to take the challenge and check the prizes out by yourself!

== Notes ==

*Each hit from a Firewall carries an [[MATK]] modifier of 50%.
*Firewall hits at a very high rate of attack: approximately 40 to 50 times per second.  Be aware that if there is any significant lag, fast-moving enemies can pass through Firewalls without being hit.  Also, if the mage casting the Firewall is incapacitated ([[Stun]]ned, [[Frozen]], [[Stone Curse]]d), the Firewall will not process attacks.

*Firewalls are aligned such that they are generally perpendicular to a line formed by the caster and the cast point, with the center cell being on the cast point.
*Firewalls with the caster's position as the cast point are aligned north-south on the map.

Forging:
== General == [[Blacksmith]]s can forge weapons from different materials. The materials used decide the weapon to be created as well as any additional properties, such as element, the weapon will have. Forged weapons do not have Card Slots. Rods, Bows, Instruments, Books and Katars cannot be forged, nor can level 4 weapons. For material lists see weapon materials or they can also be found on the corresponding Smith skill: [[Smith Dagger]], [[Smith Sword]], [[Smith Axe]], [[Smith Knucklebrace]], [[Smith Mace]] or [[Smith Spear]]. When forging a weapon there are 3 available slots for modifying items. Items such as Flame Heart, Mystic Frozen, Rough Wind and Great Nature can be used to imbue the weapon with the [[Fire]], [[Water]], [[Wind]] and [[Earth]] elements respectively. A weapon may only have one element at a time and using more than one elemental stone will cause the forge to fail. Slots may also be fitted with Star Crumbs. One, two, and three Star Crumbs will (respectively) add +5, +10, and +40 seeking damage to all attacks from the weapon. The extra damage cannot miss and ignores defense. == Process== 1. Make sure that all of the necessary items are in your inventory (not your cart). Then use the necessary hammer for the weapon level you wish to create. Once you click OK (or press enter) the hammer will disappear even if you quit. 2. A list of weapons you can forge will appear. Select the weapon you wish to create and continue. 3. A second window will appear detailing which items will be used up by the forging attempt. There are also 3 spaces to place Elemental Stones and/or Star Crumbs. 4. Drag and drop the extra materials from your inventory to the slots to add them to the weapon. Even if the forging attempt fails the items on the list as well as those in the slots will be lost. 5. If the forge is successful the newly created weapon will appear in your inventory. == Success Rate == {| class="wikitable" ! Weapon Level | 1 || 2 || 3 |- ! Base Success Rate | -0% || -20% || -30% |} {| class="wikitable" ! Smith Skill Level | 1 || 2 || 3 |4 |- ! Success rate bonus | +4% || +8% || +12% | +16% |} {| class="wikitable" ! Anvil | Anvil || Oridecon Anvil || Golden Anvil || Emperium Anvil |- ! Bonus | +0% || +3% || +5% || +10% |} * Forging success rate is decided by Forging Equipment, skills, [[DEX]], [[LUK]] and job level. * Forging equipment includes Anvil, Oridecon Anvil, Golden Anvil, Emperium Anvil, Iron Hammer, Golden Hammer and Oridecon Hammer. ** Hammers are used to begin the forging process. Iron Hammers are used to forge level 1 [[Weapons]], Golden Hammers are used to forge level 2 [[Weapons]] and Oridecon Hammers are used to forge level 3 [[Weapons]]. ** Anvils are kept in the main inventory and increase success rate. '''You cannot forge weapons with weapon level higher than your smith skill level.''' * In addition to the success rate bonus from the smith skill, [[Weaponry Research]] and [[Oridecon Research]] also affect (or should affect) the success rates of forging different weapons as well as which weapons are available to forge. * Each point of [[DEX]] and each point of [[LUK]] is believed to add 0.1% chance to successfully forging a weapon. For example, with 19 Dex and 1 Luk a Blacksmith would gain an additional 2% chance to forge a weapon after taking other factors into account. * Each Job Level is believed to add 0.2% to the overall success rate. * Using forging slots decreases the success rate of the forge attempt. An elemental stone takes off 20% and each Star Crumb takes off 15%. === Forge Calculator === A '''Forging Calculator''' can be found [https://ratemyserver.net/forge_calc.php '''''here'''''.] == Ranking System == For Forgers there is a system in which you are ranked amongst all your peers of who can make the most weapons. * Rank Point +1: For upgrading a level 1 weapon that you have forged to +10. * Rank Point +10: For successfully creating a level 3 weapon that contains 3 stones (either 2 star crumbs and an elemental stone, or three star crumbs). * Rank Point +25: For upgrading a level 2 weapon that you have forged to +10. * Rank Point +1000: For upgrading a level 3 weapon that you have forged to +10. You can check Blacksmith ranks via usage of /Blacksmith command. A weapon created by ranked blacksmith will deal an extra +10 seeking damage (pierces defense and never misses). == Item Look & Feel == * When a weapon is forged successfully it's name will have the forger's name attached.
Xeyron's Sword * Normally the forger's name will appear in blue, however if the character that forged the weapon has been deleted the forger's name is lost, and the weapons becomes nameless.
Nameless's Sword * When imbued with an element the name of the element will appear before the Weapon's name and after the forger's name.
Xeyron's Fire Sword * When imbued with one or more Star Crumb the term 'Very' will appear before the forgers name for each Star Crumb used followed by 'Strong'.
Very Very Very Strong Xeyron's Sword * When imbued with both an element and Star Crumbs the weapon's name will follow the naming conventions in the order Star Crumbs, Forger, Element, Weapon Name.
Very Very Strong Xeyron's Fire Sword [[Category: Blacksmith]]

==== Treasure digging ====
To collect treasures, find '''Mound of Sand''' located all over Island and take part of mini-game of digging!

[[File:Freeze5.png|thumb|301x301px]]
<u><small>Rules of the mini-game:</small></u>
* <small>Find a place to dig (Mound of Sand)</small>
* <small>Once selected a spot, shovel will light up with specific light:</small> 

<small>'''- YELLOW''' (that means the treasure is buried no deeper than 50 cm from the surface),</small> 

<small>'''- ORANGE''' (that means the treasure is buried between 50 - 75 cm from the surface),</small> 

<small>- '''RED''' (that means the treasure is buried between 75 - 100 cm from the surface)</small>

* <small>You can dig the treasure by using different strategies:</small>

<small>- '''With all your might''' (results in digging between 15 - 25 cm)</small>

<small>- '''Digging normally''' (results in digging between 10 - 18 cm)</small>

<small>- '''Stepping on the shovel softly''' (results in digging between 5 - 12 cm)</small>

<small>- '''Use the shovel like a trowel''' (results in digging between 3 - 6 cm)</small>

<small>- '''Scrape the earth''' (results in digging between 1 - 3 cm)</small>

* <small>You can only use the shovel ten times before it breaks, there is also a chance to destroy the treasure, so it is advice to choose the digging strategy wisely.</small>

[[Undead]] and [[Boss]] monsters cannot be frozen but can still be damaged by Frost Diver. If a mage decides to become a [[Wizard]], the skill [[Storm Gust]] can replace the need of Frost Diver for mobs. The other disabling skill, [[Stone Curse]], is also an option.

Game and Player Rules:
'''Rules tl;dr'''
* No Multiclienting for any reason – be that on one or multiple devices.
* No RMT or other out of game trading.
* No multiple master accounts. You may own one Master Account which houses 3 Game Accounts.
* No griefing or kill stealing.
* No botting, modifying the client, unapproved GRFs or other 3rd party tools (besides dgVoodoo).
* No scamming.

'''For more details, read below.'''

= Core Principles =
=== Submitting Evidence ===
When reporting issues, you should aim to provide one of the following:
* '''Gameplay recordings''' (.rrf replay files or third-party recordings like Medal).
* '''For trade/agreement issues:''' Screenshots or Recordings, showing timestamps of the trades and players involved.
* '''For chat issues:''' Screenshots showing timestamps OR use the /savechat command for .txt logs.

'''Note:''' All evidence submitted is kept strictly confidential and not shared outside of staff.

=== Punishments ===
* Penalties will be based on the severity and context of the infraction, which will be determined by Staff. They can range between being given a warning to becoming blacklisted.
* Punishments given for in-game offenses will only affect the Master and/or Game Accounts.
* Punishments given for Discord offenses will only affect the Discord account, unless the player is blacklisted.

'''Note:''' Generally the rules only apply to offenses that happen in the Payon Stories Discord and the game. However, in extreme cases, we may act on evidence provided from outside this scope.

=== False Reports ===
* False Reporting of other players is not allowed. This includes, but is not limited to, framing, proof alteration, and threats of reporting someone.

=== Baiting ===
* Baiting other players into performing a rule breaking action is not allowed. This includes, but is not limited to, standing in a mobbers way to bait mob dropping or taunting.

=== Definitions ===
'''Master Account''' – An account on the Payon Stories website that requires an email address to create. A Master Account holds a maximum of 3 Game Accounts.

'''Game Account''' – The account used to log into the game. This account is where your characters are kept.

'''Warning''' – The player receives a warning from staff to avoid or change a behavior or action.

'''Temporary Ban''' – The Master Account and all Game Accounts under it are banned from play for X number of days. During this time period, the player may not play on the server in any way, including using the guest account of a friend. Someone that knowingly gives Guest Account access to a temporarily banned player could possibly receive a punishment for doing so.

'''Permanent Ban (permaban)''' – The Master Account and all Game Accounts under it are permanently banned. The player may make a new Master Account and start over.

'''Blacklisted''' – The player’s master account is permanently banned, and the player is not allowed to make a new one. The player will be removed from the Payon Stories Discord. The player may not play on the server by any method.

= Accounts & Multi-Clienting =
=== Master Accounts ===
* Each player is allowed to own only one (1) Master Account, which will house three (3) Game Accounts within it.
* You must use a permanent, accessible email address (no temporary or disposable addresses).
* If you share an IP address with another person, each player must use their own separate Master Account. Avoid, if possible, having the other person log into their own accounts on your system. See 2.6 Multi-Clienting.

=== Game Accounts ===
* Each player may own up to three Game Accounts, which is housed by their Master Account.
* You may only have one character logged in per master account – with the exception of @autotrade.

=== Account Sharing ===
* Account sharing, trading, or transferring is forbidden, with the exception of Guild Account (see rule 2.4).

=== Guild Accounts ===
* Guild leaders may create one official guild account using the '''Guild Account Admin (oldnewpayon, 92, 159)'''
* This account may only have two characters: a Brewer (Alchemist) and a Forger (Blacksmith). They may be used for vending.
* The Guild Leader owns and is responsible for all actions taken on this account.
* If the guild account is transferred to a new leader, you must inform the previous owner and Staff first via a ticket.
* You may only have access – including owning – to one guild account at a time.

=== Multi-Clienting ===
* You may only log in and control ONE character at a time.
* Examples of violations include:
** Buffing, healing, or leeching your own characters.
** Logging in to ANY two accounts at the same time and transferring items or zeny between them.
** Semi-AFK gameplay (e.g., using auto-follow while being inactive on the following character).
* '''Rule of Thumb:''' ''If it looks like multi-clienting and benefits like multi-clienting, we treat it like multi-clienting, even if it is actually two players.''

= Cheating & Exploits =
=== Third-Party Tools ===
Forbidden: Any use of macros, bots, or automation tools (e.g., AutoHotKey) is forbidden.  
Allowed: Recording software, Wine, or dgVoodoo are permitted (if unsure, ask Staff first).

=== Client Modifications ===
* Allowed edits:
** Music files (sound effects cannot be changed).
** UI skins.
* Any GRF or client edits that have not been approved by staff and made available on the PS website are strictly prohibited.

=== Exploits ===
* Report bugs and exploits immediately via a ticket. You will not be punished for reporting them.
* Tolerated "exploits": Ice Wall traps, animation canceling and such, as long as they don’t directly give you an unfair advantage over other players.
* An example of non-allowed exploits: Finding a skill that does irregularly high damage in certain situations and using it to hunt MVPs.

= Market & Trading =
=== Vending Etiquette ===
* Respect Spacing: Maintain a distance of 3 cells from any NPC and 2 cells from other player shops or chatrooms.
* No Spot Stealing: Never use skills (e.g., First Aid) or other methods to glitch into a spot already occupied by another vendor, regardless if the vendor has a shop established.

=== Fair Pricing ===
* No "placeholder" shops: Do not set up shops with unreasonable prices (e.g., selling Jellopy for 10,000,000 zeny) just to hold a spot.
* No misrepresentation: Do not falsely advertise items (e.g., selling unslotted gear as if it were slotted).

=== Scamming ===
* This includes, but is not limited to: misrepresenting items for sale, indirect trades, or engaging in deceitful trades.
* Staff may review broken agreements between players if submitted with concrete evidence (see 1.1) of the incident in a reasonable time frame.

=== Real Money Trading (RMT) ===
* Trading in-game items or services for any type of real-world or favors is considered RMT.
* Anyone advertising or soliciting RMT services will receive a punishment that may result in being blacklisted.
* We encourage everyone to help keep the community fair and enjoyable. If you’re aware of RMT activity, please report it. Knowingly assisting, hiding, or protecting those involved in RMT goes against this spirit and will be treated as participation in RMT.

= Behavior & Communication =
=== General Communication Rules ===
* English is the only language permitted in public chat channels. Players must be able to respond to staff in English when approached.
* Be civil.
* Do not advertise other game servers. (Talking about them is fine.)
* Avoid the following topics:
** Harassment, racism, sexism, real-life threats, NSFW content, politics, or any topic that can generate drama and heated arguments.
** This includes jokes, memes, indirect references, or attempts to “test the boundaries”.
** Staff alone will decide what someone meant, what happened, and how it affected others, based on a full review of the situation. Players who try to influence, pressure, or interfere with staff decisions will receive a warning, mute, or ban depending on the severity.

=== Impersonation & Names ===
* Impersonating a Staff member results in a permanent ban.
* Offensive character or guild names will result in forced renames.
* Staff will not assist with other renames.
* Names are first-come, first-serve. Names of retired or banned players will not be released.
* All '''General Communication Rules in 5.1''' also apply to names and impersonation. Violations through names, guild, party, or attempts to mimic staff identity will be treated the same as if they were said in chat.

=== Harassment ===
* Harassment includes, but is not limited to: stalking, slander, bullying, and targeted, repeated griefing.
* Retaliation after a report may be seen as a form of harassment.

=== Staff and Players ===
* Every member of Payon Stories Staff is a volunteer not receiving any compensation for their work outside or inside the game. They are regular players when logging into their accounts.
* Staff members will never ask you for your private information or passwords, or use secret characters or accounts. See https://discord.com/channels/1051580563624042547/1064571111603441734 for the current list of Discord and In-game Accounts.
* Staff members are subject to the same rules as players, and may be reported.
* Respectful disagreements are fine, but targeted slander or harassment will be dealt with accordingly, especially when targeted at Staff.
* If you are concerned about a staff member's integrity, please open a ticket with corresponding evidence.

= Gameplay & Fair Play =
=== Griefing ===
* Do not use skills to intentionally harass or obstruct other players (e.g., buffing aggressive monsters, using Ice Wall to trap players).

=== Mob Hunting ===
* Mobbing is allowed and is a valid playstyle, but monopolizing an entire map or spawn area for extended periods is not.
* If you engage with a mob, it should be with the purpose to kill it. Exceptions:
** Luring hostile monsters into a safe spot to set up a map.
** Mob Dropping, as in, luring mobs (including those from Dead Branches) to kill other players is forbidden.
* Static parties are not allowed. The only exception which are currently allowed for static play:
** Guild Dungeons and any PvP-Enabled Maps

=== Kill Stealing (KS) ===
* Do not attack monsters or mini-bosses that are already chasing or engaged by another player.
* Do not aggro-steal mobs from another player by e.g. putting yourself directly in the path of a monster.
* The @noks command is for protecting a mob you are actively fighting – not for claiming ownership of a mob you are not attacking.

=== MVP Rules ===
* When players are '''competing''' for an MVP, the rules 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 are not in effect.
** Note: Hindering other players without actively engaging the MVP, such as spawning monsters and leaving the map afterwards, is not considered competing.
* These ground rules must always be followed:
** Skills that block or completely nullify another player's skills or damage on an MVP are not allowed.
** Reducing or mitigating another player’s effectiveness (for example, through traps, ice walls, or general damage reduction (NOTE: Reduction, not nullifying)) is acceptable as part of normal competition.
** Using Skills such as Safetywall, Pneuma, Land Protector, and Aspersio (against Holy MvPs) specifically to block player damage/skill on an MvP are not allowed.
** Intentionally making it difficult for others to loot items that are under the protection of the loot timer (e.g., by tanking a mob on top of the loot) is not allowed.
* An MvP is considered '''active''' in the following cases:
** '''The MvP is currently alive.'''
** '''Fixed-Spawn MvPs:''' The tomb is visible and active. This indicates the fixed respawn timer is running, and players may legitimately prepare, camp, or compete.
** '''In simple terms''': The MvP is considered Active when players are near the MvP itself or its tomb (for fixed-spawn MvPs).

* An MvP is considered '''not active''' in the following cases:
** '''MvP is dead'''.
** Even if a '''tomb appears''', the MvP is not considered active because its respawn location is not fixed and it may not appear near that tomb.
** '''In simple terms''': The MvP is not considered active unless players are near the actual MvP.

=== PVP Zones ===
* When players are in PVP enabled zones, such as guild dungeons, the rules 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 are not in effect.
* Please keep in mind that the Behavior & Communications rules still apply to these areas.

= Spirit of the Rules =
* These rules cannot cover every possible scenario. Staff reserve the right to act against actions that abuse game mechanics or violate the principles of fair play, even if not explicitly listed here.
* When in doubt, ask! If you are unsure if something is allowed, please submit a ticket and ask for clarification.

General Game Info:
== Overview ==
Payon Stories is a Massively Multiplayer Online Role Playing Game (MMORPG). Payon Stories allows you to create a virtual character, customize it, and partake in epic adventures across exotic lands.

Payon Stories is a great way to hang out with friends as well as make new ones. With an ever-expanding universe, in-game events, and a large community of users, there are always places to see, things to do, and people to meet in this virtual world!

== Payon Stories Features ==
*Classic [[Classes]] with [[Class Rebalance]] changes give you a lot of variety in your character builds.
*Status and Skill reset NPC available 
*Quests that are unique to Payon Stories are ever increasing and provide more options.
*Monster Rebalancing and experience changes provide players with many new leveling options. 
*Simple game mechanics that are easy to learn!
*A seasonal War of Emperium system is in place to ensure new guilds can jump into the fray and compete at any time!
*Fair seasonal Alchemist and Blacksmith point system, to be able to compete at any time
*Server is not built on any pay-to-win systems or donation system and is self-funded with plenty of capital, allowing for the guarantee of stability and longevity.
*Donation available, but only for costume headgears with no effect.
*For more information check out [[Server Information]]!

== Official Story ==
In a time of strife between God, humans, and demons...

Scarred during the gruesome war and avoiding total destruction altogether, God, humans, and demons manage to enter into a truce...

But after 1,000 years of fragile and forged peace in the world...

The lengthy peace eventually led the humans to forget their memories of the scars and hardship from the war. As they forgot faults of the past, selfishness, corruption, and arrogance slowly spread throughout the land...

Finally, the balance of peace broke and strange occurrences started happening. There came a strange howl from the boundaries that divided God, humans, and demons. Peaceful creatures became aggressive and attacked innocent villagers. Violent earthquakes ripped whole continents apart. Great hail storms drove some species to the brink of extinction...

The mysterious legend of demons were rediscovered...

As the fragile peace began to fall apart, stories about the parts of Ymir protecting the peace began to spread among the adventurers. Forgetting the true nature of the ancient relics, people set out to seek the pieces out of selfishness and the promise of wealth that would come with it...

*The damage Grand Cross deals against enemies is not affected by:

**This damage dealt to caster is based on damage done to targets. It is of element: [[Holy]] and race: [[Demi Human]]. **20% HP is lost every cast regardless of reductions. It is part of the casting cost of Grand Cross.

[[File:Guest Account Admin NPC.png|frameless|284x284px]]

The '''Guest Account Admin NPC''' (oldnewpayon 43, 106) helps to create and manage guest account.

Users are allowed to create a “Guest Account” which allows them to share access of their characters to other users without compromising their account data. The person who is a guest on the account must have an active Master Account on Payon Stories server as well.

'''However, players must trust who they loan those characters out to.''' If a rule is broken on the Guest Account, then all accounts under that Master Account will face punishment as well. Guest Accounts still follow the “linked accounts” Player and Server rules. 

'''! REMEMBER: Guest account or lend any items is up to the player's risk. Don't do it if you can't trust the other person. !'''

== How to create Guest Account? ==
Speak to the NPC and open dialogue. Here you can click on "information" to get more info about how the whole guest system works. To create your Guest Account go to "Create Guest Account" and the NPC will ask you for a new username and password.

'''Note: Remember that every guest account has the prefix guest_[username]'''

[[File:Guest1.png|frameless]]

As an example: above username will be guest_ayami

1. Enter the username of your guest account

2. Enter the password for your guest account

3. Reenter the password you just created

4. Enter the days until the guest account expires

5. Congratulations, you now have an account that can set permissions!

[[File:Guest2.png|frameless]]

Once everything is done correctly, the guest will have to log in with the account you just created!
Guild Account Admin:
[[File:Guild Account Admin.png|frameless|305x305px]]

The '''Guild Account Admin NPC''' (oldnewpayon 94, 159) helps to create and manage guild account.

A guild leader is allowed to create one single guild account. The name of this account must have as prefix 'guild_'(automatically inserted by NPC), eg. “guild_unicorn”. Only two characters are allowed on this account: 

* One brewer (alchemist)
* One forger (blacksmith)

These characters may be used for vending as well. 

The leader can remove this access by changing the password at any time. The account belongs to the guild leader and they are fully responsible for all usage performed on this account. Staff isn't responsible for any items lost from Guild Account due to any mistake. 

This account will be allowed, by exception, as the fourth account of each user. 

If a user of this guild account wants to access another guild account (eg. because they moved to another guild), they must inform the owner of the previous guild account owner, then request an authorization from the staff. This account is considered as a linked account. It is prohibited to assume a semi-AFK type of gameplay on shared accounts.

{{Infobox Job |jobName=Gunslinger |jobBase=Novice |jobType=Extended |changesAt=[[Gunslinger Job Change Guide|Einbroch]] |skills=21 |skillPoints=69 |questSkills=0 |str=4|agi=5|vit=1|int=2|dex=13|luk=7}} ==Overview== [[Image: Gunslinger.jpg|thumb|left]] Gunslinger is all about guns. Gunslingers can be really expensive and generally not a good idea if you can't fund them with your other characters. Apparently the Gunslinger Class was inspired by character of Gunslinger from the book '''''The Dark Tower: The Gunslinger''''' by '''Stephen King''' (ISBN: 978-0-937986-50-9) and the 2002 movie '''Equilibrium''' (ISAN 0000-0001-1465-0000-8-0000-0000-D). Contrary to popular belief, familiarity with any of these is not required for playing Gunslinger to its full potential. ==Job Change Guide== See [[Gunslinger Job Change Guide]] for information. == Builds == All gunslinger builds benefit from high DEX for their atk, which makes it gunslingers main stat. === Desperado === '''Playstyle''' Surprisingly [[Desperado]] has somewhat similar play style to SVD Blacksmith. The basic strategy is to gather a mob, use [[Barrage]] to boost your dmg and burst the mob down with [[Desperado]], cancel [[Barrage]] with [[Run and Gun]], recast [[Flip Coin|coins]] and repeat. All that while hoping the mob dies before you do. Desperado can pair pretty well with [[Rapid Shower]] for finishing single enemies at range, but dedicated Rapid Shower build would probably need more INT. However even against one target Desperado can still do more damage that Rapid Shower. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |Stats | Main Desperado stat is DEX. Other stats should be some combination of mid INT for SP sustain, low STR for weight limit and rest in VIT. '''''DEX''''' Stat wise aim for 120 DEX unbuff with DEX gear and 110 DEX without DEX gear. '''''INT''''' Desperado is a skill based build, moderate INT investment is necessary in absence of other SP sustain. See the [[Gunslinger#SP Recovery|SP recovery]] section for more detail. It should be possible to build Desperado with low or no INT and instead use Earth Deleter Card for SP sustain, because Desperado is considered melee. However since Earth Deleter Card occupies armor slot, it prevents use of elemental armors which are required for enemies like Ancient Mummy or Teddy Bear. '''''STR''''' Some amount of STR is necessary for increasing weight limit which enables bringing more consumables and staying longer on maps. Each point of BASE STR is equal to 30 weight capacity. In my opinion going above 41 BASE STR is not worth the high stat point investment. '''''VIT''''' VIT is extremely important. Stun ressistance, HP item efficiency and MAX HP all help while mobbing. MAX HP also provides some space for bad luck with Hunter Fly proc. '''''AGI''''' Some people are experimenting with lowering STR and VIT in favor of adding AGI for FLEE. This might provide a smoother experience in some maps, but I believe the choice of viable maps for AGI builds is more limited than for VIT builds. '''''LUK''''' If you have enough leftover points get 3+7 LUK for +1 perfect dodge. |} {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |Gear | For party play basic DEX gear like Apple of Archer and Nimble Gloves is OK and in case you are gearing for maximum damage even preferable. This... Is my BOOMSTICK!'' Shotgun Gunslingers or "shotgunners" are gunslingers centered primarily around the shotgun-specific skills [[Full Buster]] and [[Spread Attack]], using them to decimate both monsters and primitive screwheads alike. Shotgunners are slow but hard hitting, easily capable of dealing more than 10,000 damage single hits and unsurpassed in their capacity for AoE physical damage. Though they have a decent variety in terms of good places to level/farm on their own, shotgunners tend to be party-oriented builds owing to their excellent ranged physical AoE damage. Like all GS builds, the most important stat for shotgunners is DEX. DEX shortens the cast time of some skills (most importantly [[Flip the Coin]]) and significantly increases ranged ATK. Shotgunners stack STR because [[Dust]] grants a passive effect converting each point of STR into +1 ATK while wielding shotguns. Ideally total STR should be in multiples of 5 as this grants an additional +1 ATK with ranged weapons. Often, shotgunners will aim for 80 base STR in order to capitalize on the Giant Whisper Card (+20 ATK if base STR >= 80). Both [[Full Buster]] and [[Spread Attack]] are very SP-intensive, and so shotgunners stack at least a moderate amount of INT. In a party with a priest granting [[Blessing]] and [[Magnificat]], 52 base INT is sufficient for maintaining SP at later levels (80+) providing they aren't the only damage dealers. With both a [[Priest]] and [[Dancer]] present, a shotgunner could conceivably get less INT and sustain their SP, but this would seriously hamper solo play and any party without a [[Dancer]] present. For those purely solo oriented, a shotgunner benefits from any additional amount of additional INT beyond 52 base (at the cost of STR) to reduce downtime. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |Build Playstyle | '''Solo'''
A shotgunner will level solo either one shotting things with [[Full Buster]] or gathering mobs and AoEing them down with [[Spread Attack]]. Though at max rank [[Full Buster]] costs a hefty amount of SP (45), rank 1 of the skill is actually incredibly SP-efficient (+47% dmg/SP) ranking third among all single target damage skills in that regard. Its 425% damage modifier with a potential 19-cell range is enough damage to one shot a fairly large number of targets, trivializing early leveling for shotgunners providing they've allocated their stats appropriately (See: [[Gunslinger#Gunslinger_Leveling]]). [[Full Buster]]'s SP-efficiency falls off the higher the rank that's used, but higher ranks can be used to one shot a given target if rank 1's modifier is insufficient (be sure to make use of the stat calculator [[Gunslinger#See_Also]]). For mobbing, [[Spread Attack]]'s high SP demands mean that until/unless you have very high INT, you can only dispatch very large mobs with it after having gathered monsters from across most of the map (Allowing time for your SP to recover). An example of a map where you can do this is is the Iron Fist map (Morroc Field 14). Aside from the mini boss which can be easily avoided, the map only has slower moving enemies with no ranged skills that can be safely mobbed and dispatched all at once ('''make sure you aren't infringing on anyone else in the map's ability to level by doing this'''). Rather than rely on [[Barrage]], the shotgunner should stagger [[Spread Attack]]s as they gain distance with [[Run and Gun]]. Otherwise the large damage-delay caused by the very low ASPD of shotguns might get them killed.

'''Party'''
Shotgunners are typically AoE damage dealers in parties. [[Spread Attack]] is used after getting within range of the tank's mob (9 + [[Snake Eyes]]/2 cells) and activating [[Barrage]]. A shotgunner should be wary when using [[Full Buster]] as its long aftercast delay might impede them shooting a mob that the tank brings or lead to them falling behind if they're stuck in [[Barrage]]'s slowdown ([[Gunslinger#On Run and Gun & Barrage]]). If a [[Bard]] with [[A Poem of Bragi]] is in the party, a shotgunner can use [[Full Buster]] more liberally (while being mindful of their SP). Even with a [[Priest]]'s buffs while within a party, shotgunners have to be careful when managing their SP. For example, if there are other damage dealers present, let them handle stray single enemies that wander too close to the party (or they can be slowed down with [[Wing Clip]] instead). If there is a [[Dancer]] in the party, the gunslinger can generally be pretty reckless with skill-spam without much concern for SP. If in a party or duo without a [[Bard]] where single targets are being killed rather than groups, the gunslinger can help preserve their SP by sitting in between [[Full Buster]]s while waiting for its long aftercast delay (3 seconds).

All gunslingers who carry a rifle over their shoulder bear this motto. The rifle gunslinger uses the extremely hard-hitting [[Tracking]] skill with its '''1600%''' damage modifier to mow down targets in a single trigger press. The [[Tracking]] skill is capable of critically hitting, allowing rifle gunslingers to take down even the sturdiest or most evasive of foes. A Rifle gunslinger can make for an efficient solo character or a highly capable MvP slayer. Rifle GS are typically built one of two ways: A regular rifle GS and an MvP rifle GS. Regular rifle GS use [[Tranq Shot]] to set up targets to be crit with [[Tracking]]. These GS are often built as hybrid grenadiers or shotgunners. MvP rifle GS are primarily group-oriented MvP builds that take aim at the boss while part of a duo or group with a [[Priest]] present to provide [[Gloria]] and [[Lex Aeterna]]. Rifle GS rely on [[Tranq Shot]] to put any target with low INT (<27) to [[Sleep]], doubling their chance to critically hit. Paired with armor piercing bullets and the rifle bonus, they only need an additional '''6.66%''' crit to always critically hit their targets. This can be achieved by getting 23 base LUK, one crit race card (E.g., Cruiser, Assaulter) slotted in their rifle, or from other equipment. Because of their low stat and skill requirements, a rifle GS can be built as either a hybrid grenadier or shotgunner. A hybrid shotgunner rifle GS will usually go for mid INT (~52 base) and 50-80 STR. Hybrid grenadiers, with their much higher SP requirements, will go as high as 90 base INT. All rifle GS (regardless of subtype) heavily prioritize DEX. MvP rifle GS aim to reach upwards of 100% crit ''without'' relying on [[Tranq Shot]] to put targets to sleep, and with [[Gloria]] active. Unlike regular rifle GS, they tend to go lower on INT (relying on [[Magnificat]]) and much higher on LUK in their build. Between [[Gloria]], 1% base crit, Armor Piercing Bullets, LUK from their job bonus and the Rifle bonus, MvP rifle GS have to account for the remaining '''46.33% crit''' from their LUK and equipment if they want guaranteed critical hits. How exactly the gunslinger goes about bridging this gap depends on equipment availability, but will almost certainly involve investing considerably more into LUK compared to other rifle builds. See the "Build Equips" section below for more information. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Build Playstyle | '''Solo'''

Grenadiers have access to the special [[Gunslinger#Grenades|Grenade]] ammunition, which allow their attacks to inflict a variety of special effects like [[Stun]], [[Movement Speed|Slow]], [[Blind]] or [[Ghost]] element damage. Similar to a shotgunner, a grenadier makes for either an excellent solo character or party-oriented build, with the added flexibility of their special ammo. Owing to the high cost of [[Ground Drift]], Grenadier GS differ from other builds in that they get very high base INT. Solo focused Grenadier will generally get upwards of 90 or more base INT, whereas a more party-focused grenade launcher GS could get get away with less INT (70+) as they'll have [[Magnificat]] and [[Blessing]] to help them sustain SP. Party focused grenadiers can invest a moderate amount of AGI to increase DPS, as once the cast time of [[Ground Drift]] is reduced below their ASPD delay (~1.4s with a Berserk Potion and 1 base AGI) then their attack speed becomes the limiting factor to their DPS instead. The base skill point requirements for [[Ground Drift]], its pre-requisites and essential gunslinger skills like [[Barrage]] and [[Run and Gun]] leaves a lot of room to become a hybrid. A high INT/DEX grenade launcher GS build makes for an excellent [[Rapid Shower]] spamming [[Revolver]] build, and could also hybrid as a rifle GS or a shotgunner. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Build Playstyle | '''Solo'''
[[Ground Drift]] has a fairly large SP cost, even at very high INT levels (90+) it cannot be sustained if used constantly. The most practical way to use it is on maps where you can gather large mobs to group up and AoE down all at once, allowing enough time for your SP to recover in between firing sessions. The higher the gunslinger's INT, the more frequently mobs can be dispatched and the less time needs to be spent gathering them. Grenade launcher gunslingers can make [[Ground Drift]] AoEing easier by using the [[Stun]], [[Movement Speed|Slow]] and [[Blind]] special grenades ([[Gunslinger#Grenades]]).

A grenadier can more easily use these skills to one shot targets, especially at lower levels when sustaining [[Ground Drift]] in any capacity is impractical.

Unlike when solo, a grenadier in a party can be more liberal with their use of [[Ground Drift]] to deal very high ranged AoE DPS thanks to [[Magnificat]] or a [[Dancer]]'s SP song. It should be noted that unlike a [[Hunter]]'s traps, [[Ground Drift]] can be launched directly on top of monsters. The grenadier stays in the back of the party while under [[Barrage]] and safely lobs [[Ground Drift]] attacks (with their up to 19 cell range) at mobs that the tank brings to the group, similar to a shotgunner. |} {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |Skill Overview | ''The following covers skills that may not be straight forward picks, and provides context to help aspiring grenadier make decisions regarding their build.''
