[[Barrage]] greatly increases damage and ASPD at the cost of halved movement speed, whereas [[Run and Gun]] grants a burst of speed (+20%) for 5 seconds and 2 minutes of bonus FLEE and ranged damage reduction. These two skills are mutually exclusive, meaning using one cancels out the other. This interaction is important, because while you will usually want to be in [[Barrage]] while dealing damage, your only means of removing the movement speed debuff when you need to move somewhere is via [[Run and Gun]]. As much as they can, gunslingers should avoid the sluggish movement of [[Barrage]]. The meagre zeny savings and reduced downtime from having to repeatedly recast [[Barrage]], [[Run and Gun]] and [[Flip the Coin]] is less than the downtime of moving at halved speed constantly. Gunslingers should become accustomed to alternating between these two skills as needed. ===Using the PSRO Stat Calculator=== The stat calculator is a useful tool for determining what is needed in terms of equipment or stats to one shot a given target, build planning, and more. The current PSRO stat calculator ([[Gunslinger#See_Also]]) has a number of inaccuracies regarding the job which makes using it as a gunslinger difficult. Thankfully, there are adjustments that can be made to account for these inaccuracies.
[[File:GunslingerStatCalc1.png|GunslingerStatCalc1.png|450px]]
* Job Bonuses: The +4 DEX/AGI bonus from Increase Accuracy has been added into the job bonus for gunslingers. To account for this in the calculator, add these bonuses to the "Player Stats" section of "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator when planning a JobLv70 gunslinger. * Clan Bonuses: The +2 stat bonus, and +40 MaxHP/10 MaxSP bonuses from joining a clan is not accounted for in the calculator. You can add these bonuses to the "Player Stats" section of "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator. * [[Barrage]]: This skill isn't correctly accounted for in the calculator. Add +20 to ASPD under "Player Sub-Stats" and +30 to "% ATK based damage on any target" under "Other" in the "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator. * [[Gatling Fever]]: This skill isn't correctly account for in the calculator. Add an additional +20 to ASPD under "Player Sub-Stats" and an additional +40 to "% ATK based damage on any target" under "Other" in the "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator ''when planning Gatling GS characters only.'' * Custom Bullets: Ammo isn't properly accounted for in the calculator. You can add the +% damage of ammo like Hollow-Point, Heavy Plated and Heavy Tipped bullets in the "+% ATK based Damage" section of the "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator to account for them. For Ghosthunter Grenades, change the attribute of the character's weapon from [[Neutral]] to [[Ghost]] in the weapon section. * Weapon Attack Values: Many gunslinger weapons have inaccurate attack values in the stat calculator and can be adjusted for as follows by adding +x ATK to the "ATK" section of the "Player Sub-Stats" section in the "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator: Thunder-P (+20), Rolling Stone (+15), Garrison (+20), Gold Lux (+60), Branch (+20). * [[Dust]]'s Bonus to [[Shotgun]] Attack: The calculator does not account for the passive effect and can be adjusted for by adding +x ATK (your character's total STR) to the "ATK" section of the "Player Sub-Stats" section in the "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator * Chain Action, Madness Canceller, Increase Accuracy, Adjustment, Gatling Fever: These effects are '''inaccurate/obselete''' in the calculator and '''should not be toggled on or used.''' * [[Single Action]], [[Flip the Coin]], [[Snake Eyes]]: These effects ''are'' working in the calculator and can be toggled on/used (except for the +2 HIT per skillLv of [[Single Action]] which can be manually added to the "Additional Enchants & Manual Edits on Player" tab of the calculator). The following active skills in the calculator have incorrect % modifiers: [[Triple Action]], [[Soul Bullet]], [[Desperado]], [[Tracking]], [[Dust]], [[Full Buster]], [[Spread Attack]], [[Ground Drift]]. They can be adjusted for (completely or at least partially) by taking the '''minimum damage of Basic Attack''' (under Player Attack Skills in the Monster Combat Simulator window) and '''mulitiplying its value''' as follows:
[[File:GunslingerStatCalc2.png|GunslingerStatCalc2.png|450px]]
* [[Triple Action]]: Multiply by 4.2 * [[Soul Bullet]]: Multiply by (50+Dex+BaseLvl)/100) x 3 times * [[Desperado]]: Multiply by 3 * [[Tracking]]: Multiply by 16 * [[Dust]]: Multiply by 4 * [[Full Buster]]: Multiply by 11 * [[Spread Attack]]: Multiply by 4 * [[Ground Drift]]: Multiply by 8 (single target), multiply by 4 (AoE) ''The above values are for the max rank of the respective skill, and should be adjusted for if using lower ranks (See their respective skill pages for % values).''' ==Gunslinger Rework== ''Gunslinger on Payon Stories was drastically reworked, for more information please refer to the [https://discord.com/channels/1051580563624042547/1051693161132605520/1345652041103441942 Gunslinger Release Patch Notes] posted on Payon Stories Discord.'' ===Custom Skill Tree=== The gunslinger skill tree has been heavily altered. Gunslinger Job Change Guide:
To become [[gunslinger]] you will need job level 10 novice.

With that out of the way, you will need to get to Gunslinger Guild in Einbroch, either by getting warp from an acolyte or by Airship from Yuno Airport (yuno, 53, 208), be sure to chose domestic flight.

[[File:Yuno Airport.png|frameless]]

[[File:Yuno Airport Inside.png|frameless]]

In Einbroch, head to the Gunslinger Guild (a bit east from airport... einbroch 131, 199) and speak with Master Miller inside.

[[File:Einbroch gunslinger.png|frameless]]

[[File:Master Miller.png|frameless]]

You will be asked to find Wise Bull Horn in Payon (payon 142, 51)

''Note: You cannot use Butterfly Wings in Einbroch, but if you log out inside the Gunslinger guild you will be at your save location when you log back in.''

[[File:Wise Bull.png|frameless]]

Wise Bull Horn will require you to bring the following items:

* 1x Trunk (1019)
* 3x Fluff (914)
* 3x Zargon (912)
* 10x Shell (935)
* 3x Green Herb (511)
* 3x Rainbow Shell (1013)

After you bring him required items, he will ask you for Milk (519).

When you bring him milk, he will send you back to Master Miller in Einbroch to complete your job change.

You will be able to chose one of three weapons as a part of your job change:

* Rifle - Branch[3] (91019) 
* Pistol - Six Shooter[3] (13100)
* Shotgun - Thunder P[3] (13169)

== General ==
HP recovery happens every 2 seconds while sitting and every 4 seconds while standing. Characters with [[HP Recovery While Moving]] also regen HP every 12 seconds while walking. 

See also: [[Increase HP Recovery]], [[Spiritual Cadence]], [[Song of Lutie]] 

== Calculations ==
 var HPR = Math.max( 1, Math.floor(MAX_HP / 200) );
 HPR += Math.floor( VIT / 5 );
 HPR = Math.floor( HPR * (1 + HPR_MOD * 0.01) );

HPR_MOD : Sum of modifiers

Base value of 1 per 200 HP, minimum 1. Then +1 for every 5 [[VIT]]. Finally increase by modifiers.

Halloween Event 2025:
== Mimi's Sweet Tooth - The Candy Hunt Begins! == [[File:Mimi.jpg|border|center|frameless|800x800px]] A mysterious figure has appeared in Payon, ''Mimi, the Ancient Mimic''. Mimi asks players to gather various types of candy scattered across the land. In return, she grants a special item that provides a buff. Turning in different candies upgrades different attributes of that buff. === How it works === * Candy is obtained from drops and from Candy Thieves summoned with Decoy Candy. * Mimi offers daily kill quests that reward Decoy Candy, which summons Candy Thieves for 2 minutes and are owned by the summoner to avoid kill-stealing. * Candy is turn-in limited per account/type. === Rewards === * '''Costumes''': Candy Cane in Mouth Costume, Skull Hood === Candies and Effects === {| border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; text-align:center; width:100%;" ! They have low combat stats and cannot be stolen from. * Candy Thieves can drop: Candy Bag, individual Candies, and Costumes. === Useful Commands === * @mimi — Displays player’s current Mimi Buff values and limits. * @mimilist — Displays the list of enemies that drop Candy Bags.' === Mimi's Kill Quest: ===
''Mimi offers a set of daily kill quests that can each be completed and submitted once per day. Players may return the next day to submit the same quests again.''
== The Antique Dealer == [[File:Antique Dealer.png|thumb|Antique Dealer]] The wandering '''Antiques Dealer''' is back in town with a fresh selection of rare costumes and this time, he’s got a bit of a sweet tooth! 🍬 He's looking for some candies in exchange for his precious antiques. Bring him what he craves, and you might just walk away with one of these exclusive treasures: * Costume: Red Glasses * Costume: Mask of Nero * Costume: Ghostly Tophat * Costume: Cat Doll Bag '''Important:''' * You can claim only one costume per account. * All costumes are account-bound and non-tradable. == Event Notes == * Candy turn-ins are account bound and subject to the stated turn-in limits per candy type. * Make sure to include your party or guild rules on loot sharing when running Candy Thieves to avoid confusion.

==Overview==
[[Image:Hunter_art.jpg|thumb|right]]

Hunters build on their experience as Archers shooting a bow and arrows with new tools and techniques, to kill prey from a distance more efficiently and effectively. Each Hunter can train a falcon to assist them. Their falcon can strike multiple monsters at once, reveal concealed enemies, and destroy enemy traps. Hunters can also expertly lay a wide variety of traps and mines. These can destroy enemies outright, debilitate them to reduce their threat, or prevent them from approaching, to be shot full of arrows.

==Jobchange Guide==
''See [[Hunter Job Change Guide]] for detailed information.''

Changing into a [[Hunter]] from an [[Archer]] requires the player to complete a number of tasks:

*Item Collection
*Written Test
*Battle Test

After completing these tests, the player will be transformed into a Hunter.

== Build Ideas ==

=== Double Strafe (DS) ===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 90+
* VIT: 1
* INT: 9+
* DEX: 90+
* LUK: 1
Aim for 99/99/9 AGI/DEX/INT to output tremendous single-target DPS against MVPs. A downside of this build is the low INT; [[Double Strafe]] spam is very SP hungry. While a Hunter deals superior DPS, Bard outperforms at longevity.

=== Auto Blitz Beat (ABB) ===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 90+
* VIT: 1
* INT: 1+
* DEX: 20-86
* LUK: 43-95
As the name suggests, the build aims to trigger [[Blitz Beat]] from auto-attacks as much as possible. This is a great starting character as it doesn't require expensive equipment to work. AGI is typically maxed out due to [[ASPD]]'s hyperbolic scaling. For DEX and LUK, balance them by how much single- or multi-target damage you want to deal. Since we have to auto-attack anyway, the arrows might as well do something. 59/75 is a good baseline, then shift DEX in x9 multiples so it ends up on x10s after [[Improve Concentration]]. DEX also contributes to ASPD 1/4 as much as AGI. Hunters on higher budgets also benefit from high crit chances.

1. Talk to the '''Hunter Guildsman''', "''Hunter Reggie''" in Payon Field 10 ''(pay_fild10 148, 251)'' (which is situated 2 maps east, and 1 south of Payon) to go to the Hunter Guild. Talk with the '''Hunter Guildswoman''', "''Sherin''" and apply to become a [[hunter]].

Sherin tells you that candidates are required to pass three tests before they can become a hunter.

2. The first test is a '''personality assessment'''. The following are the answers to the test:
::*Wander around alone and search for a place.
::*Walk with a friend.
::*Hunt at a nearby field.
::*Go back to town.
::*Would it be possible to get a heal, please?
::*Open a chat room and wait.
::*Tell the person about a good place to hunt.
::*Guide them to their destination.
::*Watch, then attack when asked for help.
::*Try to find the owner.

3. Talk with the '''Guild Receptionist''', "''Demon Hunter''" on the left, ''(in_hunter 64, 100)'' who tells you that the second test consists of '''gathering items''' to make arrows. Gather the items he requests, then talk with him again.

4. Talk to the Demon Hunter again, he will then send you to Payon.
*'''Tip''': Bring enough healing items to recover all of your HP at least once for the final test.

[[Image:HunterJobChange0.png|400px|]]

5. Go to the building in Payon situated to the '''west of the central castle''' ''(oldnewpayon 63, 180)''.

6. When inside the building, '''go to the room''' just above the Mystic Lady NPC at ''(payon_in01 30, 150)'', then talk with the '''Hunter''' NPC and ask to take the final test.

The guild member will give you 200 Silver Arrows and transfer you to a waiting room. Walk forward and the examiner will explain the test to you.

The test area is a maze populated with Porings, Zombies, Archer Skeletons, and Mummies, and scattered with puddles of water. You are required to complete three objectives in order and within 3 minutes to pass the test:

::1. Kill any 4 of the monsters labelled "'''Job Change Monster'''".
::2. Open the exit by activating a switch.
::3. Exit the maze.

All of the monsters will die once the required number of target monsters have been killed.

The six target monsters are comprised of:
::*1 Poring, located in the north.
::*3 Zombies, each located in the east, west, and center respectively.
::*1 Archer Skeleton, located in the east.
::*1 Mummy, located in the south-west.

The switch is located at the center of the maze, and can be activated by clicking it. The exit is located in the north.
*'''Tip''': You can activate the switch from a distance; you don't need to stand next to it.
You will fail the test if any of the following happens:
::*You kill any monster that is not labelled "Job Change Monster".
::*You walk in any of the puddles of water.
::*You fail to complete the objectives within the allocated time.
::*You are killed.

When you are ready to begin the test, enter the receptionist's chat room and wait until you are transferred to the test area.

7. You are awarded a [[Image:1007.png]] [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=1007 Necklace of Wisdom] as proof of passing the final test.

8. Return to the Hunter Guild at Payon Field 10 ''(pay_fild10 148, 251)''. Give the Necklace of Wisdom to ''Sherin'' ''(in_hunter 100, 99)'' and she will make you a [[hunter]].
*'''Tip''': Before leaving the area, exit the Hunter Guild and kill enough monsters to learn [[Falconry Mastery]], then return to the Hunter Guild and rent a falcon from the '''Falcon Master''' in the right wing of the building ''(in_hunter 146, 99)''.

Ice Wall:
{{Skill Info | class = Wizard | class2 = | class3 = | type = Active | levels = 10 (Fixed) | prereqs = ([[Mage]]) [[Frost Diver]] Lv. 1, [[Stone Curse]] Lv. 1 | quest = | spcost = 20 | hpcost = | time = None | delay = ASPD | duration = (Skill Level Durability/50) seconds
Or until broken | target = Ground | range = 9 | area = 1x5 | knock = | element = | status = | catalyst = | cf_name = | cf_value = }} == Description == Summon a wall of ice in a row 5 cells long on the targeted cell. Ice wall lasts as long as its durability is above 0. Its starting durability depends on the skill level used, can be decreased by attack damage and decreases by 50 each second. Ice Wall has a maximum duration of 5 * SkillLvl seconds, or its durability/50 seconds, whichever is lower. An unlimited number of Ice Walls can be summoned, restricted only by their durability. {|class="wikitable" !Skill Level !! Durability !! Duration |- !1 |400 |5 seconds |- !2 |600 |10 seconds |- !3 |800 |15 seconds |- !4 |1000 |20 seconds |- !5 |1200 |24 seconds |- !6 |1400 |28 seconds |- !7 |1600 |32 seconds |- !8 |1800 |36 seconds |- !9 |2000 |40 seconds |- !10 |2200 |44 seconds |} == Notes == *Ice Wall can be used to immobilize monsters traveling from West to East and from South to North (using the mini-map as a reference). The easiest way to pull this off is to have an Ice Wall placed right on the ground tile the monster is currently walking on. A single Ice Wall is enough to immobilize a monster, but a second Ice Wall must be placed adjacent to and behind the first to effectively trap the monster and prevent it from escaping and attacking other players. Placing the second Ice Wall is also useful to cancel the knockback effect of [[Jupitel Thunder]] and [[Storm Gust]]. *A seemingly unlimited number of monsters can be trapped within the same Ice Wall. When multiple monsters are following the player, placing an Ice Wall to immobilize the first monster in line usually results in the other monsters following right into the wall and getting immobilized too. *''See [[Wizard#Ice_Wall_Trapping]] for a visual demonstration of the above.'' *When a monster is trapped by Ice Wall it is still vulnerable to targeted skills and physical attacks. A player standing in front of and 1 cell away from the Ice Wall will be able to attack the monster and completely avoid being hit by it if the monster's attack range is no greater than 1 cell. *Because cells affected by Ice Wall become "snipeable wall" type, AoE skills used ''after'' ice walls are in place do not directly hit those cells. Although several skills--most notably (but not limited to) [[Storm Gust]], [[Meteor Storm]] and [[Lord of Vermilion]]--sometimes appear to hit monsters in ice wall. This is a result of splash damage to adjacent non-walled cells and not any other special property of these skills. Note that casting Ice Wall on a cell after an AoE has already been used on it does not stop the AoE's effect; Ice Wall must be cast before the AoE in order to have any protective use. *Monsters with [[Teleport]] usually activate it a few moments after getting hit if they are trapped by Ice Wall. Some monsters may not teleport if the player is standing within their casting range. *Players don't get immobilized by Ice Wall unless they are completely surrounded by it. A player or monster surrounded by a 3x3 cell area of Ice Wall is still vulnerable to targeted skills and ranged attacks, but is no longer vulnerable to AoE skills including [[Storm Gust]], [[Meteor Storm]], and [[Lord of Vermillion]]. *The Ice Wall is [[Neutral]] element and can be damaged by normal attacks (melee or ranged), targeted skills, and [[Sightrasher]]. Skills and weapons with splash-damage effect like [[Hunter]]'s [[Blitz Beat]]) will damage the surrounding Ice Wall even when targeting trapped players or monsters within it. *Ice Wall is disabled in [[WoE|War of Emperium]] mode but it does work in [[PvP]]. *Ice Wall is also disabled in Endless Tower. {{Navbox Wizard}}

Insect:
Insect are a race of monster. Notably they are one of the two races to ignore all [[Hiding]] related skills, which include [[Cloaking]], [[Tunnel Drive]], [[Shadow Jump]], and [[Hiding]] itself. Some examples of Insect monsters are Hunter Fly, Argiope and Mantis.

Cards which concern the insect race include:
* '''Bigfoot Card''': Reduce damage from Insect monsters by 30%.
* '''Bloody Murderer Card''': Inflict 10% more damage with Critical Attack. Critical +7 on Insect monsters.
* '''Caramel Card''': Increase damage on Insect monsters by 20%.
* '''Galapago Card''': Add the chance of gaining 'Apple Juice'/'Banana Juice'/'Carrot Juice' each time an Insect monster is killed. Juice item restores 50% more [[HP]].
* '''Gargoyle Card''': Add the chance of gaining 'Box of Thunder' item each time an Insect monster is killed.
* '''Giant Hornet Card''': Add the chance of gaining 'Wind of Verdure' item each time an Insect monster is killed. Add 10% more tolerance against [[Wind]] Property Attack.
* '''Gig Card''': Gain 5 [[SP]] each time an Insect monster is killed by Physical Melee Attack. Drain 5 [[SP]] as the weapon is unequipped. Increase damage on Insect monsters by 4%.
* '''Skeleton General Card''': Receive 10% more Experience Points from Insect monsters. Receive 20% more damage from Insect monsters.

Equipment concerning the Insect race are:
* '''Cigarette''': Reduces damage from Insect monster by 3%.
* '''Pipe''': Reduces damage from Insect monster by 3%.
* '''Sunflower''': Reduces damage from Insect monster by 10%.

Skills concerning the Insect race include:
* '''[[Beast Bane]]''': [[Hunter]] skill that increases [[ATK]] against the [[Brute]] and Insect races.

== Description ==
Consumes 1 Spirit Sphere per cast. Inflicted damage increases in proportion with the enemy's VIT DEF and Armor DEF. Investigate is always of the [[Neutral]] element regardless of an equipped weapon's elemental attribute. Investigate cannot miss due to an enemy's Flee or Perfect Dodge. 

Investigate refunds 1 [[Spirit Sphere]] if it kills a target.

== Damage ==
The formula for Investigate is believed to be derived from a normal attack's damage (before taking into account elemental advantages), multiplied by the skill ATK boost (from the table above) and an adjustment multiplier.

*Adjustment = (EnemyDEF + EnemyVIT) / 100 

The final damage dealt is not reduced by an enemy's [[DEF]] or [[VIT]] DEF as a normal skill attack would be, but it is, however, reduced by other reductions such as Thara Frog Card or Poo Poo Hat.

== Notes ==
* Casting Call Spirits immediately after Investigate will cancel the after-cast delay (since this is actually an animation delay). Doing this before casting Investigate again is actually faster than repeatedly using Investigate (and not bypassing the delay) at 115+ DEX, as long as no [[A Poem of Bragi]] are present. 
* Causing your character to perform any other animation than occult's normal animation, such as taking a step during it's delay will cancel the delay that normally follows the skill's usage. 
*If the enemy's combined DEF is 0 or less, Investigate will miss. 
*If your weapon has an elemental attribute, then, due to a bug in the way damage is calculated, your damage will be affected by GARMENT-based reductions of an opponent.

== About Izlude ==
Also known as the Satellite City of [[Prontera]]. Izlude is home to the [[Swordsman]] association.

== Story ==
The place where those who wish to become Swordmen gather to train. There is a ferry which takes you to [[Alberta]], and an express ship which takes adventurers to the underwater dungeons, Byalan Island. King Tristan III built the Izlude Arena to promote professionals throughout the nation. ==Dungeon==

=== Undersea Dungeon ===
Known as Byalan Dungeon. A dungeon found in Byalan Island that is filled with low to mid level monsters.
Most monsters here are of Water Property so Wind Elemental weapons are very useful for leveling.
Most low level melee class characters train in this dungeon. Mostly, [[Swordsman]] and [[Merchant]] type characters usually seen [[Bash]]ing Vadons and Marinas.
While the first two levels of the dungeon is safe for a low level characters, the 3rd level needs a caution.
It is home for the Obeaune and Marse monsters. Obeaunes are aggresive mermaid like monsters fond of casting 
[[Lex Divina]] while hitting the target hard. Marse can blind the target and his attack can leave an unwary [[Merchant]] dead. Mid level characters usually train in the 3rd level of the dungeon. 
Moving on to the next level are infested with fish like monsters. Watch out for the incoming Water Ball of the Swordfish! Marc, a sea horse like monster hits really hard and can stun it's target immobile while receiving a lot of damage from a huge mob of monsters. Usually leaving a [[Knight]] kissing the seafloor. 
Stay away from the exploding Marine Spheres as much as possible.
Finally the last level, Mermans are deadly but gives a decent amount of experience. Penomenas are like Archers attacking from afar while dealing a lots of damage. Strouf keeps on casting [[Frost Diver]] and [[Lightning Bolt]] combo on you.
And the green fish like monster called Deviace is considered as Mini Boss of the dungeon can be found in here.
His [[Water Ball]] can bring a full HP Knight down in just a matter of seconds. Either way, the dungeon is a great place for some levels if you are melee type character but just remember to be cautious and bring a lot of Potions and Fly Wings with you.   

*To get to Byalan Island talk to the Sailor (201,181). He will charge you 150z.
*You can not save on Byalan Island but there is a Kafra Employee for storage and cart rental.
*To reach the dungeon, go north around the eye of the skull and then go south to reach the entrance.

=About Juno=
Juno is the floating city, high in the clouds. It is also the location of the Sage Headquarters. 

=== Story===
The capital of [[Republic of Schwartzvald]]. Located in the air above El Mes Plateau, Juno is a floating city with three islands – the glorious island Solomon, island of intelligence Sonotora, island of prosperity Mineta. The `Heart of Ymir` is what allows this land to exist. Many come to research the strange powers and ancient civilization. Juno is called the `City of the Wise One` for this reason. Juno is located above the El Mes Plateau, which is north of [[Al De Baran]]. Currently, the airship which used to provide transportation between [[Izlude]] and [[Juno]] is operating, so adventurers that wish to go to this land no longer have to climb through the rough land of the El Mes Plateau.

Knight:
{{Infobox Job |jobType=2-1 |jobBase=Swordman |jobLevel=50 |changesAt=Prontera Chivarly |skills=10 |skillPoints=76 |questSkills=1 |str=8 |agi=2 |vit=10 |int=0 |dex=6 |luk=4}} == Overview == The Knight class is the primary second job for the Swordman class. Being a hack and slash type of character, Knights are granted access to a new mastery that will open a new type of weapon to wield aside from the Swordman's swords. They are also allowed to acquire powerful AoE skills like the famed Bowling Bash and the spear exclusive skill, Brandish Spear. == Job Change Guide == 1. Go inside the Chivalry located in the northwest corner of Prontera (prontera 35, 346). This is also known as the Knight Guild. 2. Inside, speak to the Chivalry Captain (prt_in 88, 101) standing behind a desk to apply for the quest. * '''Note''': Avoid the Recruiter; signing up for his mission transports the player to the Culverts, one map west of Prontera. 3. Speak to Sir Andrew (prt_in 75, 107), located close to the entrance. He will randomly assign a list of items to collect: * '''Note''': Players who are Job Level 50 may skip this step. {| class="wikitable" !Set !Items |- |Set 1 |5 Bug Leg, 5 Clam Flesh, 5 Maneater Blossom, 5 Old Frying Pan, 5 Snail's Shell, 5 Heart of Mermaid |- |Set 2 |5 Elder Pixie's Moustache, 5 Orcish Voucher, 5 Mane, 5 Moth Dust, 5 Reptile Tongue, 5 Wing of Red Bat |} 4. Speak to Sir Siracuse (prt_in 71, 91), found at the south end of the room by the table. He asks questions pertaining to the Knight class. If you fail it the first time, speak to him again to re-take it. Quiz Answers: * Question 1 - Weapon unaffected by Twohand Quicken is '''Flamberge''' * Question 2 - Skill not required for Bowling Bash is '''Provoke Level 10''' * Question 3 - Option not necessary for Brandish Spear is '''Spear Boomerang''' * Question 4 - Weapon that can attack a Nightmare monster is '''Zephyrus''' * Question 5 - The correct amount is '''80%''' * Question 6 - You should tell the novice about a '''hunting area''' * Question 7 - In the front of a battle you should '''protect everyone''' * Question 8 - The most important value of a Knight is '''honor''' 5. Speak to Sir Windsor (prt_in 79, 94), near the middle of the room who will warp the player to a waiting room. Enter the chat room found here you will be transported to the first stage of the Battle Test if no one else is in line; otherwise, wait inside the chat room for others to finish the test. There are three rounds of fighting monsters. In each stage, different monsters will spawn. All monsters must be killed within the amount of time allocated (there will be announcements indicating the time remaining). Remember to check all the corners of the room for monsters that could have been missed. If you fail, restock on necessary items, restore your HP/SP, and talk to Sir Windsor again to retake the test. Before beginning this test, ensure you are fully prepared: * Full HP/SP * HP Potions ** There will '''not''' be time to sit and regen HP during the test because of the time limit. ** Especially recommended for those under level 60. 15 Orange/White Potions is ideal, but a large stock of Meat or the like will suffice. * Green Potions * Awakening Potions (Lvl 40+) / Concentration Potions * SP Restoring Items Many of the monsters in round 1 are weak to Fire, while some monsters in round 2 are weak to Water. Fire and Water endowed weapons can be used here. {| class="wikitable" !Round !Monsters !Tips |- |Round 1 |2 Andre, 2 Argos, 2 Deniro, 2 Dustiness, 2 Piere |A Fire elemental weapon is useful for this stage. The Argos are aggressive, so kill them first. Using Bash on them is viable, but use melee attacks on the "ants" to conserve SP for stages 2 and 3. The ants ( Andre, Deniro, Piere) will draw near to loot items but are not naturally aggressive. The Dustiness may require Bash to be hit for low level Swordman with little DEX. |- |Round 2 |2 Anacondaq, 2 Desert Wolf, 4 Drainliar, 2 Frilldora |A Water elemental weapon can help kill the Desert Wolves or Frilldoras. Try running to a corner to avoid being mobbed by all of the monsters in the room. Kill the Desert Wolves quickly, as they are aggressive and do the most damage. The second priority monsters are any attacking Drainliar. Then kill all remaining monsters in the room one by one. Remember to use a Green Potion if inflicted by the Blind status. 3 minutes are given to complete this round. |- |Round 3 |6 Goblin (assorted types), 1 Steamrider |Do not use an elemental weapon, as all the Goblins have a different element. Immediately run to a corner to avoid getting mobbed by the entire room. Players who are Job Level 50 do not receive any extra items. == Builds == === SVD/MVP === * STR: 110-120 * AGI: 40 * VIT: 80 * INT: 1-30 * DEX: 45-60 * LUK: 1 Weapon: Elemental or Carded One or Two-Handed Spears The main build for a knight. Their damage output is high while maintaining decent VIT, allowing them to excel at MvPing or PvP. The typical SVD knight will level primarily on Large sized monsters utilizing pierce or they will make use of Bowling Bash or Brandish Spear for mobbing. Strength should be 100 at a minimum, most knights typically get around 120. This allows knights to be able to gain 1-hit-KO against High Orcs and possibly Minorous. Intelligence is a variable stat, and general consensus seems to be that at least 12 points in it is necessary. If the player is able to gain 1-hit-KOs while using an Earth Deleter Card, no intelligence may be needed. Agility is not for defence and should only be gotten for the purpose of using Pierce at a faster rate. === AGI Two-Hand Sword === * STR: 90-100 * AGI: 80-99 * VIT: 10-30+ * INT: 1 * DEX: 40-60 * LUK: 1-10 Weapons: Elemental Two Handed Swords or Carded Two Handed Swords AGI Knights believe that the best way to decrease damage is to prevent it from ever happening. They have high ASPD and flee, but vitality, and by extention health, are low compared to other Knights. Additionally, using two-handed swords pushes their attack power higher than most VIT Knights. Their main method of attack is Twohand Quicken, which increases ASPD by 30%. When faced with multiple foes, they break out Bowling Bash. Finally, Counter Attack allows for a higher critical chance against evasive or fortified foes. === Hybrid === * STR: 70-90 * AGI: 60-90 * VIT: 60-90 * INT: 1 * DEX: 40-50 * LUK: 1 Weapon: Elemental or Carded Spears or Two Handed Swords These knights try to get the best of both realms. By having a good chemistry of AGI and VIT depending on the user's playing style, they gain survivability in some areas while losing it in others. Hybrids are denoted by which stat is the highest. AGI-VIT Knights usually stick with a setup similar to an AGI knight. VIT-AGI Knights, likewise, generally stay with the setup of a VIT Knight. Ranking by efficiency, players tend to use AGI-VIT combination because of its higher ASPD which allows players to do Pierce chaining or if not solo with Twohand Quicken with a decent ASPD. This build was the best for pre-Transcendent patch Knight dueling. === VIT/WOE === * STR: 80+ * AGI: 1-20+ * VIT: 90-100 * INT: 1-12 * DEX: 40 * LUK: 1 Weapon: Elemental or Carded One or Two-Handed Spears VIT Knights are good tanks in Ragnarok Online. They have the highest health and good defense rate, and unlike agility Knights, they usually use shields for added defense and Spear type weaponry. Levels mostly by mobbing, utilizing their tanking ability. However, Crusaders are the main tankers due to their skill 'devotion'. === AGI-Crit === * STR: 70-80+ * AGI: 70-90+ * VIT: 1-30 * INT: 1 * DEX: 1-20 * LUK: 30+ Weapon: Carded or elemental Two Handed Swords The AGI-Critical aka AGI-LUK Knight is essentially a knight with crit-sin stats. The advantages to this are obvious, Knights have more health than assassins, a passive health regeneration, and are also capable of attaining higher attack speeds. However, despite the increased crit rate with the skill Two-hand Quicken (only on Oath), this will not be able to match the critical rate of an Assassin, and will have significantly less flee. == Class Data == === Payon Stories Balance Changes === * '''Twohand Quicken''': Now also increases FLEE by 1 per skill level and CRIT by 0.8% per skill level. * '''Bowling Bash''': Damage is set at 400% at the maximum level and the skill hits twice, allowing damage up to 800% per instance of Bowling Bash. Knight Job Change Guide:
1. Go inside the Chivalry located in the northwest corner of Prontera (prontera 35, 346). This is also known as the Knight Guild.

2. Inside, speak to the Chivalry Captain (prt_in 88, 101) standing behind a desk to apply for the quest.

* '''Note''': Avoid the Recruiter; signing up for his mission transports the player to the Culverts, one map west of Prontera.

3. Speak to Sir Andrew (prt_in 75, 107), located close to the entrance. He will randomly assign a list of items to collect:

* '''Note''': Players who are Job Level 50 may skip this step.

{| class="wikitable"
!Set
!Items
|-
|Set 1
|5 Bug Leg, 5 Clam Flesh, 5 Maneater Blossom, 5 Old Frying Pan, 5 Snail's Shell, 5 Heart of Mermaid
|-
|Set 2
|5 Elder Pixie's Moustache, 5 Orcish Voucher, 5 Mane, 5 Moth Dust, 5 Reptile Tongue, 5 Wing of Red Bat
|}
4. Speak to Sir Siracuse (prt_in 71, 91), found at the south end of the room by the table. He asks questions pertaining to the Knight class. If you fail it the first time, speak to him again to re-take it.

Quiz Answers:

* Question 1 - Weapon unaffected by Twohand Quicken is '''Flamberge'''
* Question 2 - Skill not required for Bowling Bash is '''Provoke Level 10'''
* Question 3 - Option not necessary for Brandish Spear is '''Spear Boomerang'''
* Question 4 - Weapon that can attack a Nightmare monster is '''Zephyrus'''
* Question 5 - The correct amount is '''80%'''
* Question 6 - You should tell the novice about a '''hunting area'''
* Question 7 - In the front of a battle you should '''protect everyone'''
* Question 8 - The most important value of a Knight is '''honor'''

5. Speak to Sir Windsor (prt_in 79, 94), near the middle of the room who will warp the player to a waiting room. Enter the chat room found here you will be transported to the first stage of the Battle Test if no one else is in line; otherwise, wait inside the chat room for others to finish the test.

There are three rounds of fighting monsters. In each stage, different monsters will spawn. All monsters must be killed within the amount of time allocated (there will be announcements indicating the time remaining). Remember to check all the corners of the room for monsters that could have been missed. If you fail, restock on necessary items, restore your HP/SP, and talk to Sir Windsor again to retake the test.

Before beginning this test, ensure you are fully prepared:

* Full HP/SP
* HP Potions
** There will '''not''' be time to sit and regen HP during the test because of the time limit.
** Especially recommended for those under level 60. 15 Orange/White Potions is ideal, but a large stock of Meat or the like will suffice.
* Green Potions
* Awakening Potions (Lvl 40+) / Concentration Potions
* SP Restoring Items

Many of the monsters in round 1 are weak to Fire, while some monsters in round 2 are weak to Water. Fire and Water endowed weapons can be used here.
{| class="wikitable"

!Tips

|A Fire elemental weapon is useful for this stage. The Argos are aggressive, so kill them first. Using Bash on them is viable, but use melee attacks on the "ants" to conserve SP for stages 2 and 3. The ants ( Andre, Deniro, Piere) will draw near to loot items but are not naturally aggressive. The Dustiness may require Bash to be hit for low level Swordman with little DEX.
|-
|Round 2
|2 Anacondaq, 2 Desert Wolf, 4 Drainliar, 2 Frilldora
|A Water elemental weapon can help kill the Desert Wolves or Frilldoras. Try running to a corner to avoid being mobbed by all of the monsters in the room. Kill the Desert Wolves quickly, as they are aggressive and do the most damage. The second priority monsters are any attacking Drainliar. Then kill all remaining monsters in the room one by one. Remember to use a Green Potion if inflicted by the Blind status. 3 minutes are given to complete this round.
|-
|Round 3
|6 Goblin (assorted types), 1 Steamrider
|Do not use an elemental weapon, as all the Goblins have a different element. Immediately run to a corner to avoid getting mobbed by the entire room. First kill the Goblins attacking that are in range (do not run halfway across the map to kill the archer), save the Steamrider; if using Bash or Magnum Break on the Goblins, ensure that there will be enough SP to Bash the Steam Goblin at least 3-5 times at the end. Once all the normal Goblins are killed, Bash the Steam Goblin to death, or whenever it is not stunned. Additionally, make sure you are not at low HP when fighting the Steamrider as it self destructs. Once all the monsters in Round 3 are dead, the player will be transported back to the Chivalry.
|}

== Description ==

The target will take double damage from the next real damage source of any kind. Healing, misses, status effects and [[Shield Reflect]] do not trigger the effect.

== Information ==
Lex Aeterna is removed if the proceeding attack is blocked by [[Guard]], [[Parry]], or [[Kaupe]], even if no damage was received. 
Cannot be cast on a [[Status_Effects#Frozen|Frozen]] or [[Status_Effects#Stone|Stoned]] target. It can however be cast during the first stage of [[Stone Curse]], before the target becomes [[Status_Effects#Stone|Stoned]].

The skill can be used on silenced party members by holding Shift and targetting a party member as you would an enemy.

=About Lutie=

Lutie is the Christmas town of Ragnarok. NPCs such as Santa and a snowman can be found here, along with winter/Christmas themed monsters and buildings. The entrance to the dungeon can be found in Lutie. To get to Lutie, talk to the Santa NPC at the top right building in [[Al De Baran]]. He will teleport you for free to the field outside of Lutie. The portal at the top of this field leads to the town. 

=== Story===
Lutie was discovered not long ago by a lone adventurer that wandered into an endless land of snow, and stumbled upon this village. For centuries the residents of Lutie have isolated themselves, gathering all they needed from hunting around their small village. Along with hunting, the residents of Lutie work everyday in the Lutie toy factory. Visitors to Lutie have often commented on the singing and soft thump of hammers as the workers cheerfully build toys of every shapes and sizes. Recently, an evil man, Antonio, who was bitter when he lost the election for town mayor, stole all the toys from the factory. Citizens of Lutie, who worked to bring joy to the children, became desperate and contacted the [[Kafra]] Corp who was happy to help and made it possible for Lutie to bring toys to the happy children across the world. Lutie, which can be reached with a Kafra's assistance, has a landscape which can be seen nowhere else.

=== Santa Claus ===
Santa Claus NPC is located in Santa Claus' Home. Off holiday season, he is just a background NPC that introduces himself, then tells you how you can leave Lutie for Al De Baran. During the holiday season, he serves as a trade NPC. He tells you the dilemma that he and his Santa army face against the Antonios, rogue Santas, that have cut holes in children's stockings. His request is that you vanquish them and he will reward you. For proof of your defeat over some Antonios, he will give you 1 Gift Box for 3 Red Stocking with Hole (?forgotname). The first time you talk to him during holiday season, he will give you a small Christmas gift as well, which could be cake, candy, candy canes, etc.

=== Toy Factory === 
A colorful dungeon filled with Christmas-themed foes such as Cookies, who resemble elves, and sentient Gift Boxes. 
It is notable for having messages on the map, such as "I <3(love) U". The dungeon is located at the very northern part of Lutie and spans 2 maps. It is also home for the MVP Boss: Stormy Knight.

==Overview==

[[Image: Mage.jpeg|thumb|left]]

''Mind over matter''. Mages champion this age old dictum, relying on their intellect to outwit their foes and devastate them with magical prowess rather than weaponry. 

Mages exploit the elemental weaknesses of enemies, devastating [[Earth]], [[Water]], [[Fire]], [[Undead]] and [[Ghost]] monsters with their slow but powerful bolt spells. Despite their physical weakness, mages are perfectly capable of defending themselves. [[Fire Wall]], [[Frost Diver]] and [[Energy Coat]] are spells that any quick-thinking mage can use to disable attackers or weaken their blows.

No other 1st class has an easier time leveling than mages, often without relying on equipment at all. In fact, many other 1st jobs depend heavily on them in groups to ease their leveling woes. Whether slinging [[Fire Ball]]s in Louyang Field, controlling mobs with [[Fire Wall]], or casting bolt spells while others draw attention, a mage is always the party's linchpin.

==Jobchange Guide==
''See [[Mage Job Change Guide]] for detailed information.''










==Mage Builds==
To ensure your mage becomes functional later on, you've got to plan your skill build according to the 2nd job you'll graduate as. This section details different [[Wizard]] and [[Sage]] builds to give you a good idea of what they do, whether you might like to turn your mage into one and how you should allocate your skill points until you job change. You can see the recommended stat allocation, skill overview and example builds on the [[Wizard]] and [[Sage]] pages.

===INT/DEX Wizard===
INT/DEX [[Wizard]]s are raw power. They're the foremost AoE magical damage dealers, a solid choice for anyone who wants a magic character that's flashy and strong.

* '''Pros''' : High magic AoE damage covering 4 elements, very unique gameplay with strategic use of spells, especially solo, always in demand for parties, a good choice for a new/budget character as they are not very gear dependant. 
* '''Cons''' : Very squishy, cast times will be dreadfully long until later levels or unless paired with a [[Bard]], high skill floor

For more information see: [[Wizard#PvE_(DEX)]]

===AGI Wizard===
These are [[Wizard]]s who are more focused on soloing rather than partying, adding an extra layer of defense via dodging enemies on top of their defensive spells to make solo farming as a wizard faster/easier.

* '''Pros''' : High magic AoE damage covering 4 elements, very unique gameplay with strategic use of spells, especially solo, the strongest wizard at solo gameplay, a good choice for a new/budget character as they are not very gear dependant. 
* '''Cons''' : Cast times will be very long until later levels, even then will be considerably slower than INT/DEX wizards, high skill floor

For more information see: [[Wizard#PvE (AGI)]]

===Bolter Sage===
A spellcaster who is more focused on single target killing rather than groups. Often recommended as the best first character for a new player, bolter [[Sage]]s can be capable farmers and level easily even while basically naked. 

* '''Pros''' : High single target damage covering 4 elements, easy to play, always in demand for parties, arguably the best first character for a new/budgeting player
* '''Cons''' : "Buff self, cast bolt spell, repeat" gameplay can feel repetitive to some

For more information see: [[Sage#Bolter]]

===Hindsight Sage===
An unusual spellcaster that swings around their books in melee range to shower their enemies with spell hits. These [[Sage]]s are for those who want something powerful, but a little different.

* '''Pros''' : Very unique gameplay as a melee caster, very flexible with being able to adapt using different [[Hindsight]] spells for different situations instantly
* '''Cons''' : More gear dependant than other casters as you rely heavily on flee and take damage much more often in melee, unable to function well in melee until mid-late levels

For more information see: [[Sage#Hindsight]]

* Creamy Card: Enables use of Level 1 [[Teleport]]. A mage can farm this card relatively easily 1 map west, 1 map south of Geffen once they have ~70 INT total. This item is best placed in a Clip [1] or Brass Wristwatch [1].

A mage can farm this card relatively easily 2 maps south of [[Prontera]] then a bit further southwest in Ant Hell 02 once they have ~70 INT total. ==Gameplay Tips==
Firewall is a powerful asset for mages. With practice, it could be used to solo mob high level content for fast levels.
===Vertical Fire Wall===
Vertical [[Fire Wall]] is the technique where you cast [[Fire Wall]] adjacent to your character so it casts vertically. This is useful because combined with mobbing and anticipating monster's pathing route, you can have monsters hit all 3 pillars of fire.

<center>[[File:Firewall02.jpg|550px]]</center>
<center>''Cast [[Fire Wall]] on the yellow circle while anticipating for monsters' movements in the red arrow direction.<ref name=":0">http://myrolife.blogspot.com/2016/05/verticle-fire-wall-guide.html</ref>'' </center>


<center>[[File:Firewall03.jpg|500px]]</center>
<center>''Monsters will moving in the red arrow direction, hitting all cells of the [[Fire Wall]].<ref name=":0" />''</center>

For a more in-depth guide on vertical [[Fire Wall]]s, read [http://myrolife.blogspot.com/2016/05/verticle-fire-wall-guide.html Vertical Fire Wall Guide]

== Description ==
Enable the caster to receive the SP consumed to cast a [[Category:Magic_Skills|Magic skill]] by an enemy instead of recieving damage. Magic Rod can just be used on single target skills targeted at yourself. If the enemy casts [[Spell Breaker]] and the Sage counters it using Magic Rod, you absorb 20% of the enemy's MaxSP.

== Usage ==
* Magic Rod functions much like the [[Knight]] skill [[Counter Attack]]. You must use Magic Rod when you expect the incoming spell to hit you. There is no cast bar to show you the duration of Magic Rod, but you will know that you succeeded when you receive no damage and gain SP instead. The difference to [[Counter Attack]] is, that you can absorb multiple spells during the duration, instead of a single one
* It is generally best to trigger Magic Rod when the offending skill's cast bar is nearly full. This works for most skills with a noticeable [[Cast_Time|cast time]]. However, against skills such as [[Frost Diver]], it is simpler to spam the skill over and over.
* Magic Rod only functions on magic skills. It will not work on, for example, [[Guillotine Fist]].
* Magic Rod will not work on [[:Category:AoE_Skills|Area of Effect]] skills, such as [[Exploding Dragon]].
* Using Magic Rod will cause your character to have a short delay, like any skill. This prevents you from walking while spamming Magic Rod (despite no cast bar being present).
* When using Magic Rod against [[Water Ball]], every ball is counted as single spell and you absorb every ball within your skill duration. You can even activate it after Water Ball already started.

To gain access, you will need to find Dimitri Vladsky in Glast Heim ( '''/navi glast_01 67,276''' ). He will ask if you would like to perform a ritual to travel deep underground to a place full of cow-like creatures.

Marriage System:
==Overview==

Marriage, sealing the bond you made with that special someone you met in a game. Marriage can be between lovers, or maybe just something fun between friends. Whatever someone's reasons, it's not something to be taken lightly, and both people involved should be sure of their intentions before undertaking this ceremony.

==Requirements==

*You and your Spouse-To-Be must be different genders.

*You and your Spouse-To-Be must be over Base Level 45.

*You or your Spouse-To-Be must not be [[Adoption System | Adopted]] ("Baby" character)

===The Bride===

*1.2 Million [[Zeny]]
*1 {{item|id=2338 Wedding Dress}}
*1 {{item|id=2613 Diamond Ring}}

===The Groom===

*1.3 Million [[Zeny]]
*1 {{item|id=7170 Tuxedo}}
*1 {{item|id=2613 Diamond Ring}}

==Ceremony==

With all the items, head towards Prontera Church located in the northeast of [[Prontera]] City. Speak to the marriage [[NPC]] to initiate the ceremony. Either the groom or bride can do this. The bride/groom who first registered must then have his/her future spouse speak with the same NPC within one minute before the application times out.

Once both parties have spoken with the marriage NPC, they can proceed to the front of the church where the priest will say a few words. He will ask both parties one final time if they wish to proceed; should both parties agree, the ceremony begins and the marriage is complete.

The {{item|id=2613 Diamond Rings}} transform into Wedding Rings <sup>{{item|id=2634}}{{item|id=2635}}</sup> which must be identified using a {{item|id=611 Magnifier}} before wedding skills can be used. Once the bride and groom have equipped the rings, then marriage skills become available. The skills can be cast even if only one spouse is wearing a ring, but only the spouse who has the ring equipped can use the skills.

==Skills==

After you and your beloved tie the knot, you will obtain Wedding Rings based on your gender. When you equip the ring, you will obtain special marriage skills:

*Romantic Rendezvous
**While the Wedding Ring is equipped, spouses can summon their partners to their locations. This skill requires 15 seconds for it to cast, and does not have any delay after it is used. However, this skill cannot be used on any map that cannot be set as a memo by warp portal, ie guild war zones and dungeons.

*Loving Touch
**Consume 10% of one`s HP to restore 10% of your partner`s HP.

*Undying Love
**Consume 10% of one`s SP to restore 10% of your partner`s SP.

==Conclusion==

Afterwards, you both will be in your formal wear, and won't be able to attack or use skills for an hour. Many people decide to visit the honeymoon town of [[Jawaii]], which can be accessed from an [[NPC]] near the docks in [[Izlude]]. You can also take advantage of the [[Adoption System]], if you so choose. Also, if you are not happy with your spouse you can [[Divorce]].

==Overview==
Always on the lookout for profit, Merchants are the economic experts of the game. Setting out to make a fortune, playing as a Merchant will allow the player to get the most out of every last zeny. Merchants are also handy with items, being able to carry far more than other classes thanks to their Enlarge Weight Limit and Pushcart abilities.

Although a Merchant is bound to feel more at home at the marketplaces and auction houses, they can still hold their own in battle, specially when it comes to defending their wares. Inherently sturdy, Merchants are able to equip most of the game's heavy armor and melee weapons, allowing good defense and decent attack.

After a life of buying and selling items, Merchant second jobs provide the possibility of making their own. Merchants can choose to change into a Blacksmith or an Alchemist at Job levels 40 to 50.

Starting stats for merchants depend mostly on whether the player wishes to make a battle-oriented character or concentrate on the stats needed after job change in order to make items successfully. In the first case, a swordsman-like starting build is a good idea, both in its VIT and AGI variants. In the second case, the player should keep in mind that Blacksmiths' forging success and Alchemists' potion mixing depend heavily on high DEX and LUK, as well as INT in the case of Alchemists.

local p = {}

-- Function to find the position of a substring
function p.pos(frame)
    local str = frame.args[1]
    local substr = frame.args[2]
    local init = tonumber(frame.args[3]) or 1

    local pos = string.find(str, substr, init, true)
    if pos then
        return pos - 1
    else
        return -1
    end
end

-- Function to extract a substring
function p.sub(frame)
    local str = frame.args[1]
    local start = tonumber(frame.args[2]) + 1  -- Lua is 1-based, MediaWiki is 0-based
    local length = tonumber(frame.args[3])

    if length then
        return string.sub(str, start, start + length - 1)
    else
        return string.sub(str, start)
    end
end

return p

==Overview==

[[Image: Monk.jpg|thumb|left]]

Monks are a versatile class that can deal damage in several ways unique to themselves. They are most known for the powerful Guillotine Fist skill, which has uses in MVP, PVP and WoE scenarios. Most builds are damage-dealers, focusing on maximizing damage via skills such as Occult Impaction and their Combo abilities. Specialized Monk builds can be very efficient for MVP and WoE purposes.

==Job Change Guide==

''See [[Monk Job Change Guide]] for information.''
























==Builds==
===Combo Monk===
*STR: 80+
*AGI: 61-80+
*VIT: 1
*INT: 30+
*DEX: 40-60+
*LUK: 1

The picture painted by combo monks is exactly what comes to mind when anyone thinks of what a "monk class" should look like in any game: Fists of fury behind a huge mass of muscles. A combo monk is a unique autoattacker who follows up [[Triple Attack]] procs with skills like [[Chain Combo]] and [[Combo Finish]] as part of a chain to deal an enormous flurry of damage. Almost exclusively a solo character, combo monks have an easy time leveling with their high damage output, higher than normal flee and excellent self-sustain. 

Being an autoattacker, combo monks value STR and AGI like any other. However, because so much of their damage is skill-based, they generally tend to prioritize STR over AGI to minimize the number of [[Chain Combo]]s or [[Combo Finish]]es needed to kill targets, thus improving SP efficiency. A low to medium amount of INT is needed (even alongside other tools like magmawhip card and [[Absorb Spirits]]) to sustain combo use (See: [[Monk#SP_Regen_Breakpoints]]). Though they have an easier time reaching 100% HIT thanks to [[Blessing]], higher DEX also improves the cast time of [[Absorb Spirits]] and [[Call Spirits]], and so has value beyond just hitting things or raising the minimum damage floor. Generally speaking, a combo monk will plan their final base AGI and DEX values around whatever the highest HIT/FLEE thing they want to kill is (E,g., Corruptor, Anubis, DRILL), and then put the rest of their points into as much STR and then INT as they can get. 

Some monks looking for a lower damage but less spammy/gear dependent build make "pure autoattack" monks, which are basically combo monks but without [[Chain Combo]] or [[Combo Finish]]. These types of monks prioritize AGI more heavily than combo monks. Before making a combo or any kind of autoattacking monk, please read [[Monk#Chain Combo/Combo Finish]] as the build has unique considerations when it comes to putting points in certain skills.

''The following covers skills that may not be straight forward picks, and provides context to help an aspiring combo monk make decisions regarding their build.''

* [[Triple Attack]]: Triple Attack (TA) has an unusual skill level progression where its activation rate ''decreases'' and its damage% ''increases'' with higher skill levels. Given this, some combo monks opt to only invest 5 points into this skill to maximize the proc rate of [[Triple Attack]], allowing them to get more frequent combos and higher uptime on [[Combo Finish]]'s damage buff. On paper this seems like a good idea, however in practice most enemies do not live long enough for a full combo, much less for something like "buff uptime" to matter. The reality is that both approaches (5 points in TA vs 10 points) are fairly similar DPS, but putting 10 points into triple attack results in slightly better SP efficiency, at the cost of 5 skill points. 
* [[Chain Combo]]: Pure "autoattack" monks should '''never''' put points into this skill (See: [[Monk#Chain Combo/Combo Finish]]). Combo monks shouldn't put points into this skill until they have 5 spare points, and until their build has enough INT to sustain combo use.
* [[Combo Finish]]: Pure "autoattack" monks should '''never''' put points into this skill (See: [[Monk#Chain Combo/Combo Finish]]). Combo monks shouldn't put points into this skill until they have 5 spare points, and until their build has enough INT to sustain combo use. One interesting application of this skill is that the forced delay added to [[Chain Combo]] does ''not'' trigger if no [[Spirit Sphere]]s are active. For combo monks who don't intend on using this skill (but who ''do'' plan on using [[Chain Combo]]), there is merit to investing 5 points into this skill as the added 3.33% proc rate on [[Triple Attack]] it grants passively is worth more damage over time than the "never-miss" damage of having 5 [[Spirit Sphere]]s active.

* [[Dodge]]: An important skill as all combo monks aim to flee things, but a place where points can be taken out of if needed.
* [[Investigate]]: Combo monks are excellent users of investigate given their flee and INT investment, particularly for combo monks with 90+ base STR.

* [[Pneuma]]: Can be nice for some maps with dangerous ranged enemies like Ashes01, Clock Tower or GH Chiv01/02, but otherwise somewhat niche. Generally only an option for pure "autoattack" monks who forgo any kind of combo skills.
* [[Signum Crucis]]: Though rough on SP consumption, this skill can be very good if the monk plans on hunting certain high DEF enemies like Loli Ruri or Corruptors. Generally only an option for pure "autoattack" monks who forgo any kind of combo skills.
|}

===TSS Monk===
*STR: 80+
*AGI: 1
*VIT: 1
*INT: 13-35+
*DEX: 90+
*LUK: 1

TSS or ''Throw Spirit Sphere'' monks are powerful ranged damage dealers more akin to spellcasters than what one would typically associated with a predominantly melee class. These monks use [[Finger Offensive]] (aka "Throw Spirit Sphere") to deal high physical damage from afar, and the unique [[Investigate]] skill to turn their foe's defenses against them. TSS monks excel as solo characters, especially adept at farming high DEF/VIT monsters and enemies with 11k HP or less that have a large elemental weakness.

Given that TSS monks aim to kill their targets before being reached by them, DEX is usually the priority for these characters. This isn't always true, however, as reaching 130 total STR is the only means of one shotting many targets (E.g., Permeter, Freezer) with [[Investigate]]. If they want to invest a decent amount into INT, TSS monks generally have to choose whether they want to focus more on [[Finger Offensive]] or [[Investigate]]. If the monk opts for very little INT and aims for 95+ base STR/DEX, they will rely much more heavily on [[Absorb Spirits]] use but be more flexible in terms of where they can level.

TSS monks rely entirely on the SCOUT card to refund [[Spirit Sphere]]s when they kill a target with [[Finger Offensive]], and so generally aim to kill targets with that skill using rank 3 or lower (% damage on all ranks are normalized, see [[Class Rebalance#Monk]])

* [[Pneuma]]: Though somewhat niche, it is useful for enemies like Penomena or Gargoyle which have annoying ranged attacks (and which TSS monks excel at killing). Pneuma + [[Absorb Spirits]] spam on a ranged enemy is an especially useful combo.

===MS Monk===
*STR: 1-30
*AGI: 1
*VIT: 99
*INT: 50-70
*DEX: 60+
*LUK: 1

MS monks forgoe all offensive capability in order to turn themselves into the ultimate tank. [[Steel Body]] (Commonly known as "Mental Strength", hence the moniker) sacrifices the user's mobility and skill-use in exchange for incredible hardiness, doubling DEF and quadroupling MDEF. These monks are entirely party-focused characters, and are severely limited in their ability to level or farm solo (''With one exception, see below'').

As dedicated tanks, their most important attribute is VIT with most MS monks maxing that stat. The amount of INT an MS monk gets depends largely on their equipment. If they're using the Loli Ruri card (autocasts [[Heal]] when hit) then higher INT directly translates into more survivability, aside from its typical benefits. DEX on the other hand is important both for functionality and convenience, as [[Steel Body]] has a fairly lengthy cast time of 5 seconds. Some MS monks opt into getting a bit of STR to help with carry weight for potions or other items. 

In rare cases, MS monks who have access to incredibly rare and expensive autocast cards like Dark Lord or Mutant Dragonoid can use a High Orc carded shield to turn themselves into an incredibly efficient solo leveler. Monks built this way will put a higher priority on INT to capitalize on their spell casts, and favor maps that have a high mob density. 

Because the effectiveness of [[Steel Body]] depends entirely on the character's DEF and MDEF stats, this build is only practical for well established/geared players.

===Asura Monk===
*STR: 90+
*AGI: 1
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 70-90
*DEX: 40-60+
*LUK: 1

The legendary ''One Punch Monk''. These monks use the almighty [[Asura Strike]] (otherwise known as ''"Guillotine Fist"'') to pour all of their SP into a single, enormously powerful attack. Asura monks are chiefly hunters of MvP or "boss" enemies, especially those with lower defense or who can be affected by [[Signum Crucis]]. Aside from boss killing, asura monks are also capable users of [[Finger Offensive]] and [[Investigate]], often leveling using those two skills.

STR is usually maxed at or near 99 depending on gear choices. INT and DEX vary greatly, and is generally a matter of taste. Higher DEX means a higher damage floor and decreased likelihood of dying when going for the [[Asura Strike]]. Higher INT on the other hand means more damage, but whether that damage translates into fewer [[Asura Strike]]s needed depends on the MvP, and so on which targets the individual is hunting. It is also worth pointing out that higher DEX means an easier time leveling, as asura monks can be leveled on many similar maps as TSS monks.

===Combo Monk Gear===
Combo monks prioritize STR, AGI/FLEE and MaxSP/SP Recovery, using equipment that bolsters those stats. Aside from the more expensive options like Spectring/Firelock Soldier, Sohee card will usually be more +SP regen compared to Eggyra as it is rare for combo monk to reach enough INT for Eggyra to overtake it. The Mummy + Ancient Mummy card combo makes for a decent option for combo monks (especially pure autoattacker monks) when fighting high DEF [[Shadow]] enemies like Loli Ruri and Corruptors. The Necrofantasy set is also a solid choice for combo monks, as with offensive [[Blessing]] 1 (See: [[Monk#Debuffing Demons and the Undead]]) and [[Demon Bane]] monks are great killers of [[Undead]].

Aside from elemental fists, the weapon of choice for combo monks is generally carded Waghnak [4]s, as the +ATK/STR threshold where these fists overtake other slotted ones is quite low (See: [[Monk#Fist Weapons & STR Breakpoints]]). Knuckle Duster [3] or Studded Knuckles [3] make for a reasonable, cheaper alternative, providing you can find some for sale. Hatii Claw [1] are also an excellent cost-effective alternative, though it may be difficult to resell later.

Combo/autoattacking monks have some pretty great options for new or budgeting players owing to the cheap material costs of very very strong elemental fists ([[Forging]]). Wind or Fire fists are generally the more popular choices as far as those weapons go. As an early investment, a 3x Goblin carded Knuckle Duster [3] (very cheap, but sometimes hard to find for sale) is a solid choice for a first carded weapon as Goblin Cards are often plentiful and much cheaper than other +% race cards, and [[Brute]] enemies make up a lot of good maps for leveling. The Enchanted Peach Tree Card is another solid first investment that helps with sustain, but ''only'' if the monk has learned level 10 [[Heal]].

===TSS Monk Gear===
For using [[Finger Offensive]] TSS monks usually prioritize DEX over STR boosting accessories. For [[Investigate]], most of the more valuable targets can't be one/two hit without using STR boosting gear to reach 120/120 STR. maxSP and SPrecovery is important to TSS monks. Sohee Card is generally best choice for SP regeneration ''until roughly 46 total INT'' ([[Monk#SP Regen Breakpoints]]) when Eggyra overtakes it. 

Carded Chain [3]s are likely to be the weapon of choice for TSS monks. However, at 120 STR and higher Mace [4]s start to do more damage. This difference is slight, and may not justify the added expense, depending on if that extra damage is needed to one shot a target or not ([[Monk#See_Also]]).  

The two most important cards for a TSS monk are the SCOUT and Magmawhip Cards. SCOUT cards are dirt cheap, as far as cards go, and are essential for a TSS monk to be able to function solo. Magmawhip Card isn't ''essential'', but effectively halves the SP consumption of TSS when used to one shot monsters, and is a solid first major investment outside of weapons or weapon cards. Elemental vvs fists are very affordable ([[Forging]]), with either [[Earth]] or [[Wind]] being the first choice for a budgeting/new TSS monks depending on where they intend on leveling ([[Monk#Monk_Leveling]]). Other early investments include Sohee carded footgear, and non-slotted Gloves.

''' Recommended Stat Progression '''
* There are many approaches to stat progression for autoattackers that differ from person to person. Generally speaking those without access to +FLEE gear will have to prioritize AGI earlier, and more heavily than those with +20 FLEE garment, Scouting Scarf, Steel Chonchon Pet, etc.
** Ideally, plan your AGI/DEX around the FLEE/HIT requirement of what you'll level on in your 60s, 70s, etc and then you can put the remainder into STR/INT.
* Before putting any points into [[Chain Combo]] or [[Combo Finish]], it is recommended that you have at least ~30 total INT for SP management to be less tedious.

==Gameplay Tips==
===Chain Combo/Combo Finish===
Before investing any points into these skills, it is important to know how they function as well as the unique consequences of taking these skills.

'''[[Chain Combo]]'''
* Putting ''any'' amount of points into this skill '''PERMAMENTLY adds a (1000 - 4*agi - 2*dex + 300) ms delay to the end of your [[Triple Attack]]s'''. There is no way to opt out of this delay, whether you intend to use chain combo or not.
* This skill can only be triggered while in this delay that follows [[Triple Attack]].
* This skill passively adds a (skillLv/2)% additional chance of [[Triple Attack]] triggering.  

In essence, what the above means is that a "autoattack monk" should '''never''' put any skill points into [[Chain Combo]], otherwise they will ruin their build or be forced into becoming a combo monk instead. For combo monks, it is generally a good idea to wait before putting any points into this skill until you:

a) Have at least 5 unspent skill points so you can use the skill at its maximum potency, rather than suffer the forced ACD on [[Triple Attack]] without the full benefits.
<br>
b) Wait until you have sufficient INT/SP regen in your build so that you can sustain [[Chain Combo]] use.

'''[[Combo Finish]]'''
* Putting ''any'' amount of points into this skill '''PERMANENTLY adds a (1000 - 4*agi - 2*dex + 300) ms delay to the end of your [[Chain Combo]]s.
* This delay, however, will '''not''' trigger if you do not have any active [[Spirit Sphere]]s
* This skill can only be triggered while in the delay that follows [[Chain Combo]].
* After using this skill, the user gains a 15% damage increase for 8 seconds.
* This skill consumes one [[Spirit Sphere]] per use.
* This skill passively adds a (skillLv*2/3)% additional chance of [[Triple Attack]] triggering.

One interesting clause regarding its "forced ACD" on [[Chain Combo]] is that this delay does not trigger unless a [[Spirit Sphere]] is active. This means that a combo monk could theoretically invest 5 skill points into this skill, and then simply avoid summoning [[Spirit Sphere]]s if they don't intend to use the skill on a given map, or for a given enemy. Doing this will still yield the benefits of the added passive chance of triggering [[Triple Attack]], which is a greater boost to DPS than the "never miss" damage of 5 [[Spirit Sphere]]s.

===Debuffing Demons and the Undead===
Certain acolyte and [[Priest]] beneficial spells have negative effects when used against [[Demon]] race or [[Undead]] '''element''' enemies. Making use of these spells as debuffs can give the user an extra edge against these foes.

*[[Blessing]]: Reduces [[Demon]] race and [[Undead]] element DEX and INT by 50% for the skill duration (100% success rate).
*[[Heal]]: Deals half its normal healing amount as [[Holy]] damage to [[Undead]] element only. The damage it deals is modified by the target's [[Undead]] element level (e.g., 200% weakness to [[Holy]] for [[Undead]] 4 monsters). Using [[Heal]] to damage [[Undead]] is commonly referred to as "Heal bombing".

For monks generally only [[Blessing]] is relevant, where [[Blessing]] rank 1 can be used on [[Demon]] or [[Undead]] enemies to reduce the power of their spells and make them much easier to flee.

1. Visit the Monk Abbey (prt_monk), located one map East, one map North and two maps East of Prontera.

2. Talk to Guarding Monk (58,247) by the entrance to the map then to Sensei Moohae inside the building at around (245,104). If you meet the qualifications, he will give you the first test, item collecting.

3. Sensei Moohae will assign you one of the following quests:

4. Once the items have been collected, return to Sensei Moohae. You will be directed to Elder Touha, located at (prt_monk 251, 255), in the top right area, for the memory test (Yes, this is despite Sensei Moohae telling you that he's located in the ''northwest'').

5. Elder Touha will have you remember one of the following:

* ''And sheperds we shall be, for thee my lord for thee. Power path decended forth from the hand so our feet may swiftly carry out thy command and we shall flow a river forth thee and teeming with souls shall it ever be. In nomine Patris, et Filii et Spiritus Sancti.''
* ''I seek the path of enlightenment. We monks shall hold true to what we believe and will help protect others through the teachings we learn through our lives. In nomine Patris, et Filii et Spiritus Sancti.''
* ''I commit myself to veritas and aequitas. I will follow my path to enlightenment and purity. I will protect my brothers with life. Evil shall never be victorious while I breathe. In nomine Patris, et Filii et Spiritus Sancti.''

She will read entire passage out before allowing you to recite it. There is no penalty for failing; you can simply retry the test. Once complete, you will be sent to Boohae, located at (prt_monk 57, 179), on the left side of the map, by a cliff.

6. Boohae will give you the option of two tests: '''Marathon''' and '''Mushroom''' collecting ('''This test is recommended over the Marathon, because is less risky.'''). Later, the player may return to Boohae to change the test, if it is needed.

7a. If you choose "Marathon": Talk to the door keeper in front of the Abby at (prt_monk 192,170). After, enter the building and find Bashu. Tell him "Marathon". He will then send you to another area.

Run around this map without falling into the pits for many laps (about 10) to complete the Marathon test. The map is shaped like a ring, with occasional holes that players can fall into. This test is easier to complete by lowering the camera angle very low (Ctrl+Shift+mouse wheel up), allowing pits far ahead to be seen easily.

Note that disconnecting will send you back to your save point. After the test is completed with the needed amount of laps,you will automatically be sent out. It takes approximately 30 minutes with Increase Agility to complete.

'''Skip to Step 8.'''

7b. Talk to Bashu in the center building by the cliff, beside training dummy props. Building door is at (prt_monk 192, 170). Choose "Collect Mushrooms": you will be sent to another map where you must hunt two types of mushrooms (Gooey & Orange). The NPC does not tell the player that they have enough mushrooms until they have 30 of either type of mushroom. The mushrooms from the Thief test can also be used. While it is possible to have a prospective Thief gather the mushrooms, it should be easier to have an Acolyte with high agility and buffs to complete this test faster. It is best to do this bare-handed for maximum ASPD (since the damage is capped at 1 regardless of weapon). The NPC to exit is located at (job_monk 224, 180). In order to finish the quest you must bring him 30x Gooey Mushrooms and 30x Orange Mushrooms.

8. Now locate Tomoon, also found indoors within the Abbey (prt_monk 192, 170) inside what appears to be a glowing cross. He sends you to an invisible maze. Be warned that during this test, monsters will spawn, such as Zombies and Mummies. They should not be much of a challenge, but keep in mind that you don't have much maneuvering area here.

It is possible to check if a certain cell is passable by pointing the cursor at it. Walkable cells will have the usual green walk marker; if there is none, then that cell is blocked. Generally, try sticking to a straight line from the door to the exit. If there is a choice of routes, take the one that goes closer to the center line. Patience is highly required. Disconnecting in this test will send a player back to their save point.

9. Once out of the maze, talk to Tomoon again and he will give you a Green Potion. Return to Moohae and drink or drop any or all Green Potions you have in your inventory. Moohae will ask you some questions to prompt you for your vows as a Monk.

As a reward, he'll give you a Waghnak, unless your job level is 50, in which case he will give you a Knuckle Duster.
