Morroc:
=About Morroc=
Morroc is the desert town, located next to the {{map |id=moc_ruins Pyramids}} and {{map |id=moc_fild19 Sphinx}}. It is (basically) home to the [[Thief]] and [[Soul Linker]] guilds. 

=Destruction of Morroc=

With the new update of Episode 12 comes the Demise of Morroc.
Morroc receives massive damage because of Satan Morroc's awakening. Due to this,                                   
a refugee camp is set up near the Pyramids and several [[NPC]]s are displaced in the area.

[[Image:SatanMorroc.gif|thumb]]

=== Story===

Long ago, the Mage Knight Thanatos battled and sealed away the greater demon, Satan Morroc. Legend has it that the fallout from the battle destroyed the south eastern part of the Rune-Midgard Kingdom, creating what is now known as the Sograt Desert. In order to protect the seal and keep the demon locked away, the people of Rune-Midgard constructed a castle above the seal. Before long, buildings and tents were built around the castle, and this new-founded city took the name of the demon and was called "Morroc".

However, one thousand years have now passed, and Satan Morroc has awakened once again!

Morroc will never be the same again. All trace of the once great Desert-city has now disappeared, leaving only sorrow and destruction in its wake. The sacrifice of the heroes of old in sealing Midgard's most primal evil was put to waste.

The city and the desert sand around it were soaked in the blood of all living things slaughtered by its resurrection. Now freed from its evanescent bonds, all hope of shelter and refuge are lost.

The omen of destruction blooms as dark as the night in the cold desert. The evil that can twist the very fabric of reality looms across the land: the greatest peril that the Midgard Continent will ever face has arrived.

Morroc has risen.

==Quest==

Quests added with the Satan Morroc update can be found [[Quests#Satan Morroc Quests|here]].

==Morroc, the Aftermath==

Following the resurrection of Satan Morocc, the city of Morroc has changed substantially. The site of the Morocc Incident, the Morroc Castle, has been completely leveled, and many of the surrounding structures destroyed or abandoned. Refugees of the Morroc Incident have set up a camp near the pyramids, with some of the services that were once provided within morroc moved to the refugee camp ({{map |id=moc_ruins moc_ruins}}).

'''The following is a list of changes you can expect to see:'''

*'''Kafra Service:''' Teleport to Prontera added (South Kafra only).
*'''Inn:''' The Inn service in both the south and northeast has ended.
*'''PvP:''' No Change.
*'''Refine NPCs:''' Repairman has moved to the Refugee Camp. Others unchanged.
*'''NPC Vendors:''' All outdoor NPC vendors have moved to the Refugee Camp. (For example, the Tool Dealers, Jewelers, and Item Collectors have been moved while the Weapon and Armor Dealers remain in their shop in the SE corner.)
*'''Dungeon Teleport Vote Service:''' The Kafra/Cool Event employees running the Dungeon Teleport Voting Service have moved to the Refugee Camp.
*'''Walking to Prontera:''' It is still possible to walk to Prontera.  From Morroc, walk one map north ({{map | id=moc_fild07 Sograt Desert 7}}), one map east (Dimensional Gorge).  Walk to the central northern portion of this map and you will encounter a pair of Continental Guard at the foot of a ramp just before the top of the map.  Speak to one of the guards and ask what happened.  After some dialogue, he'll give you an option to teleport to Prontera Field.  Where you are sent, however, is the southern side of {{map | id=moc_fild01 Sograt Desert 1}}.  From here, travel two maps north to Prontera.  (Note: Due to the complication and the dangers of the Dimensional Gorge and the tendency of Dead/Bloody Branch monsters on the map south of Prontera ({{map | id=prt_fild08 Prontera Field 8}}), Kafra Teleport from Morroc to Prontera is simpler and safer.)


[[Image:Morroc.png]] [[Image:Morroc12.png]]

Following the Morocc Incident, Satan Morocc retreated into the desert. Morocc used his powers in an apparent attempt to protect himself and to separate Morroc from the remainder of Rune Midgard, changing the area drastically. Entire regions the Sograt Desert simply ceased to exist, and in their place lies a twisted anomaly of Time and Space known as the Dimensional Gorge. 
The following map shows which regions of the Sograt Desert have been removed:

[[Image:Region.jpg]]

The areas shown in grey are no longer available. All regions previously leading to those maps now bring you to the Dimensional Gorge. Because of the strange nature of the region, navigation is difficult. Members of the Continental Guard have become increasingly proficient at navigating the area, and so you should ask them for help if you need to leave. There are two other areas deeper within the crack of dimension, but because of Satan Morocc's influence within the region, only the Continental Guards are allowed to enter these areas.

=The Dimensional Gorge=

''Hoarse, dark laughter echoes from the curtain of shadow cast by the crimson moon.''
''Blood is the currency of the soul," a voice whispered… The haunting whisper escorts the red moon as it descends to earth.''

''The desert sand is soaked in blood shed by the resurrected Satan.''
''As the gap of darkness rises from hell, every semblance of safety and sanctuary seems to vanish.''

''The omen of destruction blooms in the darkness of night in the cold desert.''
''The evil that can twist the delicate fabric of time and space looms across the land: the greatest peril that the'' ''Midgard Continent will ever face has arrived.''

...

The city in the world’s greatest desert – built on the ground over which Satan Morroc was confined – became shrouded in darkness. Although the ritual to resurrect Satan Morroc was interrupted by brave adventurers whose names are unsung, they only delayed the inevitable. Waiting for the chance to escape for ages, Satan Morroc did not miss the tiny sliver of opportunity that allowed him to break free, and he has made his reappearance in the human world.

Satan Morroc immediately started destroying all paths leading to Morroc to eliminate all possibility of him being sealed away by humans ever again. First he devastated the desert surrounding Morroc, and then he destroyed the lands to the north. No living creature in those areas survived Satan Morroc’s fury.

Adventurers and quickly spread the news of Morroc’s resurrection all around the world. Many rumors circulated as the public grew more anxious about the destruction that Satan Morroc would surely bring upon them. Adventurers have started flocking to Morroc in an organized effort to fight and confine Satan Morroc as the heroes that preceded them did. They cannot fail as Satan’s ultimate goal is not merely ruining Morroc, but destroying the entire world.

Countless warriors and allied guilds challenged Satan Morroc in hopes of saving humanity. Most of them perished in vain, and although some of them were able to defeat Morroc, Satan Morroc would immediately resurrect. Finally, a group of warriors were able to drive Morroc away to another dimension, leaving a huge time-space gap in this realm. Satan Morroc is gone for now, but no one knows how long it will take to rebuild and recover from the vast devastation that it has left behind.

==Overview==

The Dimensional Gorge is an area near the town of Morroc where Satan Morroc resides added as part of Episode 12. The Dimensional Gorge is the transformed ruins of the old Sograt Desert, warped by Morrocs resurrection and home of high level monsters. Pockets of torn space riddle the desert as a result of Satan's resurrection.

Access to the Dimensional Gorge is directly out the east exit of the city of Morroc. To be allowed entrance to the Dimensional Gorge however, you must be level 80 and begin the Continental Guard quest. Within this zone, you will find many apparitions of Satan Morroc. As part of the quest, you can summon and do battle with Satan Morroc. It is recommended that you have a team of at least 20 players to properly fight him.

Upon defeat Morroc will retreat into one of the dimensional rifts. After completing the related quest, you can follow the Wounded Morroc and challenge him again as an MVP boss monster. His power here is more in line with that of a regular high end [[MVP]].

The following items provide a bonus identical to, and do not stack with [[Increase AGI]]

*{{item |id=662 Authoritative Badge}} (180%)
*{{item |id=12028 Box of Thunder}} (200%)
*{{item |id=1363 Bloody Axe}} (140%)
*{{item |id=5286 PecoPeco Hairband}} (140%)
*Any item which offers increased movement speed.

It is likely that almost any item or skill that says it increases movement rate behaves in this way as well. 

The following skills increase movement speed by some degree: 

*[[Cart Boost]] (Said to be slightly slower than Agi Up, and does not stack)
*[[Wind Walker]] (Does not stack with Agi Up)
*[[Improve Dodge]] (For [[Assassin]]s only) 
*[[Cloaking]] (boost is greater next to walls)
*[[Urgent Escape]] (For [[Alchemist]]s with the homunculus [[Lif]])
*[[Solar, Lunar and Stellar Union]]

The following skills and effects reduce movement speed by some degree: 

*[[Pushcart]] (Reduces movement speed by 50% - 5%*Skill Level while cart is equipped) 
*[[Quagmire]] (also cancels most movement speed and ASPD increasing effects) 
*[[Decrease AGI]] 
*[[Slow Grace]] 
*[[Ground Drift]] if used with the Sticky Grenade ammunition
*[[Curse]] 
*[[Battle Chant]] movement & attack speed reduction
*[[Mental Strength]] (if the user is [[Curse]]d while in MS, they will actually walk faster because their movement speed is overwritten by that of [[Curse]], which is not as slow)
*[[Stalk]] (Works the same as Mental Strength)

A Speed Potion does not stack with any other speed increases, and cancels most (all?) speed reducing effects. Speed Potions last 5 seconds.

Muspelheim is a progressive dungeon into the hellish reaches of Surtr's domain. Deep in the lands of Muspelheim are blazing caverns that meet the frozen wastes of Niflheim. However, despite once being the home of giants, Muspelheim has become overrun by dangerous horrors. The deeper you travel into its domain, the greater the challenge, greater the reward, and greater the terror you will encounter. The first couple layers are not too different from Rune Midgard, but still contain very dangerous creatures that will require you and your friends to work together to vanquish.

__TOC__

==Note: Skipping the Questline==

It is only required to go through the questline '''once per account'''. You '''must''' complete each part of the questline on at least one character. However, once that is done, you are able to '''copy your progress''' onto another character within the same account.

Simply bring your MET Permit to the '''MET Card Reader''' (located just outside the dungeon) and the storyline will move forward to your account's current progress point. Once you progress the story via this NPC, '''YOU CANNOT''' revert that change for that character.

You will also be issued a duplicate MET Permit to carry on that character's person so you don't have to keep moving cards around from character to character.

Note that the '''side quests will not be affected''' and can be done on every character.

== Main Questline ==

=== 1F Entrance Quest ===
'''Note: You must have a base level of 75 to begin this quest, otherwise, Captain Hjolnor will turn you away.''' 

1. To gain access, you will first meet with Captain Hjolnor at gef_fild09(296, 57). He will ask if you seriously want to venture inside.

2. After speaking with him he will insist that you first receive permission from Magister Renton. She can be found next to the Wizard Job Quest NPC in Geffen Tower. She was the person who tasked you with killing the Headless Horse back during Halloween. If you helped her before, she will have no problem giving you permission, but if you did not complete the Halloween quest, she will ask you a string of questions to confirm your adventuring prowess. This is a simple test and you only need to choose the correct answers.

|-

|}

After passing her test(or if she already knows you from the Halloween Event) she will give you an MET Permit and send you back to speak with Hjolnor.

3. Speak with Hjolnor again. After seeing your permit, he will ask you to find the scouting party that has gone missing inside the Cave. He tells you that you will need to speak with Mage Illyn and ask that he temporarily lower the border.

4. Speak with Mage Illyn left of the cave entrance and he will temporarily remove the barrier and allow you inside. You must speak with him again each time you wish to enter the dungeon.

=== 1F Quest ===
'''''Beware that all mobs inside the cave are aggressive and the boss mob, the Assassin Fly, will teleport frequently and attempt to hunt down the player. Therefore it is advised that you party with others before entering.'''''

1. Inside the cave you must search for the scouting party. In the top left of the map rockmi1 (60, 354) you will find the remains of one of the scouts and a journal in his hands. 

2. Take the journal back to Hjolnor. He will be distraught at mention of the Assassin Fly and ask you to speak with Magister Renton again and deliver his report. Magister Renton will ask you to destroy the Assassin Fly.

=== 2F Entrance Quest ===
'''Note:''' You must complete the '''entire 1F quest''' before the 2F entrance quest can be initiated.

1. Talk to '''Captain Hjolnor'''. He tells you that the only way to go deeper into Muspelheim is through the elevator lift, whose chain is broken. In order to fix it, you will have to craft '''Rosin''', a flux used for soldering metals. He will ask you to collect and bring '''20 Resin and 2 Alcohol''' to '''Mr. Rockwell''' in the Blacksmith's store in Prontera in order to craft the flux.

2. Head to the '''Blacksmith's store in Prontera (175, 188)''' and go''' inside the room in the bottom portal'''. Hand '''Smith Rockwell''' the items and he will give you the Rosin in exchange.

3. Return to '''Captain Hjolnor''', who gives the flux to one of his crew and asks him to fix the chain- which will take some time. Meanwhile, he has another task for you and asks that you speak to '''Mage Illyn''' (the same NPC that grants you access to the dungeon).

4. Speak to '''Mage Illyn'''. She reveals that they have been doing research on the gases inside of Muspelheim that blocked teleportation once upon a time, and explains that you will need something to amplify your magic in order to regain the ability to do so. She will require you to bring her '''5 Star Dust, 30 Witch Starsand, and an Enchanting Rod''' (bought from '''Mr. King''' in '''Juno (205, 103)''' for 45,000z) in order for her to be able to amplify your magical powers. 

5. Return to '''Mage Illyn''' with the items. She will cast the spell on you to protect you from the gases of Muspelheim- which has the side effect of draining all your remaining SP. Afterwards, she instructs you to return to '''Captain Hjolnor'''.

6. Speak to '''Captain Hjolnor''', who tells you that the chain has been fixed, and that all that needs to be done is to install it onto the elevator. He asks you to return to him if you find anything of interest.

7. Head inside of Muspelheim 1F and click on the '''Elevator''' located near the middle of the map

8. You will end up on a new map ('''there are no monsters here'''), which is just a transition area between 1F and 2F. There are a few [[Muspelheim#Easter_Eggs|Easter Eggs]] here; collect them if you wish. Either way, once you're ready to move on, head to the '''Mysterious Gate''' located near the bottom left of the map (59, 30).

9. Click on the '''Mysterious Gate'''. By doing so, you will collect the crystal affixed to the gate, which will summon a fierce Demon; in two minutes, it will appear and presumably kill you. You are told that you have two minutes to run back to the '''Elevator''' to save yourself.

10. Run back to the '''Elevator'''. Once you are "safely" back on 1F, head back outside the dungeon.

11. Return to '''Captain Hjolnor''' and tell him about what happened. He inspects the crystal you found, but claims to not have the knowledge to investigate it properly. He asks you to bring it to '''Magister Renton''', who can provide a proper analysis. He will also give you a reward for making it out alive.

{| class="wikitable"
! colspan="2" |Rewards
|-
! scope="col" |Items:
|10x White Slim Potion
|}

12. Head to the top floor of Geffen Tower to and speak with '''Magister Renton'''. She will reveal that the mine shift truly is the Road to Muspelheim, and that the crystal is a sort of key that opens a gate between realms. Upon further examination, she reveals the crystal is inactive, which implies that the gate is open despite not appearing to be, and that soon monsters will pour in from Muspelheim. To prevent this from happening, she wants to bring the stone to the Sages in Juno to figure out a way to reactivate it. She asks then asks that you head back to '''Captain Hjolnor''' to update him.

13. Head back to '''Captain Hjolnor''', who is coordinating a defensive effort against the monsters of Muspelheim. He wants to gather the troops near the lift, where they will be briefed, and asks you to speak to '''Mage Illyn''' when you are ready to depart.

14. Speak to '''Mage Illyn''' and hand her your '''MET Permit (Rank 1)'''. She will exchange it for a '''MET Permit (Rank 2)''', which she tells you will let you teleport around the mines. Then, she will ask if you are prepared to set off for the lift to meet with '''Captain Hjolnor'''. Once you agree, you will be teleported inside the Mines Lift.

15. From now on, interacting with the Elevator on 1F will return you to the Mines Lift, from which you can enter Muspelheim 2F. You can also warp directly into the elevator by speaking with Mage Illyn from outside the dungeon.

=== 2F Quest ===
1. From inside the Mines Lift, speak with '''Captain Hjolnor'''. He requests that you slay the Demon that was summoned from the Mysterious Gate. 

2. Defeat [[Logi]] (MVP) on Muspelheim 2F.

3. Return to the Mines Lift and speak with '''Captain Hjolnor'''. He tells you he feels a relieved, but a defensive effort is still required. Either way, he gives you a '''Letter''' and asks you to deliver the news to '''King Tristram III'''.

4. Go to the '''Prontera Castle''' and speak to '''King Tristram III''' (when inside, head down the hallway into the first portal, then down the next hallway into the second portal. In this room, hang left and you should see him standing on his throne). The King thanks you profusely for your services!

If this is your '''first clear on your account''', he will offer you '''ONE of the following rewards''':

*Hood[1]
*Muffler[1]
*Guard[1]
*Buckler[1]
*Sandals[1]
*Shoes[1]

Otherwise, he will reward you with an '''Old Purple Box'''.

New Player Guide:
Hello and welcome to Payon Stories! This guide is meant to answer some frequently asked questions about our server, as well as give some direction for progression in the early game.

Please check this page to see if your questions are already addressed- otherwise, our community is happy to help you over in the Discord.

== Before Getting Started ==

=== Important Payon Stories Rules ===

* There is a strict '''NO MULTICLIENTING''' rule. This applies even if you use multiple PCs.
** '''Exception''': You are allowed to '''Autovend''' on separate accounts while playing.
* You are allowed to have a '''maximum of THREE accounts on one MASTER account.'''
* Account Sharing is '''NOT''' '''ALLOWED.'''
* Custom GRFs are '''NOT ALLOWED'''.
** '''Exception''': Any GRFs provided on the official Payon Stories Download page are okay to use.
* For the full list of rules, see the Rules page or go to the '''#rules''' channel on our Discord. It is highly recommended to give them a quick read.

=== Payon Stories Discord ===
The Payon Stories Discord is the main platform that the community uses to interact. At the time of writing, the forums aren’t terribly active, so joining the Discord will give you the best social experience on the server.

Go to the '''Channels & Roles''' menu to give yourself the permissions required to view whatever content you’re interested in seeing. Simply click on the corresponding option to grant yourself a role.

It is highly recommend to give yourself the following permissions at minimum:

* BST
* Latest News
* At least 1 class related channel

If you have any questions, please try to post them in the appropriate channel.

* For anything '''not''' relating to classes or specific builds, use '''#q-n-a'''.
* Otherwise, use the appropriate class channel ('''#swordsman''', '''#magician''', etc).

=== Important References ===

Payon Stories has implemented several Custom Commands for your convenience.

Before using any of the commands, it is very helpful to know how to obtain the ID of an item or mob. You can do this using one of the following commands:

* '''@mobinfo <mobname>''': Displays mob information and drop table as well as the '''Mob ID.'''

Simply type the message in chat and press Enter/Return execute the command (as if you were chatting). Something like this should be displayed in the chat window as a result (in this example, the value outlined in red is the ID of a Pupa):

Once you have the item or mob ID, you can use them in the following commands (note that these commands also accept names as input, but using an ID is more reliable):

* '''@whereis <mobname or mobid>''': Displays the top 10 maps where a mob is found, ordered by number of spawns. Note that this list is '''not exhaustive'''.

* '''@whobuy2 <itemname or itemid>''': Same as '''@whobuy''', but also enables interacting with Player Shops. Can only be used in towns. Can be abbreviated to '''@wb2'''.

== Gameplay Guide ==

=== Training Camp ===
It is highly recommended to '''complete the entire Training Camp - INCLUDING THE PERSONALITY TEST'''. You will receive a bunch of free items to make your early game much easier, including:

* Novice Main Gauche
* A full set of Novice Armor
* 350-400 Novice Red Potions
** Dying once in the Training Camp (or using a Novice Butterfly Wing on one of the Combat maps) will net you bonus EXP and 50 extra free Novice Red Potions!
* 10 Vouchers for free Kafra Warps
* 10 Vouchers for free Kafra Storage access
* ...and a few other goodies!

'''CAUTION''': On the first map of the Training Camp, there is an NPC named '''Dr. Gerber''' that will prompt you to turn your character into a Baby (visually smaller, Size changes from Medium to Small, -25% HP/SP, lower forge/brew success rate). '''Do not talk to the NPC if you do not want your character to become a Baby''':

After the Combat Test portion of the Training Camp, there is a Kafra NPC named Betty Resetti that will '''reset your stats for free so long as you are Base Lv. 15 or under'''. As a result '''it is recommended to use a melee build (11 DEX, all the rest into VIT) until Job Lv. 10 is reached, then reset for free at the end of the Training Camp''' into whatever is more suitable for your first job.

=== Stat Reset ===
On Payon Stories, it is possible to reset your stats with the following restrictions:

* Pure Stat Resets are '''unlimited''' and '''free up to and including Base Level 15.'''
* Pure Stat Resets are '''unlimited''' and cost 20,000 Zeny and 1x '''[[Image:7005.png|24px|]] [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=7005 Skull]''' '' (Purchasable from Players via Vend (Type @whosell2 Skull in a town to see and buy the cheapest Skulls) or farmed yourself from Alarm, Wanderer, etc.) from '''Base Level 16 up to and including Base Level 45.'''
* Stat Resets '''which now also include Skills''' are '''unlimited''' and cost 5,000,000 Zeny from '''Base Level 46 ownards.''' (Also see: https://wiki.payonstories.com/Stat_Reset)

There are two functionally identical NPCs that will allow you to reset your stats (see the full Stat Reset page for more info):

* '''Betty Resetti''' in the final room of the Training Camp
* '''Phoenix''' in a house in Morroc at 3 O'Clock

=== Payon ===
The main town on Payon Stories is '''Payon'''.

Be sure to '''visit the Promotions NPC (83, 159)''' to get Manuals and other free goodies! (This can only be done once per game account.)

The '''Stylist NPCs (near 122, 156)''' can also be found in the Castle area of Payon. You will need to pay them a '''Stylist Coupon''' in order to use their services, which are obtained via the '''Stylist Exchanger (108, 162)''' in exchange for any Dyestuffs.

=== Clan System ===
Payon Stories has implemented the Clan System with 2 new custom clans. Upon talking to the Clan leader, you will receive '''bonus stats as well as additional HP/SP''' at no charge! It is highly recommended that you pay a visit to the Clan leader of your choice shortly after completing your first job quest. To know more about the clans, the bonus they give and where their leaders are, refer to the [[Clan System]] page.

Note that you can '''join any Clan, regardless of what your job is'''.

If you are '''in a Clan and NOT in a Guild''', your Clan as well as its emblem will appear on your character alongside their name:

If you are '''in a Clan AND in a Guild''', only your Guild Emblem and Rank will appear. It is worth noting that you will '''still receive the Clan bonus even if you are in a Guild'''- they are not mutually exclusive.

=== Exp Share Range for Parties ===
The party level range on Payon Stories is '''15 base levels'''; e.g. a Base Lv. 31 character can share exp with a second character anywhere between Base Lv. 16 and Base Lv. 46. For parties, every member must be within 15 base levels of each other (the difference between the highest and lowest base levels can be 15 at most).

=== Cosmetic Cash Shop ===
There is a cosmetic-only cash shop. The items are account bound. To access the shop in game, type '''@costumestore'''. To get points, you must donate to this [https://buymeacoffee.com/payonstories site] and open a ticket on the discord to claim them. For more information, see the [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=news&action=patch_20240508 patch log].

=== General Leveling Guide ===
The following is a list of commonly recommended grinding spots that is largely applicable to all classes. It is recommended to party up with other players for an easier time as well as more experience- just shout it out on the #lfp channel!

If you are playing a Melee class, please note that some of these spots '''will be very difficult if you do not focus on your defensive stat first'''. As such, it is recommended to focus on VIT or AGI until you can level comfortably without using too many potions before investing in offense.

New players may find it tough early on gearing and purchasing healing items. The following is a supplementary guide for [[Zeny Making Guide|Zeny Making]].

==== Universal tips for the early leveling of some characters ====
Some builds have a very hard time leveling throughout their journey : Full Support priest, Forger Smith, Asura monk, Woe characters... It is strongly advised to use the [[Stat Reset]] feature of Payon Stories at level 45 to make their leveling experience easier. Get the free reset at Training Grounds, then put all your stats in STR, AGI and DEX, equip and refine the weapon you’ve got from the personality test, then level like regular melee classes (see below). When you reach base level 45, reset your stats to fit the build that you're aiming for. Keep stat/skill reset post-level 45 is available; however, at a significant zeny cost.

==== Training Camp (Base Lv. 1-12) ====

* The Training Camp is an excellent place to level in order to reach Job Lv. 10 as a Novice
* You can speak to the NPC in the Hunting Grounds to move to a more challenging floor once EXP starts getting a bit slower, however this is not at all required and will likely cause you to burn through your stock of potions more quickly
* Note that there is a '''free stat reset''' in the next room, so it is recommended to use a melee build while training, then reset before leaving the training camp
** It is recommended to get ~11 DEX (not missing your target is a bigger DPS increase than investing in STR), then putting the rest of your points into VIT to save on potions
* '''Notable Drops''':
** Feather (Fabre, Lunatic)
** Trunk (Willow)
** Strawberry (Spore)
** Orange (Condor)
** Drops card (Drops) 

==== Prontera Culvert 1 & 2 (Base Lv. 12-25) ====

* Good leveling spot to start your journey. Thief Bugs are abundant and not particularly dangerous, while Thiefbug Eggs provide an opportunity to regenerate HP/SP. Just be careful for the aggressive Familiars!
* This is especially a good spot for VIT builds, as Thief Bugs will do negligible damage once you reach ~30 VIT.
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Grape (Familiar)
** Ribbon[1] (Familiar)
** Guard[1] (Thiefbug Egg)
** Iron Ore (Thiefbug Egg)
** Red Gemstone (Thiefbug Egg)
** Strawberry (Spore)

==== Spores (Base Lv. 15-25) ====

* Spores are a classic for low level players and is a great spot to party up. It also provides some early game funding via Strawberries, which can be sold to other players. Keep your HP topped up as they have a hard-hitting water attack!
* Note that Spores might be difficult if leveling solo at the lower end of the recommended range.
* '''Map:''' 1 South of Payon
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Strawberry

==== Payon Dungeon 1 (Base Lv. 15-30) ====

* A slightly more challenging map than Culverts or Spores, but with better exp as compensation.
* Acolytes can heal bomb Zombies and Skeletons if they have an INT build
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Grape (Familiar)
** Ribbon[1] (Familiar)

==== Poring Dig Site 1 & 2 (Base Lv. 15-80) ====

* Payon Stories custom map with a very high mob density. Excellent for parties, particularly with a Swordsman/Merchant with Magnum Break/Cart Revolution, respectively.
* Some classes can stay at Poring Dig Site 2 killing Geographers and/or mobbing Abomrings/Protorings up to Lv. 80 and beyond
* '''Map:''' Talk to the NPC by the boat in Aldebaran directly east from the middle (3 o'clock)
* '''Notable Drops (Level 1):'''
** Kitty Band (Smokie)
** Strawberry (Smokie & Wolf)
** Mantle[1] (Wolf)
** Main Gauche[4] (Jelring)
** Grape (Poporing)
* '''Notable Drops (Level 2):'''
** Main Gauche[4] (Jelring)
** Guard[1] (Abomring)
** Yellow Herb (Abomring)
** Empty Bottle (Abomring)
** Maneater Blossom (Geographer)
** Battle Axe[4] (Protoring) 

==== Smokies and Cocos (Base Lv. 25-40) ====

* Great option for both AGI and VIT builds, with excellent rare drop opportunities.
* Smokies sometimes use their Hide skill when being attacked, so try to party up with an Acolyte/Magician with Ruwach/Sight, respectively
* Note that both Smokies and Cocos have cast sensors, so Magicians should wait for a party member to get aggro before casting
* '''Map:''' 2 East of Payon
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Kitty Band (Smokie)
** Raccoon Leaf (Smokie) - used for crafting headgears
** Hood[1] (Coco)
** Sandals[1] (Coco)
** Strawberry (Coco)

==== Wolves (Base Lv. 25-40) ====

* One of the best early game maps exp-wise, particularly for Magicians if they are able to one-shot with Fire Bolt or Archers with Fire Arrows that can be bought from an NPC. 
* Wolves are not aggressive, however they will assist other Wolves being attacked; try to avoid large packs
* Watch out for the Vagabond Wolf (miniboss)- Fly Wing away if you see a dense pack of wolves charging you!
* '''Map:''' 2 South of Payon
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Strawberry
** Mantle[1]

==== Caramels and Floras (Base Lv. 30-50) ====

* Good option for all builds; ranged attackers can focus on Floras (who do not attack at all unless you stand too close) with fire spells/arrows, while melee attackers can focus on Caramels
* Both of their cards are highly sought after, so if you get a lucky card drop you're set for a while!
* '''Map:''' 2 North, 1 East of Geffen (can warp directly there from Geffen Kafra by selecting 'Mjolnir Dead Mine')
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Coat[1] (Caramel)
** Pike[4] (Caramel)
** Aloe (Flora)
** Singing Flower (Flora)
** Witherless Rose (Flora)
** Maneater Blossom (Flora)

==== Magnolias and Ants (Base Lv. 30-50+) ====

* Really low hp considering exp gains (1.1+k hp, almost 600 base and almost 500 job exp). Dies fast, and with a ton of them in the map - recommended spot to those that care about clearing mobs fast (and thus minimizing potion expenses).
* Magnolia card is sought after, and Andre cards are a guilt-free way to boost your attack if you have a slotted weapon.
* '''Map:''' 1 South, 2 East of Morroc (the map is also the entrance to Ant Hell, as well as the Phreeoni map).
* '''Notable Drops:''' 
** Rough Elunium
** Iron Ore
** Star Dust
** Elemental stones (Green Live, Red Blood)

==== Mi Gaos (Base Lv. 30-50+) ====
* A moving party, going around the map and defeating Mi Gaos
* Mi Gaos are slow, and can be provoked safely by Swordsmen, or via Increase Agi by Acolytes, while mages and archers whittle them down. Other classes are usually expected to take care of the smaller mobs, notably the Mantises.
* '''Map:''' Take the boat to Louyang in Alberta (1k fare), or in Payon (south west of the town map, in the pier, for 2500 zeny).
* '''Notable Drops:'''
** Caramel, Mantis Cards
** Coat [1]
** Pike [4]
** Rough Elunium
** Great Nature
** Green Live
** Gold
Ninja:
{{Infobox Job |jobName=Ninja |jobBase=Novice |jobType=Extended |changesAt=[[Amatsu]] |skills=24 |skillPoints=69 |questSkills=0 |str=1|agi=8|vit=1|int=5|dex=6|luk=4}} == Overview == [[Image: Ninja.jpg|thumb|left]] Ninjas are versatile warriors from Amatsu who use a wide array of unique skills to dispatch foes up close, with ranged weaponry or by using magic. Ninja utilize catalysts in the form of elemental stones as well as kunai and shuriken to employ their techniques, and rely on special evasive skills like [[Cicada Skin Shed]] and [[Mirror Image]] to completely avoid attacks. Similar to [[Gunslinger]]s, ninja is an expanded class and cannot rebirth or be adopted. Because of this, Ninjas and Gunslingers are granted 69 skill points to distribute.
''' Note: Ninjas on Payon Stories have gotten an extensive rework/rebalancing of their skills. See https://wiki.payonstories.com/Class_Rebalance#Ninja for a detailed overview of these changes.'''
== Job change Guide == ''See [[First_Expanded_Change_Guides#Ninja|Ninja Job Change Guide]] for information.'' == Builds == === Magic === * STR: 1 * AGI: 1+ * VIT: 1 * INT: 99 * DEX: 90+ * LUK: 1 Those who wield ninjutsu to deal [[Fire]], [[Wind]] and [[Water]] damage call themselves magic ninja. The spells of a magic ninja are fast and have little to no aftercast delay (ACD), meaning they don't have to rely on [[Bard]]s or [[Priest]]s to function well. These ninja are extremely mobile, using skills like [[Cicada Skin Shed]] and [[Shadow Jump]] ([[Ninja#Sight Shadow Jump]]) to move rapidly and evade attackers. A skilled magic ninja can level very quickly, is difficult to kill, and will impress passersby with the almost limitless number of enemies they can handle at once. Similar to INT/DEX [[Wizard]]s, magic ninja invest primarily in those two attributes. Unlike [[Wizard]]s, however, they have a much greater priority on INT over DEX in almost all situations as their cast times are shorter, meaning they are less impacted by DEX. Magic ninja also benefit more from AGI than other casters when solo, as without an ACD, the limiting factor on how often a skill can be used is based on attack speed after cast time drops below a character's ASPD delay. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |Build Playstyle | '''Solo'''
For the most part, [[Blaze Shield]] is the bread and butter of magic ninja leveling and farming, it is by far their most effective tool. While protected with [[Cicada Skin Shed]], mobs are gathered up and tightly stacked (this can be done by walking around them in a circle or jumping around with [[Sight]] [[Shadow Jump]] [[Ninja#Sight Shadow Jump]]) and then carefully lead through [[Blaze Shield]]'s embers. The ninja rotates around their [[Blaze Shield]] with the mob in tow, trying to lead them through as many of the embers as they can, recasting [[Blaze Shield]] if necessary. For more information how [[Blaze Shield]] functions, see [[Ninja#Blaze Shield and Mobbing]].
[[File:MagicNinjaPlaystyle0.gif|MagicNinjaPlaystyle0.gif|450px]]
''A solo magic ninja kills a group of Stings using [[Blaze Shield]]''
With their fast casting, no ACD spells like [[Flaming Petals]], [[Wind Blade]] and [[Freezing Spear]], ninjas can kill passive or slow-moving enemies at a distance before being reached by them. For [[Freezing Spear]] specifically, the highest rank of the spell is used, followed by chain casts of either rank 1 or of the highest known rank depending on total DEX (>85 DEX only).
[[File:MagicNinjaPlaystyle1.gif|MagicNinjaPlaystyle1.gif|450px]]
''A magic ninja chain casts [[Freezing Spear]] to fell a Goat''
At higher levels (with higher DEX), magic ninja can leverage the slow from [[Watery Evasion]] to fire off [[First Wind]] casts at [[Wind]]-vulnerable/neutral enemies. Similar to other methods of mobbing, the ninja gathers enemies while protected with [[Cicada Skin Shed]] before dispatching them.
[[File:MagicNinjaPlaystyle2.gif|MagicNinjaPlaystyle2.gif|450px]]
''A magic ninja uses [[First Wind]] on a group of Anolian slowed by [[Watery Evasion]]''
'''Party'''
Magic Ninja generally do best in guild dungeon static parties (especially Prontera Guild Dungeon) or moving parties in very specific maps like Ice Dungeon. Magic ninja can have a hard time maintaining their SP pool in walking parties. Even with [[Blessing]] and [[Magnificat]] active, skills like [[Exploding Dragon]] and [[First Wind]] can drain SP very quickly while buffed with [[A Poem of Bragi]]. To help manage SP while in these parties, don't use these skills to kill single targets even though they may be more DPS, instead use "tier 1" magic spells like [[Flaming Petals]] or [[Wind Blade]] at their highest learned rank to save on SP. In guild dungeon static parties, magic ninja can either serve a typical damage dealing role where they stay inside [[Storm Gust]] with most other party members and use AoE spells, or a special role in parties where they are the sole damage dealer. In Prontera Guild Dungeon for example, 1 or 2 magic ninja use [[Blaze Shield]] and [[Exploding Dragon]] to fell groups of monsters brought to them by mobbers while protected by their [[Cicada Skin Shed]].
[[File:MagicNinjaPlaystyle3.gif|MagicNinjaPlaystyle3.gif|450px]]

|} {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Skill Overview | ''The following covers skills that may not be straight forward picks, and provides context to help aspiring magic ninja make decisions regarding their build.'' *[[Flip Tatami]]: Though the aftercast delay is somewhat of a hinderance, this skill can be used to safely kill pesky ranged enemies like Penomena and Gargoyle. With their fast cast speeds, 1 rank of this skill (needed anyways a pre-requisite) is generally sufficient for magic ninja, but it isn't a terrible skill to invest more into if the ninja is planning on hunting in maps with ranged enemies. *[[Mirror Image]]: Its enormous pre-requisite requirements and the rare situations where it is preferable to [[Cicada Skin Shed]] make this a difficult skill to justify investing into for magic ninja. *[[Exploding Dragon]]: Though it is one of the only ninja spells with an aftercast delay, its short cast time (3s) and very high MATK multiplier (900%) make it a very powerful skill, especially in guild dungeon static parties with [[A Poem of Bragi]]. When soloing, this skill can complement [[Blaze Shield]] for mobbing [[Fire]] weak/neutral enemies, but isn't necessary to do so. *[[Freezing Spear]]: Similar to [[Jupitel Thunder]], this skill has a disproportionately stronger rank 1 for its cast time relative to other ranks, and no aftercast delay. Often, it is higher DPS to kill a target spamming rank 1 of this spell than any higher rank to kill a target. There are some cases where higher ranks are more valuable than rank 1. The first is as part of the opening cast on an enemy (E.g., Goats) that is not a cast detector, and the second is at very high levels of DEX only where ASPD is a more significant limiter of its DPS than cast time. *[[Watery Evasion]]: Though impractical until higher levels when a magic ninja can meaningfully reduce its 3 second cast time (~85+ bLvl), this skill can be paired with [[Snow Flake Draft]] for a guaranteed [[Freeze]] effect or to help facilitate [[First Wind]] use while mobbing. *[[Snow Flake Draft]]: This skill has a low damage modifier and is difficult to land on enemies without first being knocked back via [[Cicada Skin Shed]]. However, there is a decent argument to be made for putting at least 1 point into it. The skill has a 100% chance to [[Freeze]] enemies standing on [[Watery Evasion]] cells, for all ranks of the skill, despite its base [[Freeze]] chance scaling with skill level. Its cast time is fastest at lower ranks, and its area of effect is 9x9 ''regardless'' of rank used. *[[Lightning Jolt]]: For the most part, this skill is only taken because 5 points are required as pre-requisite for [[First Wind]]. It has a lower MATK% modifier and is less DPS than [[First Wind]] (which is generally also easier to land on enemies being a targetted skill), but there are a few advantages over [[First Wind]]. [[Lightning Jolt]] is better in static guild dungeons where mobs might not be stacked tightly together after being knocked around by [[Storm Gust]], or generally. It doesn't cost a reagent like [[First Wind]] does and it is more SP-efficient, which matters in walking parties where SP can be an issue for magic ninja. *[[First Wind]]: Though largely considered a DPS tool in parties, this skill is useful for solo mobbing of enemies like Anolians or Fur Seals at higher levels where high DEX allows for getting casts off before being knocked back by [[Cicada Skin Shed]], especially when paired with [[Watery Evasion]]'s slow. It should be noted that currently there is a bug where being knocked back via [[Cicada Skin Shed]] while casting this skill will result in it hitting nothing. *[[Flaming Petals]], [[Wind Blade]]: Unlike [[Freezing Spear]], these skills have a linear progression to their DPS with higher skill ranks. Because magic ninja do not excel at single target DPS, these are seldom taken past what is needed as a pre-requisite. There is at least some merit to investing more than that in these skills, however. [[Wind Blade]] is a more SP-efficient choice in walking parties than [[First Wind]] for killing single targets (E.g., a lone Ice Titan) where SP management is a challenge. [[Flaming Petals]]10 is at least comparable to a [[Sage]] or [[Super Novice]]'s [[Fire Bolt]] when solo and with very high DEX thanks to its lack of an aftercast delay and the absence of any [[Fire]]-type Siroma/Conductring cards. The [[https://tools.payonstories.com/skillV2?state=eJyrVsrKT1KyUvLLzMtKVNJRykktS80pVrKKrlby84oP9nB08Q%2BPD%2FcM8fD0U7IyrNUBC4c4hjj6ero7ugZ7eCJEIYq9Qn0DlKxMoWKhIcGhwa6%2BnggRP0%2B%2FAP9QJStzKN%2FbP9TVz9sRocDb0dUvGGybAUyLqx9IOrYWAI47Mvg%3D following]] could be considered the basic skeleton of a magic ninja's build, with skill choice varying with the remaining 31 skill points. |} === Throwing (AGI) === * STR: 80-90+ * AGI: 90+ (or 50-60)* * VIT: 1+ * INT: 20+ * DEX: 30-50 * LUK: 1 Lightning fast and devastating, AGI thrower ninjas are the picture perfect representation of what comes to mind when one thinks of the word "Ninja". These characters use the extremely rapid [[Throw Shuriken]] as their regular attack, [[Haze Slasher]] for killing groups of enemies and [[Shadow Slash]] as their most effective tool for dispatching high health targets in a single hit. When combining the [[Mirror Image]] skill with their high FLEE, these ninja boast incredible survivability. Properly equipped, an AGI thrower levels extremely fast and is one of the best card farmers in the game. Strength and agility are the AGI thrower's primary attributes. Typically AGI is the more important of the two, as aside from a large jLvl bonus, Ninja do not get any innate boost to their FLEE. Thanks to the large boost to HIT provided by [[Throwing Mastery]], these ninja can get away with having lower DEX than what is normal for physical damage builds. Though [[Ninja Training]] provides a great deal of SP sustain, some amount of INT is needed for AGI throwers, usually in the range of 20+ base INT. An unorthodox, more specialized version of AGI thrower ninja exists that focuses primarily on AoE farming with [[Haze Slasher]]. These ninja invest only a moderate amount into AGI (50-60) and invest more heavily into VIT and INT instead. VIT to increase the efficiency of healing items, and INT to help sustain [[Haze Slasher]] use. A ninja should only build their AGI thrower this way if they have the appropriate gear (Snowier Card/Spring Rabbit Card x 2, % damage reduction cards) and a good idea of specific maps they want to farm with their ninja with this build like Ashes02. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |Build Playstyle | '''Solo'''
AGI thrower gameplay is generally split between [[Throw Shuriken]], [[Haze Slasher]] and [[Shadow Slash]] use. [[Throw Shuriken]] is used when SP is low, or to kill enemies that can't be one-hit by [[Shadow Slash]], [[Haze Slasher]] is used when facing groups of enemies, and [[Shadow Jump]] + [[Shadow Slash]] is used as an SP dump to kill foes in more quickly than [[Throw Shuriken]]. At low levels [[Throw Shuriken]] (or [[Throw Kunai]], if you elect to take it) will be used almost exclusively, but as you get higher and higher in level and unlock the other skills as well as gain higher SP regen via INT and [[Ninja Training]], your skill use will trend more towards [[Haze Slasher]] and [[Shadow Slash]]. Even at high levels, [[Throw Shuriken]] will always see at least some use on a given map. [[Throw Shuriken]] is a special skill which automatically repeats its use similar to an autoattack. This has some caveats, however. * Though it has a 9 cell range, it will often fail to repeat its use when cast at its maximum range. It is recommended to use the skill 7 cells or closer to an enemy to avoid this issue, or be ready to hit the skill again if this happens. * Despite being similar to autoattacks, it is not one. It will not proc equipment or cards which activate on regular attack like [[Corruptor Card]]. * Being a skill, its use is completely prevented by the [[Silence]] status effect. * Despite being a ranged attack, it ''does'' benefit from a [[Bard]]'s ASPD song, and is ''does not'' follow the same "attacks per second" logic that regular attacks do at a given ASPD value. For example, a knight attacking at 190 ASPD (the attack speed cap) deals 5 hits per second, whereas [[Throw Shuriken]] strikes closer to 10 times per second at the same amount of ASPD.

One of two options for killing groups of monsters available to AGI thrower ninjas is the [[Shadow Jump]] + [[Haze Slasher]] + [[Cicada Skin Shed]] combo. Once monsters are gathered up into a tight group, the ninja [[Shadow Jump]]s to them and uses [[Haze Slasher]]. The knockback from [[Cicada Skin Shed]] should trigger, and then this cycle is repeated until the enemy group is dead, all the while refreshing [[Cicada Skin Shed]] every third knockback. This combo only works on non-[[Demon]]/[[Insect]] foes who cannot see through [[Hiding]], and with no ranged attacks (unless you can FLEE them). There is no upper limit as to how many monsters can be killed in a group with this method.

The second option for killing groups of monsters is to spam [[Haze Slasher]], with or without [[Mirror Image]] active. Any AGI thrower can use this method against smaller groups, but for large groups it is more suitable for a specialized higher VIT/INT variant of the build. For large groups, consumables and %reduction equipment is necessary to survive dispatching them. This option kills faster than the [[Shadow Jump]] combo, but has an upper limit on the number of monsters that can be killed in a single group. Unlike the [[Shadow Jump]] combo, this method can be used on any monsters regardless of their race.

The [[Shadow Slash]] skill has dual purpose. Used while in [[Hiding]] via [[Shadow Jump]], it is a very effective tool for killing mid-high HP enemies in a single hit. Used outside of [[Hiding]], it is a superb tool for killing low-mid HP enemies for card or equipment farming. When used for farming, it may be faster to use the skill ''without'' any equipped weapon if their health is low enough to be killed without one as [[Shadow Slash]] is ASPD-based.

[[Angel]] | None | N/A |} ===Magic === Ninjas cannot use staves or books, and so primarily use Asura or Bazerald as these daggers raise their MATK. Of the two, Bazerald is the superior choice but may be too expensive for many. Asura [3] with Drops cards represents the next best thing in a magic ninja's arsenal. In terms of other equipment, magic ninja tend to focus on stacking INT to reach the highest MATK bonus possible. While still important, DEX is of lesser priority for ninja compared to other spell casters as their repertoire of fast casting spells means that DEX gets less value when compared to a job like [[Wizard]]. A Punk carded Hood [1] is a very cheap tool that can help with mobbing, as the [[Quagmire]] 1 effect can trigger even if damage isn't directly taken (i.e., [[Cicada Skin Shed]] is triggered), and can help with mobbing faster groups of enemies with [[Blaze Shield]]. Crown [0] and unslotted Earrings are good first investments for new players providing they haven't already obtained a Vitata and Creamy carded accessory (which can very easily be hunted by magic ninja). {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example budget/starter equipment for Magic Ninja: *Head: Crown [0]/Tiara [0], Geek Glasses, Mr. Scream/Smile *Weapon: Asura [2] *Shield: Arm Guard [0] *Body: Thief Clothes [0] *Garment: Hood [1] (Punk card) *Boots: Shoes [0] *Accessories: Earring [0], Glove [0], Clip [1] (Creamy card, Vitata card) *Pet: Baby Desert Wolf Some example higher-end equipment for Magic Ninja: *Head: Fricca's Circlet, Apple of Archer, Crown [0]/Tiara [0], Crown of Mistress *Weapon: Bazerald, Asura [3] (Drops card x 3) *Shield: Guard [1] (Any racial card), Advanced Arm Guard [1] (Any racial card, Horn card) *Body: Guardian's Robes [1]/Sacred Saint's Robes [1]/Thief Clothes [1] (Baby Desert Wolf Card, any elemental armor card like Bathory), Ninja Suit *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Raydric card, Noxious card, Punk Card) *Boots: Shoes [1] (Kalec card, Living Magma card) *Accessories: Earring [1] (Zerom card), Glove [1] (Zerom card), Earring [0], Shinobi Sash *Pet: Munak, Dokebi, Isis, Kalec, Baby Desert Wolf |} === Throwing (AGI) === Throwing (AGI) Ninjas generally use properly carded Main Gauche [4] to maximize their [[Haze Slasher]] and [[Shadow Slash]] damage. This usually means specific weapons for each area (e.g., 2x peco peco egg + 2x drainliar Main Gauche [4] for killing Siroma) or more generalized weapons (e.g., 4x Drainliar Main Gauche [4]). At least as far as carded Main gauche [4]s are concerned, these ninja share their weapons of choice with DD [[Assassin]]s and [[Shield Boomerang]] [[Crusader]]s. Similar to other melee builds, these ninja aim for ATK-boosting equipment and stack STR to reach the highest (multiple of 10) bonus possible. Flee-boosting cards like whisper or nine tails are also used. The Ninja Suit + Shinobi Sash combo represents a valuable tool for farming easier enemies or reducing downtime. Kamaitachi [0] are a great purchase for new ninja, as it is a higher attack, considerably cheaper elemental dagger compared to blacksmith-made elemental damascus (which are another option). A Poring Dagger is a very affordable weapon with a +20% [[Formless]] damage boost and high weapon ATK. Khukri is another cheap weapon option that boasts a useful effect ([[Curse]] on hit) with high attack. A Main Gauche [4] with 4 Goblin cards represents a good first carded weapon to pursue, as it's relatively cheap, easy to farm and is a solid option for many good targets like Spring Rabbits, Minorous and Ninetails. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example budget/starter equipment for Throwing (AGI) Ninja: *Head: Sakkat, Momoe's Hairband, Mr. Scream/Smile, Geek Glasses *Weapon: Poring Dagger, Kamaitachi, Khukri, VVS elemental damascus, Main Gauche [4] (Goblin card x 4) *Shield: Arm Guard [0] *Body: Pantie *Garment: Undershirt *Boots: Shoes [0], Sandals [1] (Male Thief Bug card) *Accessories: Matyr's Leash, Brooch [0], Ring [0] *Pet: Picky, Drops Some example higher-end equipment for Throwing (AGI) Ninja: *Head: Marionette Doll [1] (Deviruchi card, Cramp card), Magni's Cap, Momoe's Hairband, Hot-Blooded Headband, Ghost Bandana, Crown of Mistress, Evil/Angel Wing Ears, Aggyu Mask, Scouting Scarf *Weapon: Main Gauche [4] (2x2x race/element card, or 4x race/element card) *Shield: Guard [1] (Any racial card), Advanced Arm Guard [1] (Any racial card, Horn card) *Body: Thief Clothes [1] or any slotted armor (Porcellio card), Ninja Suit *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Giant Whisper card, Whisper card), +8 Hood [1] (Nine Tails card) *Boots: Shoes [1] (Firelock Soldier card, Male Thief Bug card, Sohee Card, Matyr Card), +8 Sandals [1] (Spectring card), Fricco's Shoes *Accessories: Ring [1]/Brooch [1] (Mantis, Tarou, Kukre, Spring Rabbit, Snowier), Shinobi Sash *Pet: Orc Warrior, Yser, Earth Petite, Picky |} === Throwing (DEX) === Throwing (DEX) Ninjas primarily use properly carded Huuma Calm Mind [2]s to maximize their [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]] damage. This means specific weapons for each area (e.g., a 2x Peco Peco Egg Huuma Calm Mind [2] for killing Stings). Some DEX throwers opt to use Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] as their weapons of choice so that they can use the same weapon for both [[Shadow Slash]] and [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]]. A Huuma Blaze Shuriken [0] can also be used for its innate [[Fire]] property, high base ATK and high availability. Like their AGI counterparts, Throwing (DEX) ninja should aim to maximize +ATK-boosting equipment and reach as high as possible a strength bonus as they can. Unlike AGI ninjas however, they do not pursue flee-boosting cards like Nine Tails or Whisper. Aside from magic builds, DEX thrower ninja are one of the somewhat cheaper builds and a reasonable choice for a new player who wants to play ninja. The bare minimum for this build to function reasonably well (at level 75+ when you roughly start using [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]]) is to acquire at least one Huuma Calm Mind [2]. These weapons are not expensive, but rarely sold. They drop off Kapha in Amatsu Field 01 at a relatively high rate. 2 Goblin cards or 2 Peco Peco Egg cards are good first choices for carding these weapons, and are relatively easy to farm. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example budget/starter equipment for Throwing (DEX) Ninja: *Head: Sakkat, Kitsune's Mask, Mr. Scream/Smile, Geek Glasses *Weapon: Huuma Calm Mind [2] (Peco Peco Egg card x2, Goblin card x2), Poring Dagger, Kamaitachi, Khukri, VVS elemental damascus *Shield: Arm Guard [0] *Body: Thief Clothes [0] *Garment: Hood [1] (Punk card) *Boots: Shoes [0] *Accessories: Ring [0], Glove [0] *Pet: Picky Some example higher-end equipment for Throwing (DEX) Ninja: *Head: Marionette Doll [1] (Deviruchi card, Cramp card), Magni's Cap, Hot-Blooded Headband, Crown of Mistress, Evil/Angel Wing Ears, Aggyu Mask *Weapon: Huuma Calm Mind [2] (2x race or clement card), Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] (2x2x or 4x race/element cards, for [[Shadow Slash]]) Main Gauche [4] (2x2x or 4x race/element cards, for [[Shadow Slash]] and early-mid leveling with [[Throw Kunai]]) *Shield: N/A *Body: Sacred Saint's Robes [1]/Thief Clothes [1] (Porcellio card), Ninja Suit *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Raydric card, Noxious card) *Boots: Shoes [1] (Firelock Soldier card, Sohee Card) *Accessories: Ring [1] (Mantis, Tarou), Glove [1] (Zerom card), Shinobi Sash *Pet: Orc Warrior, Picky |} === Shadow Slash Critical === Shadow Slash Crit ninja generally use Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] as their primary weapon as huuma avoid size penalties. Consider whether one or more race crit % card like Cruiser card or Assaulter card is going to be needed for your build to reach 50% crit (i.e., 100% crit with [[Shadow's Within]] [[Shadow Slash]]) when deciding on weapons (See: [[#Ninja#Cards_(+%_Crit)]]). To reach this value, Shadow Slash ninja use different combinations of LUK, weapon cards and equipment. The following are ''example'' combinations and are by no means definitive, serving only as a reference. *12% CRIT from gear (Goddess of Cursed Fortune Brooch, Yoyo Pet, Ruby Pumps) + 14% CRIT from weapon cards + 71 LUK *15% CRIT from gear (Goddess of Cursed Fortune Brooch, Yoyo Pet, Ruby Pumps) + 7% CRIT from weapon cards + 84 LUK *17% CRIT from gear (+9 Green Maiden Hood [1], Ring of the Claw, Yoyo Pet, Ruby Pumps) + 7% CRIT from weapon cards + 78 LUK ''(LUK refers to base values)'' One unusual thing that shadow slash ninja share in common with SB [[Assassin]]s and MvP Rifle [[Gunslinger]]s is their potential use of the Goddess of Cursed Fortune Brooch accessories. These three builds are the only CRIT-based characters that generally use these accessories, as being skill-based builds their rate of attacks is very slow, and the probability of being [[Curse]]d by the accessory much lower. Regardless, any ninja wanting to make use of this accessory should carry some Holy Water with them, just in case. As mentioned in the [[Ninja#Shadow_Slash_Critical]] section, it isn't recommended to make these type of ninja without already being an established player with the necessary equipment. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example equipment for Shadow Slash Critical Ninjas: *Head: Marionette Doll [1] (Deviruchi card, Cramp card), Magni's Cap, Momoe's Hairband, Hot-Blooded Headband, Evil/Angel Wing Ears, Aggyu Mask *Weapon: Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] (Combination of crit%race and race cards, see [[Ninja#Cards_(+%_Crit)]]), Main Gauche [4] (2x2x or 4x race/element cards, for early-mid leveling with [[Throw Kunai]]), Gladius [3] (3x race or element cards, for early-mid leveling with [[Throw Kunai]]) *Shield: None *Body: Thief Clothes [1] or any slotted armor (Porcellio card) *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Giant Whisper card, Raydric Card), +8/9 Hood [1] (Green Maiden aka CHUNG-E card) *Boots: Ruby Pumps, Crystal Pumps, Shoes [1] (Firelock Soldier Card, Sohee Card) *Accessories: Ring [1]/Rosary [1] (Mantis, Tarou, Kobold), Ring of the Claw *Pet: Yoyo, Lunatic |} === Killing Stroke === Because weapon damage is irrelevant (but [[Killing Stroke]] benefits from +% cards), a properly carded Main Gauche [4] is typically used (Usually 2x2x race/element for monsters, or 2x2x race/size for PvP/WoE). These Ninja use an unusual assortment of equipment because they don't care about the ATK stat, but still benefit greatly from STR. The formula for [[Killing Stroke]] is "(STR*40) + (HP*80%)", so their equipment aims to maximize STR and maxHP ''without'' the typical focus of hitting multiples of 10 for STR. [[Ninja Training]] ticks every 5 seconds while standing/sitting. ''Standing'' only means when the ninja isn't actively walking, i.e., movement produced from skills like [[Shadow Jump]], [[Shadow Slash]] and [[Cicada Skin Shed]] does not interrupt ticks from this skill, nor does using fly wings or teleport. That means the best way to maximize SP recovery from the passive skill is try and walk as little as possible. Leveling on a map by using fly wings or teleport is especially advantageous for ninja. Try to avoid little bits of movement between skills like [[Throw Kunai]] or [[Throw Shuriken]] if you're in the habit of staggering movement on other classes. To further aid in SP management, ninja and [[Thief]] classes can use the Ninja Suit (Shinobi 0.03% drop) + Shinobi Sash (Shinobi 0.03% drop, also obtained from old blue box/old purple box by low chance) combo to reduce SP consumption by 20%. It's also typical for non-magic ninja classes to also get at least 21 base INT for their final build. 21 base INT adds up to 36 total with job bonuses + [[Ninja Aura]], which is a multiple of 6 ''and'' brings MaxSP to ~700 for the purposes of increasing SP regen (every 100 MaxSP = 1 extra regen). Finally, when killing targets with [[Shadow's Within]] [[Shadow Slash]], consider that all SP regeneration including [[Ninja Training]] ticks is '''halted''' when in the [[Hiding]] status from something like [[Shadow Jump]]. waiting ~1 second after each [[Shadow Slash]] is best practice for accommodating the 3 second delay from [[Shadow's Within]]. ===Sight Shadow Jump=== Normally the [[Shadow Jump]] skill enters the ninja into [[Hiding]] status upon use. However, if the [[Sight]] spell is active (from any accessory with a Horong Card) then the [[Hiding]] status is immediately cancelled, allowing the ninja to repeatedly teleport around with [[Shadow Jump]]. Aside from just rapid movement, this is useful for mobbing, leading enemies into [[Blaze Shield]] cells (especially fast enemies), and for hopping over enemies in narrow spaces without getting hit. [[File:SightJump_Demonstration4.gif|center|SightJump_Demonstration4.gif]] ===Blaze Shield and Mobbing=== [[Blaze Shield]] functions differently depending on whether multiple targets are hit by it. When two or more enemies are inside the spell's area, the skill changes to where any target hit produces a 3x3 AoE (50% MATK) at 3x the number of hits consumed per ember. Put another way, if one enemy inside a lvl 10 Blaze Shield would be hit 9 times per ember, 5 enemies inside a lvl 10 Blaze Shield would get hit 3 times per ember.
[[File:BSDemo3.gif|BSDemo3.gif]] [[File:BSD21.gif|BSD21.gif]]
A magic ninja should aim to gather mobs of enemies into as tight a stack as they can before dragging them into the [[Blaze Shield]].
[[File:BSDemo5.gif|center|BSDemo5.gif]]
Allowing them to capitalize on the small 3x3 AoE each target entering the spell produces.
===How to Use the Calculator For Ninja Skills=== Being able to determine what stats/equipment you need to one shot or two shot something is important for leveling or farming as any class. Unfortunately for ninja, none of the stat calculators available are accurate for the majority of our skills given the extent of the changes on Payon Stories. Thankfully there's a fairly easy workaround. Using the PS stat calculator [https://payonrocalc.jaludev.com/ here], ninja can use the ''Basic Attack'' damage figure to calculate the damage of skills like [[Shadow Slash]] and [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]]. Some examples...
[[File:Ninjagptips2.png|thumb|Multiply minimum damage by 9.5 to get [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]] minimum damage]]
[[File:Ninjagptips1.png|thumb|Multiply critical damage by 8, to get [[Shadow Slash]] crit damage]]
[[File:Ninjagptips3.png|thumb|Multiply minimum damage by 3 to get [[Throw Kunai]] minimum damage]]
Note that some monsters in the calculator have different maxHP values than in-game (E.g., Merman). ==Overview==
The '''Novice''' is the starting point for all characters in Ragnarok Online. When you create a new character, you may choose from different Hairstyles and Hair colors. Novices do not incur any EXP penalty upon death, and regain 50% HP when respawning. You may also choose which starting Stats to have. Once Job Level 10, Novices can change into one of the following First Classes:
* [[Swordman]]
* [[Magician]]
* [[Archer]]
* [[Merchant]]
* [[Thief]]
* [[Acolyte]]

Alternatively, they can choose to become an Expanded Class:
* [[Super Novice]]

==Training Grounds==
1. Talk to the '''Shion''', the very first NPC where you spawn. Talk to her '''twice''' to gain +1 base level.

2. Talk to the '''Receptionist''' inside the building, type your character's name then choose ''Apply for training''.

3. Talk to the '''Interfaces Tutor'''. Choose first option until levels are gained.

4. Talk to the '''Item Tutor''', when asked to use [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=569 Novice Potion], '''use it''' for +1 Base Level. When asked to equip [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=2414 Novice Slippers], '''equip it''' for +1 base level.

5. Talk to the '''Kafra Employee'''. Choose ''About Kafra services'' then read the first two options for levels.

6. Talk to the '''Skill Tutor'''. He will give you some experience and teach you the First Aid Skill.

7. Go to the left room and talk to '''Helper''', the left NPC in the combat field room.

8. Talk to the '''Entrance Guard''', the right NPC in the combat field room to warp you to the training field.

9. Here in the Training Field, it is your choice on what monster to kill to gain experience. For access to higher difficulty monsters in the training field, talk to the '''Trainer''' and choose "''I do want more of a challenge~''" or "''I wanna fight tough monsters!''"

*'''Note''': You have the option to die to a random monster or use a [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=12324 Novice Butterfly Wing] in order to go back to the combat field room and gain +1 base level by talking to the '''Entrance Guard''' again.

10. Kill monsters until Job Level 10 or until satisfied then head to the '''Test Examiner''' NPC on the rightmost part of the map to go to the next room.

*'''Note''': Talk to the '''Stat Specialist''' NPC to reset your stat points if necessary.

11. Talk to '''Bruce''' for a quick First Job Class Explanation. Go through any option you want once.

12. Talk to '''Hanson''' and choose if you want to take the Novice Personality Test by choosing the option, "''I'll take the course.''" or going straight to town by choosing the option, "''Let me start Ragnarok Online please.''"

*'''Note''': It is advisable to take the Novice Personality Test for starter gear based on the job that you will get from the test.

Party:
== Overview ==
Parties are small groups of players (maximum of 12) for the purpose of easier leveling and companionship. To create a party, use the /organize "Name" command. You must have the [[Novice]] [[Basic Skill]] level 7 to create a party. Players can join a party at any level. The person who creates the party becomes the Party Leader. The Party Leader can remotely invite people to the party (they don't have to be on the same screen or even the same map) using the ''/invite'' command. (Usage: /invite "<name>")

== Setup Options ==
=== Item Setup ===
Item setup can '''only''' be set when the party is created. If you want to change this, the party will have to be remade.       

*Each Take - Items can be picked up first by the person that killed the monster.
*Party Share - Items can be equally picked up by all party members.
*Individual - Items picked up go to the person that picked it up.
*Shared - Items picked up randomly go to one of the party members.

=== Experience Setup ===
'''EXP Bonus has been changed''' here, for more information look here:

https://tools.payonstories.com/party_exp?m=80%2C80
[[File:Image32.png|left|thumb]]                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                        

[[Experience]] setup can be changed at any time (as long as the party leader is on and all online members are within '''15''' [[Base Level]]s).       

*'''Each Take''' - Party members only gain EXP for monsters they do damage to.
*'''Even Share''' - Party members share EXP. I.E if a [[wizard]] is sharing with a [[Priest]] and [[Monk]], the experience gained by the monsters killed by all three will be equally distributed between the three of them. Only people within 15 Base Levels of each other can share (Example: Level 75, Level 89, Level 81 could share with each other // if you are alone and looking for a party, you basically can look for people within range of 30 because 15 level down and 15 level up)

## <:sitting_down:1534910606539493586> Merchant Changes

- Adrenaline Rush has a similar effect to Full Adrenaline Rush;
- Blacksmith buff duration normalized to 60/120/180/240/300 seconds;
- New tools for auto attacker builds, cart revolution builds, and forging
builds.
## <:smug_sip:1534850429954031646> Alchemist Changes
- Increased flexibility in Chemical Protection skill allocation;
- Expanded Brewer viability in active combat;
- Simplified and strengthened AGI/INT scaling for plants;
- Improved the foundation of magic-oriented autocast builds;
- Introduced unique effects to pitched potions.
## <:this_is_fine:1533890478791987280> New Status Effect: Burning
- Burning has a single duration of 5 seconds;
- Burning can stack up to 5 levels;
- Each level applies:
  - 60 Fire (magic) damage per second;
  - -2 MDEF per stack.
- Applying Burning:
  - Increases the stack level by 1 (up to 5);
  - Resets duration to 5 seconds;
  - Does not interrupt or delay damage ticks.
- Burning does not maintain separate timers per stack, only the current stack level;
- Damage is treated as Magic Fire Damage, and as such it is mitigated by the usual Fire Resistance, MDEF, INT, Armor Element, etc.

Patch Note - 14 Aug 2024:
<markdown>
@Payon News 
There are some confusion on buff related to Sage land skills, here's how it works

**Violent Gale/Deluge/Volcano usage:**

The land skills buff doesn't increase the final damage, but increases the elemental modifier.
Element modifiers can be viewed here: https://irowiki.org/classic/Element

So let's consider an example of 20% is added to element modifiers with the buff:
1. Attacking Undead 4 with Holy is 200% element modifiers, with 20% buff, it will be 220%, i.e final damage is increased by 10% 

2. Attacking Undead 4 with earth is 50% element modifiers, with 20% buff, the modifier will become 70%, i.e.40% damage is increased.

3. Attacking Shadow 4 with Water element has 25% element modifiers, with the buff, it will be increased by 20%, i.e to 45%, which is ~80% increase in damage.
</markdown>

Following changes are now live after today’s maintenance:
* **Brandish Spear** adjustments(More consistent now) [Try it yourself] - Thanks to @alardun & @ocatamai for fixing it's behavior.
  * **No longer hit twice** under certain **nebulous circumstance**.
  * Now **hits twice** when affected targets would **collide in a unmovable cell** after a movement of at least 1 cell.
  * **Diagonal **now hits reliably.
  * **Affected range** no longer follows and center on the target. It is now always starting from the knight, from **4 tiles in front toward the target** (Minus the edges for the front-most row) to 1 tile behind the knight (+1 in case of diagonals)). 
  * ** The skill has a grace range given to it. If the target is out of the AoE at lower level (cast range in straight cardinal direction), the range is extended up to the level 10 range as needs be, although, if it benefits from this, the AoE of the max-range hit is 1x1 instead of 3x1 (Level 10 extra row) or 5x1 (Every other)
  * **Pushback is always toward the target**, regardless of whoever being affected location in relation to the knight.
  * All of these changes means the skill fares poorly versus ranged monster, since you now hit them at the sourspot if you don't manually move up close, and they're unlikely to get off the wall to allow further collision. Priorize other skills versus ranged foes.

   * ACD normalized to 1s at all level.

   * Now requires Martial Arts 5 instead of Dodge 5.

   * Damage ratio changed to 200 + 60 *SkillLvl. (was: 160 + 80 * SkillLvl)

   * Can now be casted instantly after Triple Attack triggers, cancelling the Combo.

   * ACD changed to 1s (was: 2s).

   * Now immune to pushback while casting.
   * SP Cost changed to 30+6*SkillLv (was: 30+7*SkillLv).

   * No longer grants Critical Hit

**Mob Refresh Logic:**

Most of the maps are filled with monsters. There's a mechanic in-game called "dynamic mobs" or "mob refresh"

Here’s how it works: If no one has been there on a map for 10 minutes, the game automatically gets rid of those monsters [i.e mobs are removed from the map]. This system is only applicable for non-damaged monsters. This helps keep the game running smoothly and ensures that monsters will reappear when new players come along or when someone returns to the map.

With the new change, the condition is revised to exclude auto-traders from "active user" count. Traders without @at still counts towards the active user on map.

Payon Undertombs:
=[[Dungeon]]=
The Payon Undertombs can be located in Payon at (oldnewpayon 70, 169).

[[File:Payon Undertombs Location.png|border]]

Between the Payon and the Dungeon is the Undertombs Lobby, which serves as the Hub for Undertomb-related quests.
=Reputation=
You can gain favor with the Payon Vanguard by completing various tasks, which is measured in '''Reputation'''. Once you reach certain thresholds, you will gain access to unique items only available through this system.

You can check your current Reputation and obtain rewards by speaking to the '''Quartermaster'''  (untomb_01 48, 35) in the Undertombs Lobby after you have completed the 1F & 2F Entrance Quest.

'''Note:''' Reputation is '''not shared between characters'''.

===Gaining Reputation===
Reputation gained be gained via the following methods: 

*Finishing quests in the '''Main Questline''' as well as '''Side Quests''' (not repeatable)
*Finishing '''Daily Quests''' available from '''Yanni Jeong'''  in the Undertombs Lobby ('''500 Reputation''' each clear)
*Turning in '''Ancient Urns''' to '''Serah Erun'''  in the Undertombs Lobby ('''150 Reputation''' for each Urn)

=== Reputation Thresholds ===
The Reputation thresholds are as follows:

*'''Known''' (200 - 4,999)
*'''Friendly''' (5,000 - 9,999)
*'''Praised''' (10,000 - 14,999)
*'''Revered''' (15,000 - 19,999)
*'''Deified''' (20,000)

=== Reputation Rewards ===

= Main Questline =

=== 1F & 2F Entrance Quest ===
1. Speak with '''Guard Yang''' (untomb_01 32, 49)
in the Undertombs lobby. He will require you to speak with the Chief of Payon for permission to access the Undertombs ('''"Seeking Permission"''' quest).

2. Check your Zombie kill count (@killcount 1015). If you have killed at least 1 Zombie, proceed to the next step. Otherwise, kill 1 Zombie in Payon Dungeon F1.

3. Head to the '''Chief of Payon''' in Payon Castle (payon_in01 137, 143)
(walk up the main pathway into the main castle entrance. Follow the hallway 1 portal into the 2nd main room, then turn right). '''Tell him about your Zombie kills'''. He will grant you access to the Undertombs. Note that this will also work with Raydrics, but Zombies are obviously easier. The Poring option will only work if you never killed a poring before. [[File:Chief of Payon.png|none|thumb]]

4. Head back to '''Guard Yang''' (untomb_01 32, 49) in the Undertombs lobby, who will grant you access to the Undertombs ('''"Return to Guard Yang"''' quest) as well as give you '''200 Reputation'''.

===3F (Mortal Realm) Entrance Quest===
1. Talk to '''Subchief Olen'''(untomb_01 37, 46) in the Undertombs lobby.

2. '''Kill 50 Ninetails''' and '''collect 25 Dokebi Horns''' (called "Dokkaebi Horns" ingame) in Payon Dungeon F5 ('''"Believe It!"''' quest).

3. Return to '''Subchief Olen''' (untomb_01 37, 46) in the Undertombs lobby, who will reward you with '''25 Light White Potions''' and '''500 Reputation''', then ask you to find the Broken Mechanism in order to open      the Stone Door that leads deeper into the Undertombs ('''"Mechanisms"''' quest)

4. Head to Undertombs 2F and search through the '''Dirt Mounds''' in order to find the '''Broken Mechanism'''. The item will be in one of four Dirt Mounds: 

* At the base of the stairs near the top right portal (untomb_03 125, 124):
[[File:Undertombs 2F Dirt Mound 4.png|none|thumb]]
*In a prison cell near the bottom right of the map (untomb_03 162, 20):
[[File:Undertombs 2F Dirt Mound 1.png|none|thumb]]
*In a junk pile near the bottom left of the map (untomb_03 26, 42):
[[File:Undertombs 2F Dirt Mound 2.png|none|thumb]]
*In the pond in the middle of the beach area (untomb_03 68, 141):
[[File:Undertombs 2F Dirt Mound 3.png|none|thumb]]
5. Head to '''Antonio''' at the '''Payon Blacksmith Shop''' (payon_in01 91, 31) (the gear refiner) who will repair the mechanism for you. You will obtain the '''Repaired Tomb Mechanism''' as well as '''500 Reputation'''.

6. Bring the '''Repaired Broken Mechanism''' to '''Undertombs 2F''' (untomb_03 93, 98). Click the Lever to attach it and open the Stone Door. Once you do, you will have access to Undertombs 3F and gain '''250 Reputation'''.
===3F (Spirit Realm) Entrance Quest===
1. Head to the '''Empress of Payon'''  (untomb_04 31, 42), who is on the map past Undertombs 2F inside the portal near the lever. She refuses to speak to you, so you decide to head back to '''Subchief Olen''' in the Undertombs lobby ('''"The Empress"''' quest).

2. Head to '''Subchief Olen''' (untomb_01 37, 46) in the Undertombs lobby. He will send you to the '''Payon Historian''' ('''"Ancient History"''' quest).

3. Speak to the '''Payon Historian''' (payon_in01 101, 111) in Payon Castle (upon entering the castle from the main entrance, enter the 2nd portal on the left). He will send you to a Waiting Room, where you will be tasked with seeing Payon's past through the Magic Mirror.
[[File:Payon Historian.png|none|thumb]]
4. Enter the Waiting Room (click the chat bubble) and watch the cutscene.

5. Speak to the '''Payon Historian''' (payon_in01 101, 111) one more time to receive '''500 Reputation''' and complete this subquest.

6. Now that you better understand the history of Payon, you must seek a clue to helm you better communicate with the Empress ('''"Sorrow"''' quest). Head to Undertombs 3F and click the '''Odd Flame''' (untomb_05 158, 32) to complete this subquest and receive '''500 Reputation'''.

7. Return to the '''Empress of Payon''' (untomb_04 31, 42) ('''"Grief'''" quest). She will give you the Spirit Medallion and ask you to kill Lady Huo. From this point on, you are now able to use the Spirit Medallion on Undertomb 3F to travel back and forth between the Mortal Realm and the Spirit Realm.

===3F Quest Finale===
1. Head to Undertombs 3F (untomb_05) and use the Spirit Medallion to head to the Realm of Spirit and kill Lady Huo ('''"Spirited Away"''' quest).

2. Return to the '''Empress of Payon''' (untomb_04 31, 42). She will grant you the Ornate Crest. Speak with the '''Payon Historian'''  once more to receive the '''Ring of Peace if and only if this is your the first clear on the account'''. Otherwise, she will reward a '''Clip[1]'''. If she has already given you 3 Clip[1]s, she will instead simply give you a Light White Potion.
