Server Information:
Payon Stories is a Hercules emulated Ragnarok Online server that is meant to create a nostalgic, yet fresh experience for all players. We have created a low-rate server that expands on the hard work of the developers of the Athena and Hercules emulators by enhancing gameplay while staying true to the original design of Ragnarok Online.



Rates: 1.5x/1.5x/1x (lowest drop rate: 0.02%)

Max level: 99/50 99/99SN

Atk Speed cap: 190, Instant cast: 150 dex

Dual logging: NO

Donation: Yes - but only for costume headgears with no effect // @costumeshop ingame

Custom NPCs: Dyer / Stylist / Events (Can turn in Dyestuff for a Stylist Ticket!)

Player commands and server features: https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=main&action=features

==== Server Summary ====
Payon Stories uses a classic RO (pre-transcended classes) foundation for players to start their journey. Our research indicates that most of the major balancing changes occurred between RO’s beta and the Episode 3 release. That said, some balancing changes made in later episodes have been retroactively applied to our initial release for the purpose of providing players with consistency and familiarity in the function of specific items, skills, and cards as seen on other servers.

Nevertheless, we have considered key gameplay features when developing Payon Stories that we determined were necessary to balance and/or enhance gameplay and player experience. Such changes and considerations include:

* A rework of the entire mob database’s base and job experience tables to add competitiveness of the benefit of killing mobs.
* A rework of the HP and attack of mobs to add competitiveness of the benefit of killing mobs.
* Changes to the spawn rates and locations of certain mobs.
* Modifications to some skills to make specific builds more competitive and viable, adding more variety to the game.
* Drop rates of specific items that are unnecessarily difficult to obtain that are used for quests to encourage NPC interaction and pave the way for an expanded quest system.
* Additions of informational and flavor NPCs to make the game world feel “full” of actual meaningful NPCs that have value-added interactions with players.
* Substantial rework of official NPC text for clarity and grammar (it goes without saying the people who originally translated everything did a great job, but we just want to take their work one step further).

Our staff will continue to make changes to improve the game. We plan to continually polish the text you read in-game and balance the core mechanics of gameplay to adhere to our mission.

== Finding the quest giver ==
First step is talking to Ancient sage in pay_dun03, around 117, 67

== Trial of Strength ==
In this part of the quest you will be required to kill 20 of each type of minion of the first map and 10 of the brown colored minions on the second map. All minions are nonaggressive. 

=== First map minions ===
First type of minion uses firewall and can turn player undead for a short duration. They are demon/dark3 and require 84 hit for 100% chance.

MonsterID: [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=monster&action=view&id=25535 25535]

[[File:Minion1.png|frameless]]

Second type of minion uses soul strike. When not engaged it will often hide and use grimtooth aggressively. They are demon/dark3 and require 87 hit for 100% chance.

MonsterID: [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=monster&action=view&id=25534 25534]

[[File:Minion2.png|frameless]]

=== Second map minions ===
Second map has blue and brown minions, but only brown minions are counted towards the quest progress.

This type uses Thunderstorm and decrease agility. They are angel/holy2 and require 80 hit for 100% chance.

MonsterID: [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=monster&action=view&id=25536 25536]

== Confront the Shadow Lord ==
After talking to the Ancient Sage one more time you will be teleported to another map for the encounter with Shadow Lord himself.

Shadow Lord is a modified Shinobi with 55% extra HP. Shadow lord is demi-human/dark3 and requires 94 hit for 100% chance.

Notable abilities are Teleport, Cloaking, Rebirth and Claymore Trap. There are also all types of his minions, but since they are nonaggressive they can be ignored. The map can get crowded, so you will have to be careful not to agro any minions and avoid all of the hidden minions with grimtooth. Due to higher HP of Shadow Lord, some consumables would be helpful, but since he doesn't see thru hiding and is the only aggressive monster on the map, you can safely disengage him and regenerate.

== Hit versus Accuracy ==
Sonic Acceleration does not give a flat +50 [[Hit]]. If your status window Hit is 100, using [[Sonic Blow]] while having SA will not increase it to 150. SA gives +50% "Hit", the Hit actually being Accuracy rate. Accuracy rate is the final percentage the game calculates after counting in the player's Hit Rate and Enemy's Flee Rate. If the player's Hit was 100 and the enemy's Flee is 150, the Accuracy rate is 30%. When the player uses Sonic Blow, Sonic Acceleration increases that 30% chance to 45%.

== Description ==

Summons a Marine Sphere with a custom HP formula. After being hit, it starts a 5-second countdown and moves 7 cells away from the attacker. When the countdown reaches 0, it explodes and inflicts damage to any enemies equal to its remaining HP. You cannot summon more than 3 spheres in a 9x9 area. The Maximum HP is based on your skill level, and when used in WoE, the defense value of the castle will raise the defense of the Sphere.

== Notes ==
*The damage from Sphere Mine ignores DEF, and is [[Fire]] element.
*The damage from Sphere Mine is not affected by weapon size penalties. 
*The original damage formula is 2000 + 400 * SkillLV and the skill costs 1 Marine Sphere Bottle.
*New Damage formula: 1000 + 200 * SkillLv + 25 * Total VIT
**Marine Sphere Bottle cost removed.
**Cooldown after cast increased to 0.5 seconds.
**The summoned Marine Sphere is Water 3 property.
A new platinum skill [[Remote Detonator]] immediately detonates all of your summoned Marine Spheres wherever they happen to be. Being Water 3 allows [[Demonstration]] to launch Spheres without dealing any damage to their HP.

The countdown launch depends on the sphere being within melee range (2 cells) of the Alchemist. The Alchemist and other players can target and damage a sphere outside that range without causing a launch. If there are less than 7 cells of open ground away from the Alchemist for the Sphere to move through, it can start its countdown but will not move. There used to be an exploit where Alchemist players would hold a Moonlight Sword and drop a Demonstration (or two) on a trio of Spheres and walk away.

Due to the way knockback works, if you detonate improperly stacked Spheres with Remote Detonator, enemies will only be damaged by one explosion. They essentially kick targets outside of each other's Area of Effect. You have to wait for targets to slip in between the Spheres. With practice all 3 can be made to hit at once.

St. Patrick Event:
The gold coins of Luck o' the Leprechaun were stolen by mischievous fairies while he was drunk, and they were scattered across Midgard along with other treasures. To aid in the recovery of his stolen treasure, magical treasure chests will appear in towns or fields every odd hour, but only magical creatures can see them, like Luck o' the Leprechaun. Anyone who finds Luck o's gold coins can decide to keep them or continue searching for more. 

The event can be initiated by meeting Luck o' Leprechaun at aldebaran, where he will provide a magical hat that allows you to touch the magical treasure chests. The treasure chests will disappear if left unattended for too long and only appear during odd hours. If the magical hat is lost, Luck o' may provide a replacement. 

Return the gold coins to Luck o' once enough have been collected to receive a reward, which could be "The Luck o' Leprechaun Hat!", "The Green Scarf!", "Give me Green gum in mouth!", "Give me 4Leaf Clover in mouth", or "Give me the Luck o' Pint". 

Rewards: Treasure Chest allows to search deep inside the chest (Tier 1 to Tier 4), however, once you get the coin, you won't be able to change the tier. Be aware, treasure chest can turn into a monster.

Static Party Guide: == On which maps are static parties allowed?== Since January 10 2026, it is only allowed to run static parties on a few specific maps: *gld_dun01 (Payon GD) *gld_dun02 (Alde GD) *gld_dun03 (Prontera GD) *gld_dun04 (Geffen GD) {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" |The original announcement | '''''Devastate — 2026-01-10''''' Hi everyone. Based on player feedback, and to better align the server with our vision of active and engaging gameplay, we have decided to introduce the following change: '''Effective as of this posting, static parties are only allowed on Guild Dungeon PvP maps. Those maps are: gld_dun01 (Payon GD), gld_dun02 (Alde GD), gld_dun03 (Prontera GD), and gld_dun04 (Geffen GD). Static parties are thus banned on all other maps.''' This is a decision we have discussed and debated internally for a long period of time… In the past we have explored ways to reduce the viability of static parties without negatively affecting other players or fundamentally altering maps. However, that limited our design freedom in terms of improving maps as well. With this change, we believe we will enter a new era of creativity and map design. This change also sets the stage for how progression will happen during the upcoming Transcendence patch, as players experience a re-leveling experience that does not include low risk static parties. In the past we have made many map and class enhancements to improve gameplay, and more of that is on the way. Our goal is to be a server that rewards active play and feels distinct within the low-rate server landscape. From the Payon Stories Team: Thank you to everyone who supports and shares our vision, and we are looking forward to the future with you all. |} ==How does exp party sharing work?== Parties are able to set exp to "Exp Shared" when members are within +/- 15 level. Party exp calculated by the following: Even Share: The EXP reward of a monster is split evenly across all party members regardless of their level. *(EXP to be Shared / Number of Party Members) + 1 EXP *EXP to be Shared changes with party size, see [[EXP Rebalance]] for exact values ==Why join static parties?== Static parties are a way to easily and quickly level up by having characters focused on designated roles and have an optimal mob killing set-up. The party is typically parked in one spot (a "static party"), with mobbers luring hordes of mobs into area of effect attacks like firewalls/thunderstorm/storm gust. ==What are the roles in static parties?== The following are the common terms used in the server for static parties: {| class="wikitable" |+ Core Roles !Role Name !Role Description |- |Mobber |Character brings hordes of mobs into the stack |- |FS |“Full Support”. Designates by extension Acolytes and Priests with a Full Support build, looked after for skills such as Heal, Blessing, Increase Agility, Warp Portal, Kyrie Eleison, Magnificat, Resurrection |- |Taxi |Acolyte classes that will warp party members from town to designated map whenever there's a death or needed |- |Kim |Abbreviation for the skill “Mr. Kim A Rich Man”, an ensemble skill for bard + dancer that boost the exp of monsters killed within its aoe. |- | AoE damage | Any character able to quickly kill large amount of enemies with AoE skills, usually wizards. |} ===Acronyms and Jargon=== *'''LFP''' : “Looking for Party”. It’s used by the server-wide #lfp channel, crucial to find parties, in two ways : **'''LFP >''' '''[class] [role] [level]''' for characters looking for a party **'''LFM > [class] [role] [level range]'''” for parties looking for members. Sometimes also written with '''R >''' for "Recruit" *'''Rep''' : “Replacement”. In the duration of a party, some people have to leave, so party leaders are recruiting a “rep”, meaning a replacement for that person’s role. *'''OOP''' : “Out Of Party”. Designated characters that aren’t in the parties but contribute to its efficiency. OOP characters are generally either musicians, for either the support songs (poem of bragi, service for you) or the unique Mr. Kim song, or mobbers for a faster output. Status Effects:
==Bleeding== The Bleeding status effect has been fully reworked on Payon Stories. * Bleeding now causes the target to lose 5% of Max HP every 0.5s for 2.5s → Total: 25% Max HP loss in 2.5 seconds * This damage can kill both monsters and players. * After bleeding ends, the target gains 35 seconds of Bleed immunity. Aside from this immunity Bleed cannot be mitigated, reduced or resisted. * Bleeding cannot be inflicted on targets that are +15 base levels or higher than the attacker. * Bleeding cannot be inflicted on boss protocol targets. * Successful Bleeding application is indicated by a red mist effect on the target. [[File:Bleeding_Red_Mist.png|frameless]] ==Blind== This status ailment causes the following effects: *Reduce your HIT and FLEE rate by 25%. *Also graphically reduces range of your visibility. ==Chaos== Also known as Confusion, causes the character to move into unintended directions when trying to navigate. Chaos has its success rate and duration reduced by STR and INT, with 100 total (in any combination) resulting in immunity to the status effect. E.g., 43 STR and 17 INT = 60% reduced success rate and duration. LUK also plays a role in additive reducing the chance of being afflicted, similar to many status effects. ==Chilled== The Chilled status effect reduces the monster’s movement speed by -40% for 10 seconds. ==Coma== This status ailment causes the following effects: *Reduces afflicted target's HP to 1. *Reduces afflicted target's SP to 0. ==Curse== This status ailment causes the following effects: *Reduce your ATK by 25%. *LUK becomes 0. *Drastically Reduces your Movement Speed. To prevent from infliction: *LUK reduces the % chance of being afflicted by 1% per point **This attribute confers immunity at both 100 ''and'' 0 total LUK (due to how the status effect is written in the code) *VIT reduces the duration by an (unknown) percentage per point. At 100 total VIT, the duration of curse becomes almost imperceptibly short. *The Evil Snake Lord Card grants immunity to curse. ==Divest== The player can not reequip any items into a given equipment slot, depending on which one was targeted. To prevent from infliction: *High DEX lowers chance. *Protection skills of Alchemists grant immunity. ==Frozen== This status ailment causes the following effects: *All DEF contributed by items reduced by 50%. *Monsters Hard-DEF and Soft-DEF is reduced by 50% (round up). *Any flee will be negated. *Increases your Hard-MDEF by 25%. *Ignores Steal, Lex Aeterna, Wizard's skill - Storm Gust, Ninja's skill - Snow Flake Draft. *Impossible to move, attack, pick up items, skill usage, sitting, force disconnection, and item usage. *Armor attribute becomes "Water 1". (175% damage from Wind based attacks, 25% damage from Water, 50% damage from Fire). ==Hypothermia== This status causes the following effects: *-20% movement speed (does ''not'' stack with [[Quagmire]]'s or any other slow effect) *-20% attack speed *+20% longer cast time (players only) *-10 DEX (stacks with [[Quagmire]]'s DEX reduction) Hypothermia lasts 10 seconds. It cannot be resisted/reduced by any attributes. Card effects: * Frost Lich Card - Grants immunity to the hypothermia status effect. ==Mailbreak== This status causes the following effect: *10% more damage taken from all sources for '''10 seconds, or up to 7 hits, whichever occurs first''' Mailbreak can be applied by an [[Assassin]]'s [[Venom Dust]], a [[Blacksmith]]'s [[Hammer Fall]], a [[Rogue]]'s [[Raid]] or via the Mailbreaker weapon. There is no way to obtain immunity to the Mailbreak effect. Bosses are not immune to Mailbreak. ==Poison== This status causes the following effects: *Defence gained from VIT is reduced by 50% (server specific change, up from 25%) *HP is reduced by 2% per second (server specific change, up from 1%/sec) *SP regeneration is disabled
Developer Comment: Poison as a status was not very detrimental and was easily countered in PVP due to Green Potions and Herbs. While the curing methods are unchanged, the detrimental effects of poison will make it a higher priority to counter in PVP/GVG settings. More importantly, the PVE setting is improved by giving those who inflict poison the ability to dispatch mobs faster.
To remove this status effect use: *Green Herb, Green Potion, Panacea, Royal Jelly, Thief's skill - [[Detoxify]] can undo the effect. *Having high VIT and LUK will reduce amount of time this ailment affects you, as well as chance of being affected. *Priest's [[Renew]] prevents damage taken from poison but does not cure the reduced DEF effect.
Card effects: *Argiope Card grants Poison element, and immunity to Poison attacks, but not the poison status itself. *Ghoul Card increases resistance to poison by 20%. *Poporing Card allows use of [[Detoxify]]. *Venomous Card has a 30% chance of inflicting poison to self and a 30% chance of inflicting poison on the attacker when receiving physical damage. *Zenorc Card has a 4% of inflicting poison status to an enemy when attacking.
Equipments: *Gas Mask increases resistance by 30%. *Oxygen Mask increases resistance by 20%. ==Silence== Inability to use any active skills. ==Sleep== This status ailment causes the following effects: *Impossible to move, attack, pick up items, skill usage, sitting, force disconnection, and item usage. *If enemy attacks you, you will always get hit. *If enemy attacks you, they will have 2x CRIT chance with their attack. *Can be resisted with high INT ==Stone== This is a two stage status. 1st stage prevents player from attacking and use of skills. After a short time player turns into stone (2nd stage). 2nd stage has additional effects: *All DEF contributed by items is reduced by 50%. *Monsters Hard-DEF and Soft-DEF is reduced by 50% (round up). *Increases your MDEF by 25%. *Changes your elemental status as "Earth LV 1" *Ignores Steal and Lex Aeterna, although due to custom change if Lex Aeterna was applied in 1st stage it will not be cleared by entering 2nd stage *Impossible to move, attack, pick up items, skill usage, sitting, force disconnection, and item usage. ==Slow== * Reduces the target's movement speed by a given % (''This value differs depending on the source of the slow''). * Some sources of Slow also remove ASPD increasing buff effects and [[Increase AGI]]. Slow Sources: * [[Spear Stab]], [[Quagmire]], [[Frost Nova]], [[Gunslinger]]'s Sticky Grenade, [[Freezing Trap]] when the Rust-Worn Apparatus is equipped, [[Watery Evasion]], [[Slow Grace]], [[Decrease AGI]] ==Stun== This status ailment causes the following effects: *Any flee will be negated. *Impossible to move, attack, pick up items, skill usage, sitting, force disconnection, and item usage. ==Undead== This status ailment causes the following effect: *The player become Undead property. *Support buffs such as Blessing and Increase AGI are removed. *Support buffs such as Blessing and Increase AGI deal damage to the player and the buffs are not applied, even in PVM. They will do 1 damage, but cannot be copied by the Rogue class using Intimidate *Heal and Sanctuary have no effect on the player in PvM *Aspersio will deal damage to the player and can be copied by Rogue's Intimidate *The ailment causes the player's sprite to glow green.

Steal:
{{Skill Info | class = Thief | class2 = Super Novice | class3 = | type = Active | levels = 10 (Fixed) | prereqs = None | quest = | spcost = 10 | hpcost = | time = None | delay = 1 second | duration = | target = Monsters | range = Melee | area = | knock = | element = | status = | catalyst = | cf_name = | cf_value = }} == Description == Attempts to "steal" an item from the targeted [[monster]]. Only items dropped by the monster can be stolen. A successful attempt will not affect what is dropped when the monster dies. After success, it is not possible to Steal again from the same monster. [[Boss]]-protocol monsters cannot be stolen from. Cards can never be stolen. === How Steal Works === Each monster has their own drop table. As an example: {| class="wikitable" |+ !Item !Drop Ratio |- |Skull |70% |- |Brigan |70% |- |Oridecon |30% |- |Elunium |30% |- |Chain Mail |25% |- |Silk Robe |25% |- |Elemental Sword |0.02% |} When Steal is triggered, a roll happens sequentially from top-down. For each item, if the attempt fails, a subsequent roll will happen for the next item on the table. The ramification for this is that if you want to steal higher rarity items like Elemental Sword in the example above, you will have to fail Steal attempt rolls on all the items prior to it on the drop table. The formula for stealing is: 
(playerDEX - mobDEX)/2 + ((stealLvl * 6) + 4)
You can think of the steal "success chance" as more of a rate modifier. For example, for a player with steal 10 and 71 dex vs Kapha with 73 dex... 
(71 - 73)/2 + (10*6) + 4) 
-1 + 64 = 63%.
You then times the drop rate by that: Yellow plate 65.01 * 0.63 = 41% chance to steal. Success = steal and finish, fail = check next item. {| class="wikitable" !Skill Level || Success Chance |- |1 || 10% |- |2 || 16% |- |3 || 22% |- |4 || 28% |- |5 || 34% |- |6 || 40% |- |7 || 46% |- |8 || 52% |- |9 || 58% |- |10 || 64% |} == See Also == * [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1GXbyv8D3TPf0w6O3TVwMn09FmJO9JJW0raC49jXDUis/edit?gid=0#gid=0 Steal % by DEX for notable monsters spreadsheet] * https://tools.payonstories.com/steal {{Navbox Thief}} {{Navbox SuperNovice}}

Summons a devastating blizzard that strikes a targeted area, dealing [[Water]] damage for up to 10 hits and pushing enemies struck up and to the right. Enemies hit 3 times by Storm Gust may freeze depending on their [[MDEF]] (see below), but boss and undead enemies cannot be frozen. [[Frozen]] enemies cannot be hit by Storm Gust.

== Notes ==
*A target struck by Storm Gust a 3rd time has a 150% chance to be frozen. For most targets, this guarantees they are frozen. However, targets with sufficiently high [[MDEF]] can lower this chance to under 100% and may not be frozen on the third hit. 
*Storm Gust does not stack with other Storm Gusts; two simultaneous Storm Gusts will not result in additional damage or effect. Anything hit by Storm Gust is temporarily immune to the skill for a preset period (half a second). In this way it is similar to [[Lord of Vermilion]].
*Each cell affected by Storm Gust unconditionally splashes a surrounding 3x3 area. This means that the actual area-of-effect of the skill is 11x11.

Super Novice:
__TOC__ {{Infobox Job|jobBase=Novice|jobName=Super Novice|jobType=Novice|changesAt=[[Al De Baran]]|skills=49|skillPoints=419|questSkills=0 |str=5|agi=5|vit=5|int=5|dex=5|luk=5}} ==About Super Novices== Super novices are a special kind of class which exploits nearly every first class skill. Super Novices also sport highly effective armor and shields which reduce elemental attacks. Super Novices are the most versatile among all classes have "true freedom" in build and skills. The downside to this freedom of skills is the limitations that haunt all Novices -- very low HP and SP (a Novice at heart). Super Novices lose the use of the Play Dead skill and also lose exp upon death with 1 HP remaining, just like a regular first class. Super Novices only can equip anything a normal Novice would be able to, including specialized Novice only equipment. Super Novices also have a Job Level of 99. Additionally, Super Novices have their own unique cart, should they choose to get one. ==Jobchange Guide== {{:Super Novice Job Change Guide}} ==Builds== ===Caster=== * STR: 1 * AGI: 1 * VIT: 1-40 * INT: 90+ * DEX: 90+ * LUK: 1 The only class that currently has the ability to achieve instant cast (150 DEX), a caster Super Novice is an incredibly efficient farmer that can be tailored to your needs with very few downsides. Compared to other casters, they do much higher damage as a result of INT bonuses and the Hypnotist Staff giving +25% MATK (instead of the regular 15%), but this comes at the cost of having much lower maximum SP even with the bonus granted by the Angelic set. They may also struggle on higher end maps due to their squishiness, but even that can be mitigated depending on your build. Mammonite * Blessing * Improve Concentration * Increase SP Regeneration * Increase AGI ==Super Novice Secrets== Being a Super Novice has its benefits as well as it's disadvantages and the class of Super Novice remains to be explored by many adventurers. Here are the secrets of Super Novicehood. :Doridori ::Using the command "/doridori" restore HP/SP two times faster. You need to shake your head approximately 6 times in a 1.5-3s time period. A super novice insists that head-shaking supposedly speeds up his SP restoration. This only applies to HP and SP recovered by the skills Increase HP Recovery & Increase SP Recovery (Despite the description on the international version website, this only affects SP recovery, not HP recovery at all) :Guardian Angel ::A Super Novice has its own level up Angel. When leveling-up, this Guardian Angel is different from those of the other classes. The angel will cast all skills from the following list: Kyrie Eleison, Magnificat, Gloria, Suffragium and Impositio Manus on the Super Novice. :Never give up! ::According to hearsay, when a Super Novice's HP reaches 0 when he she is 99.0%-99.9%, their Guardian Angel may appear to refill his HP and cast Mental Strength on the Super Novice. This will not occur again until you relog or level another level. :Undying Love ::A Super Novice wife will give +1 for every stat when she uses the marriage skill Undying Love on her husband. Also, the husband's SP recovery will double. However, the wife's Stats will all be reduced by 1. This however only occurs randomly and temporarily. :The Power of love ::A super novice wife will heal her husband for 2x the normal amount. :Really Super ::If a Super Novice can manage to avoid even a single death until job 70 and onwards, you will get +10 for all stats. If you die anytime afterwards, you will lose that bonus. This death record can be cleared (and the bonus stats recovered) using Super Novice Spirit. :Super Novice Cart ::Super Novices get their own special cart for an extra fee (1900z) in Al De Baran behind the Kafra Headquarters in the Northwestern corner of the map. :Fury ::A strange phenomenon when the Super Novice's EXP reaches increments of 10% such as, at 10.0%, 20.0% - 80.0%, 90.0%. During these times the Super Novice has been rumored to summon his Guardian Angel for help. If you change maps or relog, you have to repeat all the steps but otherwise you can just repeat the last 3 lines to get fury status again. Type 7 lines of text (or you will be silenced) and then type the following phrase to get the Fury Status (critical rate +50): ::* Dear angel, can you hear my voice? ::* I am (your name) Super Novice~ ::* Help me out~ Please~ T_T ::* & (Edit 01/2024: In PayonStories one line above is changed. The original line is "... SuperNovice~") ::OR ::* Guardian Angel, can you hear my voice? ^^; ::* My name is (your name), and I'm a Super Novice~ ::* Please help me~ T.T ::* & ::& is random text. Sometimes you don't have write one more line after "Help me out" to make the effect activate. ==Super Novice: Life After 99== Upon reaching level 99, a super novice has a few new tricks up its sleeves. *The two Super Novice Secrets which depend on your current % of Base EXP can still be used, but you must continue leveling to gain the exp required. :*To Fury, you must gain n*10.0x million exp (where n=1,2,3,...). :*In order to use Mental Strength you must gain an additional 99 million exp or more after 99-ing. :*Upon attaining 99,999,999 exp (as shown on the character select screen) you will be able to use both the novice fury chant and Mental Strength upon 0 hp. ==Super Novice Data== ===Payon Stories Balance Changes=== *[[Soul Harvest]] (Quest Skill) added, which allows a Super Novice to obtain Soul Fragments- a currency used to reset their death counter and buy Novice-specific gear (see the skill page for a complete list). *HP Changes: Super Novices will now receive bonus HP at every 10 level increments starting at level 40. ==Overview==

[[Image:Swordman.jpeg|thumb|left]]

Natural born leaders and men-at-arms, swordman are the frontline of any adventuring party. 

Swordman are capable tanks and mobbers, owing to their ability to equip heavier armor and access to skills like [[Provoke]] and [[Endure]]. Swordman are also capable of wielding a greater variety of weapon types than any other 1st job, and have powerful physical attacks in the form of [[Bash]] and [[Magnum Break]].

Upon reaching job lvl 40, swordman can swear to uphold the codes of chivalry as [[Knight]]s, or take sacred vows and prepare for the holy war as [[Crusader]]s. 

==Jobchange Guide==
See [[Swordman Job Change Guide]] for more information.










== Swordman Builds ==
To make sure your Swordman becomes fully functional, you’ve got to plan your stat build according to the 2nd job you’ll graduate as. This section details how you should allocate your stats until you job change. You can see the final stats allocation for the various builds on the [[Knight]] and [[Crusader]] pages. 

Swordman have these most common builds to evolve into:

=== SVD Knight ===
'''S'''trength, '''V'''itality, '''D'''exterity knights or "SVD" knights are the premiere brawlers in the game. Capable of tanking hoards of enemies with their very high health pools whilst simultaneously dispatching them with [[Brandish Spear]] or [[Bowling Bash]]. SVD is a choice of build for aspiring knights who want to level up as fast and as efficiently as possible, or who relish the idea of being an unstoppable behemoth.

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Raise DEX and VIT together until you reach 30-35 DEX, then focus entirely on STR. You want to prioritise STR because your leveling speed/efficiency later on depends on minimizing how many [[Pierce]], [[Bowling Bash]] or [[Brandish Spear]]s you need to kill a target or group of targets.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate[0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0], VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance
* Offhand: Shield[0]
* Garment: Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash, Ring [0]

<u>First Major Investments:</u> VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance, Pike [4] (Orc Lady Card x 3, Hydra Card), Shield/Buckler[1] (Thara Frog Card)

=== AGI (2h) Knight ===
For knights who prefer the sword over the spear, or for those who like the more leisurely style of autoattacking enemies. A 2h knight's playstyle is a mix of quickly going from enemy to enemy and gathering groups of foes and knocking them over with [[Bowling Bash]]. Sharing the title with Spear Saders, 2h knights are the fastest autoattackers in the game, capable of reaching more than 185 ASPD (5+ attacks per second).

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 30-35 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 60-70 AGI, start investing in STR. Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR earlier and more-so to capitalize on carded weaponry and +flee equipment.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain, Sakkat
* Body: Pantie, Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Claymore[0], Two-Handed Sword[0], VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Claymore
* Offhand: NPC-bought Shield [0]
* Garment: Undershirt, Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash, Ring [0]

<u>First Major Investments:</u> VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Claymore, Two-Handed Sword[2] (Goblin Card x 2)

===  GC (Grand Cross) ===
For Crusaders who want to combine might with magic, GC saders are armor-clad spellcasters who specialize in killing groups of [[Undead]] and [[Shadow]] element enemies with their [[Grand Cross]] spell. Though more of a late bloomer than other types of crusaders, GC saders eventually make themselves rich as they rid the world of evil with maps like Glast Heim Chivalry and Niflheim as their stomping grounds.

For more information see: [[Crusader#GC (Grand Cross)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in INT, with a little bit of VIT and DEX (E.g., 80 INT, 30 VIT, 20 DEX).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Haedonggum[0], Fireblend*
* Offhand: Mirror Shield [0]
* Garment: Manteau[0], Ragamuffin Manteau
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Earring

<u>First Major Investments:</u> Fireblend (as an early leveling tool only, to be later resold), Mirror Shield [1] (Thara Frog Card), Earring[0], Diadem of the High Priestess [1] (Elder Willow Card)

=== HC (Holy Cross) ===
For those that like flashy skills, or who fancy themselves as [[Demon]] hunters. HC saders are similar to GC saders in that they primarily hunt [[Shadow]] and [[Undead]] element foes, but differ in that they do so with spears rather than spells. These crusaders are skill spammers, making use of the incredibly efficient ranged physical skill [[Holy Cross]] to kill monsters.   

For more information see: [[Crusader#HC (Holy Cross)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in STR, with a little bit in INT and AGI (E.g., 80 STR, 30 INT, 20 AGI).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain, Sakkat
* Body: Pantie, Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0], VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance
* Offhand: Shield[0]
* Garment: Undershirt, Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash, Ring [0]

<u>First Major Investments:</u> Trident [3] (Santa Poring Card x 3)

=== AGI Spear ===
For crusaders who want to hunt more than just [[Demon]]s or [[Undead]], AGI Spear or "Spear Saders" have almost total freedom as to where they can go with their collection of two-handed spears. They are similar to AGI knights in that they are the fastest autoattackers in the game, but differ by trading AoE capability for higher single target kill speed.

For more information see: [[Crusader#AGI Spear]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 30-35 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 70-80 AGI, start investing in STR. Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR earlier and more-so to capitalize on carded weaponry and +flee equipment.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain, Sakkat
* Body: Pantie, Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0], Poring Dagger, VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance
* Offhand: Shield[0]
* Garment: Undershirt, Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash, Ring [0]

<u>First Major Investments:</u> VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance

=== Boomer (Shield Boomerang) ===
Utterly unique, Shield Boomerang Crusaders or "boomers" turn their defense into offense by quite literally throwing their shields at their foes. Boomers combine their ability to rapidly dispatch low - medium health enemies with their mounted movement speed and hardiness to be one of the most efficient farmers around.  

For more information see: [[Crusader#Boomer (Shield Boomerang)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in STR, with a little bit in INT and VIT (E.g., 80 STR, 30 INT, 20 VIT).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0], Poring Dagger
* Offhand: Buckler [0]
* Garment: Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Ring[0], Clip [1] (Mantis Card)

<u>First Major Investments:</u> +7 Stone Discus [1] (Tamruan Card)

=== Devo (Devotion) ===
These crusaders focus on maximizing the defensive and protective potential of their vocation. Either as a tank, mobber or through their special role of keeping party members alive with [[Sacrifice]], Devo Saders make for an essential component of parties. Devo crusaders can be either full support, hybrid boomer or hybrid gc crusaders.

For more information see: [[Crusader#Devo (Devotion)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in VIT if you're planning on being a full support Devo Sader. Otherwise, how you invest your stats will depend on whether you're going to be a hybrid boomer or hybrid gc devo sader (see those build sections) with an added priority on VIT.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0]
* Offhand: Shield[0]
* Garment: Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Necklace, Clip [1] (Spore Card)

<u>First Major Investments:</u>: Buying high defense Swordman--only armor like Full Plate[0] and Greaves[0] from NPCs and upgrading them to the safe limit (+4) with elunium is a solid first investment to make you a more solid mobber and tank for parties.

=== Devo (Devotion) ===

An aspiring full support Devo sader should build their attributes and level on the same monsters as an 2h Knight/AGI sader would until level 45, and then reset their stats as appropriate (i.e., VIT) by talking to Pheonix (See: Stat_Reset). Solo leveling after this point is largely impractical, and the devo sader should try and find groups where they can serve as the party's mobber for their leveling needs (e.g., Mi Gao -> Stala/Pront Guild Dungeon/Turtle Dungeon -> Magma/Abyss).

A devo sader built as a hybrid boomer or GC sader should follow those leveling sections above.

===Payon Stories Balance Changes===
See [[Class Rebalance#Swordman|Class Rebalance (Swordman)]] for detailed information.
*[[HP Recovery|'''HP Recovery''']]: Ticks every 5 Seconds in line with the overall increased HP/SP regen in Payon Stories.
*[[Bash|'''Bash''']]: SP cost has been reduced to a rate of 3 SP + 1 SP per skill level.
*[[Magnum Break|'''Magnum Break''']]: Range has been increased to 4 cells, its SP cost has been reduced from 30 SP to 18 SP per cast.
*[[Moving HP Recovery|'''Moving HP Recovery''']]: Can now be learned at Job Level 15. The quest now requires [[Image:713.png|24px|]] 50 [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=713 Empty Bottle] instead of 200.
*[[Sword Mastery| '''Sword Mastery''']] and [[Two-Handed Sword Mastery| '''Two-Handed Sword Mastery''']]: Have been combined into [[Blade Mastery]].

3. ''First Map'': A simple map. Just walk to the other side. If you fall you will be sent back to the beginning.

4. ''Second Map'': This map involves two parallel bridges. Take your time and be careful not to fall off. You don't have to hold the mouse button down to walk.

5. ''Third Map'': Similar to the first map except for the upper and lower levels. The lower level has a darker color than the upper level. Take your time and click carefully to get to the lower level. At the point where there is a gap in the top level, simply click on the lower level, and you will jump down. Then do the same to get back up.

6. Upon traversing the three maps and their checkpoints, talk to '''Mae''' in the last room to finish the test.

7. After exiting the test maps, speak to the large Swordman in the main room to become a [[Swordman]].

The Lost Legacy:
The Lost Legacy is a custom questline that has you uncovering the secret of the mysterious Turtle Island. One of the quest rewards is the best FLEE headgear in the game at the time of writing: [[Momoe's Hairband|'''Momoe's Hairband''']].

== Prerequisites & Preparation ==
You must have completed the '''Turtle Island Entrance Quest''' to initiate The Lost Legacy.

'''IMPORTANT:''' The final step of the quest '''requires you to do the most damage to a miniboss with 26k HP under a time limit'''; it is highly advised to '''not complete the quest steps on a support character'''.

All of the items required for this quest can be collected ahead of time to speed up the questline. These items are:
* '''Sprinter's Tail''' (100% drop from Master Sprinter)
* '''Small Bell''' (1% drop from Solider)
* '''Odd Wooden Object''' (1% drop from Permeter)
* '''Chalice of Water''' (1% drop from Freezer)
* '''Triangular Key''' (1% drop from Assaulter)

Heaters (the fire turtle) do not drop any items relevant to the quest.

The Main Questline is broken down into the following subquests:

== The Ninja Rat ==
1. Speak with '''Oroku Saki''' at the Alberta docks (230, 116), who is cursed and wants revenge on the monster who cursed him. He will ask you to slay Master Sprinter and return his tail as proof.

[[File:LostLegacy1.png]]

2. Slay Master Sprinter and loot '''Sprinter's Tail'''. Master Sprinter is a miniboss with the appearance of a giant Cramp, who summons giant turtle slaves. He has a static spawn near his house on the bottom left of Turtle Dungeon 2F. Note that the drop is capped at 90%, so there is a possibility it does not drop when he is killed.

[[File:LostLegacy2.png]]

3. Return '''Sprinter's Tail''' to Oroku Saki, who realized that he is still cursed despite Master Sprinter having been slain.

== The Lost Legacy ==
1. Oroku Saki asks you to look for clues as to why he may still be cursed. Search the '''Urns''' surrounding Master Sprinter's house in Turtle Dungeon 2F (61, 35) to discover a scroll; read it to uncover the clues you were searching for.

[[File:LostLegacy3.png]]

'''Note:''' If you loot a Panacea, you are interacting with the wrong Urn; there's a second one on the other side of the house.

== Dungeon Keys ==

=== The First Key ===
1. The first clue talks about "fueling the fire" and suggests that the turtles "with trees on their back" may be holders of the first key. Slay '''Permeters''' until you obtain an '''Odd Wooden Object'''.

2. Head to the upper left corner of Turtle Dungeon 3F and interact with the '''Bronze Statue''' (31, 167). Place the Odd Wooden Object into the slot in the statue, which results in a **CLICK**, implying something has unlocked in the distance.

[[File:LostLegacy4.png]]

=== The Second Key ===
1. The second clue refers to a "bell of earthly bronze" and suggests that "earthlike turtles" may have something to do with it. Slay '''Soliders''' until you obtain a '''Small Bell'''.

2. Head to the right side of Turtle Dungeon 3F to find an '''Ornate Desk''' (164, 92). Place the Small Bell on the stand on the desk, which results in a **CRASH!**, implying something "that sounded like a small jar" has broken in the distance.

[[File:LostLegacy5.png]]

=== The Third Key ===
1. The third clue refers to "some kind of water" and suggests that "the ones made of ice" may be its keeper. Slay '''Freezers''' until you obtain a '''Chalice of Water'''.

2. Head to the '''Urn Stand''' in a hallway near the top of the map (96, 132). Pour the water into the small recess in the stand, which results in a *drip* *drip* *drip*; all of a sudden, there seems to be a crack in the ceiling and water is leaking through it, implying something happened to the water two floors above.

[[File:LostLegacy6.png]]

=== The Fourth Key ===
1. The fourth and final clue describes the wind and strongly implies that turtles that are "swift like the wind" may possess the final key. Slay '''Assaulters''' until you obtain a '''Triangular Key'''.

2. Head to the upper left corner of Turtle Dungeon 1F and interact with the '''Puddle''' (79, 223). Insert the Triangular Key into the carved stone at the bottom of the puddle, which results in a loud noise from below in the palace, revealing that a hidden way has opened.

[[File:LostLegacy7.png]]

=== The Mysterious Chamber ===
1. Head back to Turtle Dungeon 3F and interact with the '''Grand Statue''' just south of the middle of the map (96, 47). Drop down into the gap underneath the statue.

[[File:LostLegacy8.png]]

2. You will appear on a new map. Follow the path to the right, then head south ('''do not speak to the Hydra''') and back down to the left again. To find an '''Old Turtle Shell''' (35, 23).

[[File:LostLegacy9.png]]

3. Reach under the shell to pull out the final key, but you are stopped by a mysterious presence. They claim they have already taken the real key to the treasure and that "this place will be your grave!" and commence an attack; defeat the '''Ashi Clan Leader''' and take the key from them!

'''Note:''' You must do the '''most damage to this boss''' in order to obtain the Treasure Key. It is a Quest Item that will appear in your inventory which '''cannot be dropped or traded'''.

4. Once the Ashi Clan Leader is defeated and the '''Treasure Key''' is obtained, interact with the Hydra you walked past ("'''Curious Vines'''") to climb back up to the surface of Turtle Island.

'''Note:''' The following two questlines, '''The Final Key''' and '''The Library / Momoe's Memento''', can be done in any order. Seeing as you're already on the Turtle Island surface, it is recommended to complete The Final Key first.

== The Final Key ==
1. Head to the top left corner of the Turtle Island surface and interact with the '''Big Turtle Statue''' (91, 189), which yields the treasure of Turtle Island!

[[File:LostLegacy11.png]]

You will obtain:

* 1 Old Purple Box
* 3 Yggdrasil Leaf
* 1 Yggdrasil Seed
* 1 Ruby
* 1 Cursed Ruby
* 1 Opal
* 1 Garnet
* 1 Aquamarine

== The Library ==
1. Head back down to Turtle Dungeon 3F one final time. Interact with the '''Old Tomes''' on the bookshelf near the bottom left of the map (75, 48). You find a journal; reading it reveals the true origin of Oroku Saki's curse as well as a way to potentially end the suffering. You find Momoe's Hairband nearby and decide to take it back to Oroku Saki.

'''Note''': The "Momoe's Hairband" item in this step is a Quest Item and is '''not yet equippable'''.

[[File:LostLegacy12.png]]

== Momoe's Memento ==
1. '''Return to Oroku Saki''' at the Alberta docks (230, 116), to give them Momoe's Hairband and explain the contents of the diary. This relieves him of the hatred he has been holding on to; he decides to give you '''[[Momoe's Hairband]]''' as a thank you for ending his suffering, and so the memory of Momoe can live on.

[[File:Momoe's Hairband.png]]

==Overview==

[[Image: Thief.jpg|thumb|left]]

''Carpe diem'' -- Seize the day! A motto that perfectly captures the spirit of thieves. Wielding dagger or bow, they strike swiftly, overwhelming foes with [[Double Attack]]s. Their high flee thanks to [[Improve Dodge]] makes them difficult to hit, while skills like [[Hiding]], [[Envenom]] and [[Steal]] add a layer of thematic utility that makes them truly feel unique. 

Thieves are a job with a high level of accessibility thanks to their highly practical passive skills, which makes them a popular choice for new players and veterans alike. 

Upon reaching job lvl 40, thieves can choose to undertake a trial to join the mysterious [[Assassin]]s, or embrace a life of greater crime and cunning by becoming a [[Rogue]].

==Jobchange Guide==
See [[Thief Job Change Guide]] for more information.














== Thief Builds ==
To make sure your thief becomes fully functional, you’ve got to plan your stat build according to the 2nd job you’ll graduate as. This section details different [[Rogue]] and [[Assassin]] builds and how you should allocate your stats until you job change. You can see the final stats allocation for the various builds on the [[Rogue]] and [[Assassin]] pages. 

All thieves (regardless of 2nd class) should distribute their skill point as follows:

* [[Double Attack]] 10
* [[Improve Dodge]] 10
* [[Envenom]] 3
* [[Detoxify]] 1
* [[Envenom]] 10
* [[Steal]] 10
* [[Hiding]] 8

If planning on job changing ''before'' job50, the above distribution can be changed, but this is not recommended. The jEXP requirements for 1st classes has been modified on Payon Stories to be lower, and whether changing into an [[Assassin]] or a [[Rogue]], a valuable Gladius [3] is awarded if changing at job50 thief.

Thieves have these most common builds to evolve into:

=== Dual dagger(DD)/Hybrid Katar Assassin ===
DD assassins make use of their unique ability to equip two daggers at once, allowing them to reach the pinnacle of single target DPS. They also boast excellent mobbing ability thanks to the very powerful [[Venom Splasher]] poison skill. Another version of this build uses Sidewinder carded Katars and forgoes [[Venom Splasher]] to instead get [[Katar Mastery]] and [[Grimtooth]], allowing for an alternate playstyle (usually differing only in terms of skills taken, not stat allocation).

* '''Pros''' : Excellent mobbing ability, highest dps on low defense monsters, good mobber in static parties.
* '''Cons''' : Notorious for being "The most expensive build in the game" (huge arsenal of carded gladius/main gauche)

'''Stat distribution :'''
Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 20-30 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 40-50 AGI, start investing in and prioritizing STR (STR should generally be 20-30 points higher than AGI). Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR over AGI much earlier instead. 

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Damascus, Poring Dagger
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Ranked VVS Wind/Fire Damascus, Brooch [0], Sidewinder carded Jamadhar [1] (if going hybrid katar)

=== Critical Assassin ===
Critical Assassins use of the special assassin-only Katar weapon class to double their critical rate, allowing them to dispatch high DEF/Flee enemies that many other classes struggle with. These assassins also boast high single target DPS, have excellent one-shot potential with [[Sonic Blow]] and strong mobbing potential with [[Grimtooth]].

* '''Pros''' : Affordable low-end equipment, critical hits bypass DEF/Flee making them excellent hunters of those enemies, can fill in for ABB [[Hunter]] role in parties, good mobber, the sound of rapid critical hits is pure dopamine 
* '''Cons''' : High-end equipment is extremely expensive

'''Stat distribution :'''

*Levels 1 - 45: It's best to just build your thief like an aspiring Gank Rogue (see below) until base level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]])
*Levels 45 - 60+: You shouldn't invest in LUK at all until becoming an [[Assassin]], as you'll get little out of it. Focus solely on AGI/STR, usually more AGI than STR (~10-20 point difference).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Damascus, Poring Dagger
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Skeleton Soldier/Bonechewer carded Jur [3], Kobold carded Clip [1], Ruby Pumps, Yoyo Pet

=== Gank/Snatcher Rogue ===
[[Snatcher]] is a unique skill that can proc the [[Steal]] skill when you auto-attack a monster without consuming SP. These rogues in essence get double the loot from each monster confronted. A Gank Rogue is built to capitalize on this skill, making for not only an excellent farmer but a character with great self-sustain and map variety.

* '''Pros''' : More loot means more money, relatively cheap to make, excellent sustain and flexibility thanks to [[Plagiarism]]
* '''Cons''' : Not very good in non-static parties, eventually becomes an inferior farmer of low HP enemies compared to other jobs who can more efficiently one shot them.

'''Stat distribution :'''

Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 30-40 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 50-60 AGI, start investing in STR (STR should generally be ~20 points lower than AGI). Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR over AGI instead.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Damascus, Poring Dagger
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Ranked VVS Wind/Fire Damascus, Brooch [0], Myst Case Carded Hat [1]/Cap [1]/Marionette Doll [1], Creamy Carded Clip [1]

=== Bow Rogue (AGI) ===
Bow Rogues can be thought of as a more flexible [[Hunter]]. While they may boast less raw power when wielding a bow, these rogues have the added ability to copy almost any player skill with [[Plagiarism]], allowing them to do things [[Hunter]]s can't like mob groups of enemies with [[Bowling Bash]] or dispatch high DEF foes with [[Acid Terror]].

* '''Pros''' : Relatively cheap to make, can function similarly to Gank Rogue with the same benefits (especially using Great Snake card), ranged character with those inherit benefits to kill speed/lower damage received
* '''Cons''' : Thief leveling with only a 3 cell bow range can be painful, without [[Arrow Crafting]] must rely on another character to create quivers/craft arrows.

'''Stat distribution :''' DEX should always be ~20 points ahead of AGI, it is still the most important stat for AGI Bow Rogues. Avoid investing in INT (if at all) until late levels as a [[Rogue]].

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Gakkung [1]/Repeating Crossbow [1]
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Sidewinder carded Gakkung [2] ''or'' Sidewinder carded Repeating Crossbow [1], Apple of Archer, Glove [0], Brooch [0]

=== Bow/Caster Rogue (INT) ===
INT Rogue is a build that allows a player to be especially creative with their use of [[Plagiarism]]. Because of how bow damage is calculated, these rogues have an unusual combination of high ATK, fast cast time and a high MATK/SP recovery which let them make use of skills other rogues would not, like [[Grand Cross]], [[Blaze Shield]], [[Storm Gust]], and more.

* '''Pros''' : Unique (dazzle others with your weirdness), can fill wizard roles in parties at high levels, has access to a super-powered version of [[Water Ball]], better at using [[Acid Terror]] than [[Alchemist]]s, no one will ever be as cool as you.
* '''Cons''' : Early-mid [[Rogue]] leveling will be painful, leveling experience will be a struggle without very careful planning of maps and skills to plagerise.

'''Stat distribution :'''

*Levels 1 - 45: It's best to just build your thief like an aspiring Bow Rogue (AGI) (see above) until base level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]])
*Levels 45 - 60+: Largely depends on how you plan on leveling as a [[Rogue]]. If you plan on leveling with spells like [[Blaze Shield]] (currently bugged for [[Plagiarism]]) then pump only INT and rely on Mi Gao parties (see below) until you can use Plagiarism 10. For most builds, DEX will be by and large the priority and should be ~30-40 points higher than INT, or raised exclusively until reaching 8x/9x DEX.

1. Head off to the Pyramids, which is north-west of [[Morroc]].  

2. At the pyramid (58,159), enter, and head for the middle of the map to the Thief Guild (90,105).

3. Once inside, follow the hallway down and take the left gate (90,115). In here you will see two NPCs that will guide you through the quest. 

4. Talk to the one closest to the portal. She will ask you a few questions, then instruct you to find an "Irrelevant Man" somewhere outside the Pyramid (141, 125) in order to steal mushrooms from a nearby mushroom farm.

[[Image:Thiefmap.JPG]]

5. At the farm, kill the mushrooms and collect the mushrooms that drop.  Aggressive Fabres and Chonchons (and Spores, but they're not aggresive) protect the farm, so you may want to avoid them.  Your mission is to collect at least mushrooms worth of 25 points.

*'''Note''': If you die, you can talk to Mr. Irrelevant to return to the farm as many times as needed. 

6. After collecting a sufficient amount of Mushrooms, head back to Thief Guild.

7. Talk to NPC farthest from the warp portal. He will count your mushrooms and if you have enough points, he will promote you to a Thief.

== Notes ==

Throw Shuriken functions as both a skill and a regular attack, with the following properties:
* It is affected by ATK, +%ATK cards, weapon status cards like Magnolia Cards, STR and weapon damage in the same way most skills are (e.g., [[Haze Slasher]]).
* It does ''not'' benefit from non-weapon cards which have a chance of activating on regular attacks (auto attacks) like [[Corruptor Card]], Enchanted Peach Tree Card, etc.
* This attack inherits both the attack speed and the size penalties of the weapon class you are using. For example, holding a dagger will make you throw faster than holding a huuma shuriken, but will have a 50% penalty VS large enemies whereas the huuma shuriken deals its full damage (see: [[Size]]).

* The damage dealt by this skill is increased by using shurikens with higher ATK. However, similar to other ammunition like arrows, the actual damage contributed from shuriken ammo +ATK is only a fraction of the displayed value. 
* Throw Shuriken cannot be used while silenced.

Turtle Shell Quest is a short custom quest that has you aid Rulf van Nostros in his bid to collect Turtle Shells. The quest rewards the player with a moderate amount of base experience, job experience and zeny. == Prerequisites & Preparation == You must have completed the '''Turtle Island Entrance Quest''' to initiate The Lost Legacy. == NPC Location == [[File:TurtleShellQuestNPCLocation.png|500px|]]
''The quest giver is located at 162,235 on Turtle Island surface''

== General WoE Information ==
War of Emperium on Payon Stories server occurs weekly on '''Saturday at 22:00 GMT to 23:00 GMT (server time)''' and is divided into Seasons. Guild Seasons will last a period of 10 weeks, followed by 2-4 weeks of break (that will consist of standings tallying, reward distribution  and next season changes implementation).

=== WoE Information: ===

* '''Time:''' Saturday, 22:00 to 23:00 (Timezone: GMT)
* '''Guild Cap:''' 22 Members 
* '''Participation''': Only whitelisted guilds (submitted by WoE GM) can participate in Payon Stories WoE

* '''WoE Rewards:''' In addition to castle ownership, a Seasonal Point System will be implemented during every to provide all guilds a chance to earn valuable loot for actively participating in WoE.
* '''WoE Supplies Shop''': Available

== WoE Guilds Whitelisting ==
To participate in the WoE, you must have your guild whitelisted by submitting an online application form. Application forms can be found in server discord #annoucement channel before each season starts. To qualify for whitelisting, your guild must have at least 4 active WoE members.

Please note that only whitelisted guilds will be allowed to enter castles during the season. New guilds can request whitelisting at least 24 hours before the start of WoE, but they might not be approved until after WoE if the request is not made within the 24-hour timeframe.

== Castle Information ==
'''Each season, castles will randomly be selected''' by the WoE GM. 

'''As the season progresses and the WoE population changes, the number of castles during different WoE Seasons will vary'''. WoE GM has the authority to open a castle to expand the overall field of combat, or to close a castle to condense it. The WoE GM has the authority to give compensation in the event that a castle with considerable economy points is closed, but compensation is not defined or guaranteed. The WoE GM has the authority to alter the drops and rate of drops of castles in the event of a castle closure or a castle opening. 

Castles will have '''different treasure loot tables'''. Owning a castle entitles your guild to treasures. Each castle will spawn '''four treasures per day''', with an '''additional treasure spawn for every 5-economy invested into the castle''', up to a maximum value of 60 economy, equivalent to 16 treasure chests per day. Breaking an emperium will reduce the economy of the castle by 5 each time that the emperium is broken.

Castles also provide a guild the full waiving of the '''guild dungeon access fee so long as the castle is held by that guild'''. Treasure is spawned based on the previous day's economy.

== WoE Battle Parameters ==
Before each WoE Season starts, a list of the key battle parameters and other seasonal details will be provided by WoE GM in server discord #annoucement channel. Note that this list is subject to change at the discretion of the WoE GM when it is deemed necessary.

Battle Parameters list will include key information such such: guild cap limitations, guild skill usage, alliances, economy and defence caps, player skill limitations, etc.

Please make sure to keep an eye on WoE Details or any further updates before and during each WoE Season.

== Battlegroups and other Rules ==
Each guild and guild member hereby agrees to the following rules to maintain fairness. A “Guild Group” is defined as not only the main guild that carries the name, logo, and brand of a guild, but also any subguilds, slave-guilds, and alternative guilds created with the purpose of housing overflow members, casual guild members, or alts. 

Only members of the main guild that is registered as a participating guild and representing the Guild Group will be allowed to enter. Other guilds within the Guild Group will be blacklisted from entry. Attempts to circumvent this 22-person cap will be dealt with harshly. Any guild attempting to circumvent this rule will 

# lose any castles immediately
# be blacklisted from participating for the remainder of the season. 

Additionally, in severe circumstances of cheating, a guild may be dissolved by force, losing all experience and learned skills. Only approved guilds will be allowed to enter castles and you must submit a request for approval before you will be able to enter. We put these terms in place to protect the integrity of the WoE environment. 

'''Battle-Groups''': In the event that two guild entities in WoE act in a highly coordinated manner that is considered by the WoE GM to be disruptive to the competitive environment of WoE, they might be considered to be one battle-group. The WoE GM will issue a warning to them in this case, in an attempt to break up the highly cooperative behavior. 

'''Cross-Merging''': A large number of guild members from one WoE guild merging into another guild for WoE is considered cross-merging, and might violate the separate battlegroup rule. Please discuss this with the WoE GM beforehand to ask for guidance and approval. 

'''Emperium Break Trading and Seasonal Points Rigging''': Cooperative play between two guilds for the purpose of farming seasonal points from a castle in an unfair way could be considered to be seasonal points rigging. An example of this would be letting a guild break your emperium for the purpose and intention of them getting points while stopping other guilds from doing so. If you have questions about this rule please contact the WoE GM. 

'''Spirit of the Rules and Evolution of the Rules''': Rules will never be perfectly written, and WoE rules especially are young. With this in mind, WoE players and guild leaders are expected to: 

* Consider the spirit and intention of the rules thus far, and be mindful of them. 
* Ask questions to the WoE GM if something isn’t clear or understood. 
* Be cooperative as rules evolve over time.

== Seasonal Point System ==
In addition to castle ownership, a Seasonal Point system will be implemented to provide all guilds a chance to earn valuable loot for actively participating in WoE. After the regular season of 10 weeks has concluded, a final tally and validation will occur 1 week after the last WoE of the season. Thereafter, in the following week seasonal rewards will be distributed to each guild leader who has qualified for a reward. 

Points are earned in three ways and are additive and combined after each WoE: 

* Attendance Points (Participation) 
* Defense Points (Holding Castles) 
* Offense Points (Breaking Castle Emperiums)

=== Attendance Points ===
Every participating guild member’s time spent on a castle map will be tracked while WoE is in progress. Following the end of that WoE, all time on WoE castle maps for each player will be totaled. If that player has spent 20 minutes or more on the castle maps, then 50 seasonal points are awarded to that player’s guild. Each week, guilds can earn up to 500 attendance points through this attendance tracking feature. Therefore, even smaller participating guilds may get full attendance points as only 10 people need to participate each week for the required 20 minutes per person to earn the full 500 attendance points

=== Defence Points ===
Defense is important to guilds and if a guild is actively defending a castle, they will be entitled to receive points. Depending on the length of time a castle is held, a certain number of points will be rewarded to a guild. Points will be awarded first, based on the economy of the underlying castle being held, and then by tracking the minutes spent defending that castle during WoE. Note that each castle has a unique tracker of time, so holding one castle for five minutes and another castle for five minutes does not equate to ten minutes of holding time as each castle is independent when rewarding these defense points.

'''All up to date Defence Points Requirements for each season will be provided in Seasonal WoE Details which can be found in server discord #annoucement channel.'''

=== Offence Points ===
Attacking castles and breaking emperium will also reward guilds with points. Each successful break of a castle emperium for different economy levels will provide a certain number of points with diminishing returns (once a castle emperium is broken during a WoE, the points awarded for subsequent breaks quickly diminishes).

'''All up to date Offence Points Requirements for each season will be provided in Seasonal WoE Details which can be found in server discord #annoucement channel.'''

== WoE Supplies Shop ==
[[File:Woe Supplies.png|frameless]]

'''The [[WoE Informant]] NPC''' (oldnewpayon 50, 149) will '''trade WoE Supplies in return for Tokens'''. 

After WoE ends, up to 22 characters from each guild that received any points will also receive certain number of tokens. Tokens amount may be altered during the season if deemed necessary. In order to be eligible, the account needs to have been inside castles for 20 minutes in total (can be split between multiple characters). Only one character from each account can receive tokens (the one with highest participation time). If more than 20 accounts in a guild are eligible, those with higher participation time are prioritized. The tokens are handed out when WoE ends through RODEX.

These tokens can be exchanged for WoE Supplies (i.e. WoE Potions, WoE Boxes). Please note that these potions can only be used in WoE castles, and the boxes can only be used in Towns (not in inns).

== Guild Dungeon Access NPC ==
Castles provide a guild the full waiving of the '''guild dungeon access fee so long as the castle is held by that guild.'''

Other players (even those who don't participate in WoE at all) can also enter guild dungeons by talking to special NPC located in north Payon - '''[[Guild Dungeon Administrator|Guild Dungeons Administrator]]''' (oldnewpayon 53, 135) and pay entrance fee. First time entrance is free of charge, every next attempt will cost a multiple of 5k zeny (i.e.: 5k, 10k, 15k, etc.), up to a maximum fee amount of 25k zeny per entry.

Weight Limit:
== General ==

The weight limit is how much you can carry. If a character is carrying 50% or more of the weight limit, he has minor overweight. Minor overweight cancels [[HP Recovery]], [[SP Recovery]], [[Increase HP Recovery]] and [[Increase SP Recovery]] as well as restricting the use of skills that create items, like [[Find Stone]] and [[Arrow Crafting]]. When carrying 90% or more of the weight limit, the character has major overweight. During major overweight, a character cannot attack or use skills at all.

[[Pushcart]] does not increase your character's weight limit. See the skill description for how it works.

== Calculation ==

 var MAX_WGT = 2000;
 MAX_WGT += 30 * BASE_STR;
 MAX_WGT += WGT_JOB;
 MAX_WGT += WGT_MOD;
 
 BASE_STR : Base stat value of STR
 WGT_JOB : See the job modifier table
 WGT_MOD : Sum of modifiers

Base value 2000. Add 30 per base STR. Add mod from job. Add modifiers.

=== Modifiers ===

* [[Enlarge Weight Limit]]: +200 per level
* [[Peco Peco Ride]]: +1000 when mounted
Note that there are two versions of [[Enlarge Weight Limit]]. One of them is a [[merchant]] class skill, while the other can be obtained through the use of the [[Kafra Shop]] item Gym Pass. These two versions do stack.

Winter Carnival:
== Introduction ==
Welcome to Winter Carnival! Enter the special carnival event map, take a look around and experience a lot of fun minigames and exclusive rewards!

Take your time to visit this colorful festival area and try your luck in various mini games that require either skill or luck. Collect Carnival Coins by winning the games and exchange them for exclusive rewards in a special Carnival Shop.

== How to start? ==
To enter the Winter Carnival, simply '''type "@carnival"''' in the in-game chat (towns-only) and experience the joy of festive games and exclusive rewards!

Please note that whenever you ride a Peco Peco and you enter the map, it will be unequipped.

Welcome to the Carnival Area!

== Games Tickets ==

=== Getting Carnival Coupons ===
[[File:Ticket Master NPC.png|thumb|200x200px]]
Speak to the '''Ticket Master NPC''' to receive '''10 Carnival Coupons'''. You can exchange them to participate in various Festival Games.

New Carnival Coupons can be collected from Ticket Master NPC '''every 24 hours'''.

You can always check the number of currently held coupons or how much time is left to collect new coupons by speaking to the NPC again.

'''''Note: Carnival Coupons are account bound, that means you won’t receive any additional coupons if you speak to the NPC with a different character from the same game account.'''''

If you don't have any coupons, the game will ask if you want to play without it. On playing without coupon, you still need to beat the game to win the costume, however no carnival cash will be rewarded.

=== Mini Games Map Tags ===
Ticket Master NPC will tell you about all the games awaiting. He’ll also put color tags on your mini map so you can easily find all the games.

== Reward Shop (Costumes) ==
As a reward after winning the games you’ll receive different amounts of '''Carnival Cash''' – a unique event currency which can be exchanged for various prizes in Ticket Master reward shop.

The better you score in games (or the bigger risk you take by placing bets in some of the games), the more Carnival Cash you’ll get from them.

Some games offer additional unique prizes for reaching best scores (i.ex. headgears).

=== Black Jack ===
[[File:33334.png|thumb|Location of NPC]]
Popular card game in which the goal is to get 21, or as close as possible to 21 without going over this number. Play the game and make a bets to win against the card dealer. You can place a bet of 1, 3, 5 or 10 Carnival Cash or even take a risk and double your bet to win (or lose) even more Carnival Cash.

'''Requirement''': 1 Carnival Coupon and at least 1 Carnival Cash 

'''Can Play Without Coupon?''' No 

'''Rewards''': 

* Carnival Cash - Cannot be won without coupon.  You can win some carnival cash plus your bet back.  
* Carnival Coupon - Cannot be won without coupon.  You can win a carnival coupon and your bet back.
* Parade Cap - Cannot be won without coupon. You can win the hat and your bet back.

'''Tips'''

* The dealer stays at 17 or higher.
* If you have the same as the dealer when he stays, you will PUSH and get your money back.
* A SOFT value means you have an ACE that is counting as 11.  A HARD value means you do not have an ace or you have an ace counting as 1.  An ace counts as 1, if it giving you 11 makes you bust past 21.
* Here is basic strategy for beginners for this version of the game:
** If the dealer has 12 - 16,
*** If you have less than HARD 12, HIT.
*** If you have HARD 12 or more, STAY.  This is because the most likely value is 10 and the dealer is likely to bust, letting you win!  The game forces you to hit if you have 12, unfortunately.
*** If you have a SOFT value of 12 - 16, HIT.
*** If you have a SOFT value of 17 or more, STAY.
** If the dealer has 17 or more,
*** If you have less than the dealer, HIT until you either have more than the dealer (then STAY) or you bust.
*** If you have the same as the dealer, STAY so you PUSH and get your money back.
*** If you have more than the dealer, STAY and you will win.
** If the dealer has 11 or less, I usually hit until I have a HARD 17 or more or I bust.
* There are more advanced strategies, especially once you include Double Down.  However, this basic strategy should give you a overall winning chance.
